# F-57 Converged Program Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Deliver F-57 from one approved design through a dependency-ordered Windows development slice, complete integration, and highest-security release certification without weakening any of the 185 RequirementIDs.

**Architecture:** One Windows Server authority owns commands, data, policy, generations, automation, and evidence; every other surface is a non-authoritative client or governed provider. One canonical plain `CapabilityGraphV1`, authenticated by the exact verified generation reference rather than by a standalone CMS envelope, generates protocol, authorization, UI, package, provider, Excel/MCP, test, and documentation projections, while feature-first bounded contexts own business state and communicate only through typed public commands and committed facts.

**Tech Stack:** Rust 2021/MSVC, PostgreSQL 16, SQLx, native Windows Server 2022 services, Tauri 2 with a Flutter + Rust fallback decision gate, HTTPS, PowerShell, Windows CNG/TPM/BitLocker/Service SID/Job Object/DACL, GitHub Actions on self-hosted runners only (ADR-0027; F-77 removed the trailing "or an equivalent thin self-hosted orchestrator", which ADR-0027 decision 1 forbids).

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-23-f57-governed-automation-fabric-design.md`

## Global Constraints

- This plan is development-ready. **Development authorization was explicitly granted by the user on 2026-08-27** (verbatim directive recorded in 00c F-65); the state-machine node remains `READY_NOT_AUTHORIZED` until `G0_BOOTSTRAP_GREEN` per §7, and implementation may start with G0.
- The normative set remains exactly 185 RequirementIDs: 174 current requirements plus 11 deferred-boundary requirements; no plan may delete, merge, rename, or silently postpone one.
- The current first-release production authority is native Windows Server 2022 on the ThinkStation P340 profile; Linux, WSL, systemd, Podman, Compose, Kubernetes, and `/run|/etc|/var/lib` paths are not production evidence. A future IaaS deployment is a separate `IAAS_WINDOWS_SERVER_HDD_STRICT` profile, never an alias or substitute for P340: it remains `NOT_IMPLEMENTED/PRODUCTION_NOT_READY` until a graph-version amendment freezes provider identity, dedicated-host/VM trust, auditable HDD-backed authority storage, key custody, snapshot/backup independence, network boundary, restore target and its own soak/capacity/recovery evidence. P340 certificates, host fingerprints, UPS evidence and acceptance IDs cannot be reused in that profile.
- The exact mandatory job — **`APPROVED_TARGET`, not yet landed in `.github/`** (F-68: the file named here currently contains one job, `pipeline`, the D-07 eleven-stage Linux pipeline; the present-tense claim below was contradicted by the very file it names) — is `.github/workflows/ci.yml` / `windows-f57-release-precommit` on the approved self-hosted Windows Server 2022 x64 runner with locked MSVC. Its YAML is a thin adapter that invokes only `cargo xtask f57 verify --level l1 --profile windows-f57-release-precommit`; the Rust-owned frozen `WindowsF57ReleasePrecommitPlanV1` deterministically derives and executes the complete auditable subprocess transcript solely owned by [CI pipeline §7.1](../../ci-pipeline.md), including graph and ABI generator checks, PowerShell trust, the complete release/runtime/package/backup/generation/tenancy/UPS/Authority-kernel/adapter/recovery/testkit/release-gate package set, release builds, named Windows composition tests, backup/recovery components and explicit PostgreSQL/backup/UPS test binaries. Task-local tests may add coverage but cannot replace, subtract from or restate a divergent minimum. Linux/macOS, `cfg(windows)` elision or an engineering no-service lane can never satisfy it.
- All authoritative customer data and attributable derivatives persist on the encrypted HDD data volume. The 256 GB SSD contains only OS, binaries, reproducible static material and the closed no-business-data control/code exception set defined in the storage-residency section: bounded POWER capsule, bounded package recovery-continuation capsule, recovery-domain-signed kernel pointer/journal head, and reconstructible signed code slots/cache. The `33554432`-byte cap applies to the POWER capsule; every other exception has its own strict size/retention contract. No exception may contain a customer field or substitute for HDD authority.
- PostgreSQL 16 is the only first-release authoritative database; all other databases are governed providers and have no authoritative write path.
- Every Fresh PostgreSQL proof starts from the same signed pre-F57 baseline: 66 immutable SQL files plus three controlled pre-release draft corrections, followed by the contiguous `CREATED` F57 suffix. The 310 superseded legacy paths and nine absent F55 paths are never applied. At final release this is exactly 69 baseline files + 47 F57 files = 116 applied migrations.
- Every write enters one `CommandPipeline` and records current state, immutable fact, audit, Outbox, and command receipt in one PostgreSQL transaction.
- Every repository operation uses `AuthorizedPgTx`; raw pooled connections and session-scoped security context are forbidden on business paths.
- Runtime authorization uses `PrincipalRefV1`, dynamic scoped grants, field return visibility, and independent query-use permission; role/job names are templates only.
- `CapabilityGraphV1` is the sole business capability authoring source; generated projections carry the same graph digest and generator version and may not be hand-edited.
- `STANDARD` and `DROP_SHIP` are mutually exclusive release families; CTC-01 proves only `STANDARD`, while release certification proves both.
- Local AI remains deferred; CTC-01 uses a deterministic effect simulator and read-only MCP conformance probe.
- The existing single HDD can only qualify for `SINGLE_DISK_DEGRADED_PRODUCTION`; no real customer data is admitted without UPS, server-external append-only backup, two encrypted offline rotation HDDs, separated recovery material, and clean-restore hardware.
- Commits are scoped to one reviewed task. Implementation runs in a dedicated clean F-57 worktree created from the approved base commit. `cargo xtask f57 task begin|stage|verify-staged --task <task-id>` is the only normative staging path; it records the pre-task tree/index/worktree digests, stages only the task registry's allowed post-snapshot changes, and rejects pre-existing dirt, unregistered paths, globs, directory operands, or a cached-set mismatch. G0-01 is the sole bootstrap exception because it creates that command: its brand-new worktree must first prove an empty porcelain status and record the full base commit outside the repository, then its new command accepts only `task stage --task G0-01 --bootstrap-clean-base <full-commit>` and re-proves the worktree/base/allowlist invariants. Existing unrelated worktree changes are never staged.

### 2.1 Exact feature-owner registry

`FeatureOwnerIdV1` is a closed, registry-resolved identifier, not a display label or database-schema guess. G0 creates `docs/f57-feature-owner-registry.v1.tsv` from the following exact 18-row set（F-69：由 17 行增至 18，新增 `inventory-costing`；成因见 00c F-69） with header `feature_owner_id\tcrate_root\tdatabase_schema\trepository_module\tauthoritative_fact_scope`. Rows are UTF-8/LF, sorted by `feature_owner_id`, byte-unique, and exact-joined by the CapabilityGraph, architecture gate, generated DTO manifest, repository registration, business contract, and Fresh-PG ownership checks. Sharing a physical schema never permits sharing a fact or repository writer.

| `feature_owner_id` | Crate root | DB schema | Repository module | Sole authoritative scope |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `contracting` | `crates/features/contracting` | `clm` | `clm::contract_repository` | contract/version/obligation/milestone/attachment-link facts |
| `cpq` | `crates/features/cpq` | `cpq` | `cpq::quote_repository` | quote/version/customer-acceptance facts |
| `crm` | `crates/features/crm` | `crm` | `crm::crm_repository` | opportunity/follow-up facts and authorized customer-360 projection definitions |

| `inventory-costing` | `crates/features/inventory-costing` | `inventory` | `inventory::costing_repository` | inventory value and cost-layer facts: moving-weighted-average unit price and its recomputation, and price-variance splitting |
| `inventory-fulfilment` | `crates/features/inventory-fulfilment` | `inventory` | `inventory::fulfilment_repository` | receipt/delivery/return and quantity/batch/serial facts |
| `operating-ledger` | `crates/features/operating-ledger` | `ledger` | `ledger::operating_ledger_repository` | internal operating entries, mappings, trial balance, and operating periods |

| `portal-identity` | `crates/features/portal-identity` | `portal` | `portal::identity_repository` | invitation and external-subject/customer/contact/legal-entity binding lifecycle |
| `procurement` | `crates/features/procurement` | `procure` | `procure::procurement_repository` | demand/RFQ/supplier-quote/evaluation/award/purchase-order facts |

Credential/authenticator/device/session facts remain owned by the platform mechanism `platform.identity`; Objective/Obligation/Effect/Evidence/Incident/Cycle facts remain owned by `platform.flow`. They are deliberately absent from `FeatureOwnerIdV1`. `CapabilityNodeV1.owner` is a tagged `CapabilityOwnerRefV1::Feature(FeatureOwnerIdV1)` or `CapabilityOwnerRefV1::Platform(PlatformMechanismIdV1)` resolved from the corresponding committed registry; a free-form owner string, short legacy alias (`mdm`, `clm`, `sales`, `finance`, `invoice`, `ledger`, `portal`, `identity`, or `automation`), or crate/schema inference is rejected.

## 3. Stable program interfaces

All child plans use these exact names. A signature change requires a design amendment and coordinated edit to every consuming plan before code changes.

```rust
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct CapabilityGraphV1 {
    pub purpose: CapabilityGraphPurposeV1,
    pub schema_version: u32,
    pub graph_id: String,
    pub graph_version: u64,
    pub architecture_inputs: Vec<ArchitectureInputBindingV1>,
    pub client_lifecycle_fixture_trust_roots: Vec<ClientLifecycleFixtureTrustRootSourceV1>,
    pub client_lifecycle_fixture_sources: Vec<ClientLifecycleFixtureSourceV1>,
    pub capability_package_slot_templates: Vec<CapabilityPackageGraphSlotV1>,
    pub semantic_table_anchors: Vec<SemanticTableAnchorV1>,
    pub semantic_row_schemas: Vec<SemanticRowSchemaV1>,
    pub capabilities: Vec<CapabilityNodeV1>,
}

pub enum CapabilityGraphPurposeV1 { CapabilityGraph }
#[serde(rename_all = "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE")]
pub enum ArchitectureInputIdV1 { ClientStackDecision }
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct ArchitectureInputBindingV1 {
    pub input_id: ArchitectureInputIdV1,
    pub artifact_sha256: Sha256Digest,
    pub archive_manifest_sha256: Sha256Digest,
    pub media_type: String,

// The generator writes exact numeric EVIDENCE_PLACEMENT_CLASS_COUNT_V1,
// EVIDENCE_OBJECT_FIELD_BINDING_COUNT_V1 and EVIDENCE_INPUT_FIELD_BINDING_COUNT_V1
// constants beside these registries. Their reviewed golden freezes every class,
// occurrence-to-class edge and ordinal, and rejects gaps, duplicates, a zero count,
// an unregistered field/class or a count that differs from the generated rows.

pub struct VerifiedEvidenceObjectContractV1 {
    placement_class_ordinal: u32,
    occurrence_binding_ordinal: Option<u32>,
    location_class: EvidenceStoreLocationClassV1,
    media_type: &'static str,
}

impl VerifiedEvidenceObjectContractV1 {
    pub fn placement_class_ordinal(&self) -> u32 { self.placement_class_ordinal }
    pub fn occurrence_binding_ordinal(&self) -> Option<u32> { self.occurrence_binding_ordinal }
    pub fn location_class(&self) -> EvidenceStoreLocationClassV1 { self.location_class }
    pub fn media_type(&self) -> &'static str { self.media_type }
}

pub struct VerifiedEvidenceInputLocationContractV1 {
    placement_class_ordinal: u32,
    occurrence_binding_ordinal: Option<u32>,
    location_class: EvidenceStoreLocationClassV1,
    media_type: &'static str,
}

impl VerifiedEvidenceInputLocationContractV1 {
    pub fn placement_class_ordinal(&self) -> u32 { self.placement_class_ordinal }
    pub fn occurrence_binding_ordinal(&self) -> Option<u32> { self.occurrence_binding_ordinal }
    pub fn location_class(&self) -> EvidenceStoreLocationClassV1 { self.location_class }
    pub fn media_type(&self) -> &'static str { self.media_type }
}

pub struct VerifiedEvidenceInputContractV1 {
    location: VerifiedEvidenceInputLocationContractV1,
    expected_trust_policy_sha256: Sha256Digest,
}

impl VerifiedEvidenceInputContractV1 {
    pub fn location(&self) -> &VerifiedEvidenceInputLocationContractV1 { &self.location }
    pub fn expected_trust_policy_sha256(&self) -> Sha256Digest {
        self.expected_trust_policy_sha256
    }
}

pub trait EvidenceObjectContractResolverV1: Send + Sync {
    fn resolve_class(
        &self,
        placement_class: &EvidencePlacementClassV1,
    ) -> Result<VerifiedEvidenceObjectContractV1, EvidenceStoreErrorV1>;

    fn resolve(
        &self,
        binding: &EvidenceObjectFieldBindingV1,
    ) -> Result<VerifiedEvidenceObjectContractV1, EvidenceStoreErrorV1>;
}

pub trait EvidenceInputContractResolverV1: Send + Sync {
    fn resolve_class_location(
        &self,
        placement_class: &EvidencePlacementClassV1,
    ) -> Result<VerifiedEvidenceInputLocationContractV1, EvidenceStoreErrorV1>;

    fn resolve_location(
        &self,
        binding: &EvidenceInputFieldBindingV1,
    ) -> Result<VerifiedEvidenceInputLocationContractV1, EvidenceStoreErrorV1>;

    fn verify_trust(
        &self,
        location: VerifiedEvidenceInputLocationContractV1,
        trust_policy: &VerifiedArtifactTrustPolicyV1,
    ) -> Result<VerifiedEvidenceInputContractV1, EvidenceStoreErrorV1>;
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum EvidenceStoreErrorV1 {
    InvalidRoot,
    ContractMismatch,
    SourceNotVerified,
    NotFound,
    DigestMismatch,
    ExistingConflict,
    PartialWrite,
    PathEscape,
    ReparsePoint,
    FsyncFailed,
    Io,
}

pub trait EvidenceObjectStoreV1: Send + Sync {
    fn create_or_adopt(
        &self,
        contract: &VerifiedEvidenceObjectContractV1,
        exact_bytes: &[u8],
    ) -> Result<ArtifactRefV1, EvidenceStoreErrorV1>;

    fn load_exact(
        &self,
        expected: &ArtifactRefV1,
        contract: &VerifiedEvidenceObjectContractV1,
    ) -> Result<Vec<u8>, EvidenceStoreErrorV1>;
}

pub trait EvidenceInputStoreV1: Send + Sync {
    fn materialize_signed_envelope(
        &self,
        contract: &VerifiedEvidenceInputContractV1,
        verified: &VerifiedSignedEnvelopeBytesV1,
    ) -> Result<ArtifactRefV1, EvidenceStoreErrorV1>;

    fn load_exact_unverified(
        &self,
        expected: &ArtifactRefV1,
        location: &VerifiedEvidenceInputLocationContractV1,
    ) -> Result<LoadedEvidenceInputV1, EvidenceStoreErrorV1>;

    fn finalize_loaded(
        &self,
        loaded: LoadedEvidenceInputV1,
        contract: &VerifiedEvidenceInputContractV1,
        verified: &VerifiedSignedEnvelopeBytesV1,
    ) -> Result<VerifiedLoadedEvidenceInputV1, EvidenceStoreErrorV1>;
}

// `ProductionAdmissionHoldCauseV1` is the sole reason/reference union; a generic reason string, null cause reference or cross-variant reference is invalid. `PACKAGE_MAINTENANCE` exact-loads the current reservation and may use legal-entity or deployment scope. The three resilience variants require the canonical deployment scope: `CURRENT_ROOTS_ROTATION` freezes the already verified successor topology/storage/trust tuple before hold creation; `DATA_HDD_DISASTER_REPLACEMENT` exact-loads the one immutable two-custodian recovery attempt from the server-external trust path; and `UPS_RUNTIME_LINK_LOSS` exact-loads the one immutable runtime-loss episode whose first stale monotonic tick and deadline never change. Their closed state graphs are cause-specific: package maintenance is `HOLD_INTENT -> ADMISSION_CLOSED -> DRAIN_COMPLETE -> BARRIER_COMMITTED -> CHECKPOINT_BOUND -> FORWARD_INTENT_COMMITTED -> TERMINAL`, with `REOPENED -> TERMINAL` allowed only from `ADMISSION_CLOSED|DRAIN_COMPLETE|BARRIER_COMMITTED|CHECKPOINT_BOUND` after current dual-control cancellation and before forward intent; current-roots rotation is `HOLD_INTENT -> ADMISSION_CLOSED -> DRAIN_COMPLETE -> BARRIER_COMMITTED -> FORWARD_INTENT_COMMITTED -> CHECKPOINT_BOUND -> REOPENED -> TERMINAL`; disaster replacement is `HOLD_INTENT -> ADMISSION_CLOSED -> DRAIN_COMPLETE -> BARRIER_COMMITTED -> FORWARD_INTENT_COMMITTED -> CHECKPOINT_BOUND -> REOPENED -> TERMINAL`, where `DRAIN_COMPLETE` may be constructed only from zero accepted leases or typed proof that the old authority is unreachable and fenced, and `BARRIER_COMMITTED` binds the server-external recovery cut rather than a read from the dead volume; UPS loss is either `HOLD_INTENT -> ADMISSION_CLOSED -> REOPENED -> TERMINAL` after the exact in-window two-fresh-PASS predicate or `HOLD_INTENT -> ADMISSION_CLOSED -> DRAIN_COMPLETE -> BARRIER_COMMITTED -> CHECKPOINT_BOUND -> FORWARD_INTENT_COMMITTED -> REOPENED -> TERMINAL` after fail-safe shutdown and manual recovery. For every cause, `previous_record_sha256` is null only at `HOLD_INTENT`; `drain_result_ref` is nonnull from `DRAIN_COMPLETE`, except the UPS in-window reopen branch where it remains null; `write_barrier_id` is nonnull from `BARRIER_COMMITTED`; `recovery_checkpoint_ref` is nonnull from `CHECKPOINT_BOUND`; fields never return to null. A route may open only inside the upper admission CAS that also resolves the live hold: successful package maintenance appends `TERMINAL` from `FORWARD_INTENT_COMMITTED` only together with the verified `PACKAGE_DELTA|ROLLBACK_REOPEN` admission; pre-forward package cancellation and every resilience release append `REOPENED` under their cause-specific predicate before `TERMINAL`. A standalone `REOPENED`/`TERMINAL` write or terminalization without the matching admission CAS never opens a route.

It proves only path shape/existence, never signer trust, volume role or DATA_HDD residency. The three evidence-specific path nominals remain G0-owned under `xtask/src/f57/` and are not imported by runtime, so `crates/platform/runtime` never depends on `xtask`.

The current normative storage supplement is the `F57AuthorityStorageManifestPayloadV1` above; the 2026-08-23 plan is historical input only. G1-01 solely owns its Rust wire, the non-serialized `AuthorityStorageTrustBootstrapInputPathsV1|ValidatedDataRootV1`, and the only `verify_authority_data_root_v1` constructor in `crates/platform/runtime/src/storage/manifest.rs`, plus strict schema `docs/schemas/f57-authority-storage-manifest.v1.schema.json`; exact media is `application/vnd.ep.f57-authority-storage-manifest-v1+json`, `schema_version=1`, and purpose is `EP-F57-AUTHORITY-STORAGE-MANIFEST-V1`. The signed alias is the one four-field `SignedBusinessArtifactV1<T>` envelope. Revision, authority epoch and root generation are positive; the external-current-configuration issuance descriptor accepts the trusted CMS signing time only in the checked inclusive window `[issued_at_unix_ms,issued_at_unix_ms+300000]` while verification remains `CURRENT_AT_VERIFICATION`; the payload is complete before signing and no signing/TSA time is written back into it. `f56_deployment_manifest_sha256`, deployment, API origin and deployment trust bootstrap exact-match the independently verified Stage-14 manifest. Role wires are exactly `RUNTIME_SSD|DATA_HDD`, occur in that order, and software/data volume identities are nonempty and distinct. Roots are canonical absolute final-handle Windows paths without a trailing separator; software and every DATA_HDD descendant cross no reparse point and exact-match their declared volume. `customer_authority_data_roots`, `backup_target_ids` and `policy_ids` are nonempty, UTF-8-byte sorted and unique; every authority-bearing PostgreSQL/WAL/temp, attachment, audit, Outbox, search, working/generated, package/vault/generation/evidence/archive/release/backup-staging class maps to exactly one longest-prefix DATA_HDD root or is explicitly disabled, and the set includes the global architecture archive and G6 release-evidence roots. The constructor accepts the signed-manifest absolute path plus exactly the six validated absolute paths in `AuthorityStorageTrustBootstrapInputPathsV1`, performs the complete deployment-signature/roster/chain/revocation/checkpoint/anti-rollback and live-final-handle checks, and alone may construct `ValidatedDataRootV1`; its private value carries the canonical path, live volume identity and verified seven-input content identities. G5/G6 store constructors consume that value by reference and have no raw-string/raw-path alternative. The loader rejects unknown fields, drive-letter/UNC/device aliases, equal volumes, SSD authority roots, unlisted persistent classes, root overlap ambiguity, revision/root/checkpoint rollback and trust substitution before any database connection. Schema/serde bytes, every field mutation, final-handle identity, sorted-set, trust rotation, wrong-file/path, signing-window boundaries, signing-time backfill and private-constructor goldens are G1-01-owned; G5/G6/P340 import these nominal types without redefining them.

Release is an idempotent compare-and-set to `RELEASED` with one frozen `released_at_unix_ms>=acquired_at_unix_ms`; ACTIVE requires null and RELEASED requires nonnull. An expired ACTIVE lease stops being a live lease blocker but is not rewritten as RELEASED and cannot be renewed.

`ArtifactPersistentReferenceV1` is independent of lease time. Every signed-root schema directly imports foundation, composes its envelope exactly once, refines `payload` to one local strict payload definition, and closes the result with draft-2020-12 `unevaluatedProperties=false`; it may not copy or relax the other three envelope fields. `signature_cms_b64url` is canonical unpadded base64url of one complete DER CMS value, and the strict verifier recomputes `payload_sha256=SHA256(JCS(payload))` plus the SPKI identity rule. Every F57 schema that uses any foundation-owned nominal has one exact relative `$ref` to this path; a transitive-only use, second primitive/client/delivery/principal/evidence definition, or copied signed-envelope shape is illegal.

G0's schema-DAG bootstrap and final offline-closure golden visit this unique root transitively, reject absolute/network refs, copied definitions, a missing direct foundation edge or any edge back out of foundation, and byte-test all ten principal wires, full `(kind,id)` identity, the seven profile wires `G0_BOOTSTRAP|G1_AUTHORITY_SPINE|G2_CTC_DATA|G3_CLIENT_SHELL|G4_CTC01|G5_INTEGRATION|G6_RELEASE`, all 276 registered TestIDs, both probe assertions, all three data-classification wires, both client-stack wires, all four platform/fixture-role/outcome wires, package/path/runner and every identifier grammar/closed registry, candidate-run and all eight candidate-identity fields, both result-ref shapes, the Fresh-PG ref purpose/shape, digest/token/base64url and unknown-field boundaries before another schema may compile. `UuidV1` serializes and accepts only 36-byte lowercase `8-4-4-4-12` hyphenated text; uppercase, simple, braced, URN, whitespace and malformed aliases fail at its strict serde boundary, and each consuming field separately enforces nil/non-nil semantics stated by its owner.

`docs/evidence/f57-release-carrier-common.v1.schema.json` is the sole canonical schema owner for exactly `ReleaseCarrierBindingV1`, `ReleasePhysicalEvidenceContextV1` and `ReleaseCarrierOutcomeV1`. It is a helper-only descriptor with no artifact binding and imports only `docs/evidence/f57-foundation.v1.schema.json`; it never imports the P340 or consolidated release schema. Both `docs/evidence/f57-p340-soak-evidence.schema.json` and `docs/evidence/f57-release-evidence.schema.json` use exactly one relative `$ref` to this common owner, while release may additionally import P340 in the existing one-way direction; P340 never imports release. G6 Task 10 creates the common schema and its three-type byte/unknown-field goldens before the first authority carrier type is emitted. Task 13 imports it for every P340 context/outcome, and Task 14 imports it for the remaining carrier family, includes it in the generated offline closure, and owns a schema-import-DAG golden that rejects any release↔P340 cycle, copied nominal definition, missing helper descriptor or reverse edge.

The signing interface is deliberately one-way, typed and authorization-carrying: a complete payload and its digest exist before CMS generation, and there is no public bare-digest signing call. Each sole-owner crate implements public cross-crate `CmsSignableArtifactV1` only in generated code and returns one generated public `CmsArtifactTypeIdV1` associated constant. `registered_cms_artifact_descriptor_v1(type_id)` is the sole public lookup for the private-field descriptor. Its projection freezes the stable artifact-type wire, ordinal, exact kind/discriminator/producer/runner/trust-domain and issuance rule; `descriptor_sha256=SHA256(JCS(CmsArtifactDescriptorProjectionV1))`. Neither Rust module path, crate alias, compiler `type_name` nor `TypeId` enters this persistent digest. Foundation's sole `prepare_cms_signing_request_v1` looks up and exact-matches that stable type ID, recomputes `SHA256(JCS(payload))`, asks one trust-domain `CmsAuthorizationDecisionProviderV1<T>` for its already verified context/row and durable operation decision, validates every returned scalar, and alone constructs private `VerifiedCmsSigningRequestV1<T>`. The only production decision-provider families are `ArtifactSignerRegistryBootstrapAuthorizerV1` for the one 89-row registry-bootstrap payload, `F57EvidenceSigningAuthorizerV1` for its candidate-evidence rows, `GenerationApprovalRegistryBootstrapAuthorizerV1` for the one signed generation-approval-registry payload, `GenerationApprovalSigningAuthorizerV1` for that registry's three generation/reverse-plan/migration rows, `CapabilityPackageTrustRegistryBootstrapAuthorizerV1` for the one signed package-trust registry, and `CapabilityPackageSigningAuthorizerV1` for that registry's package and customer-maintenance-plan rows. The three bootstrap authorizers are mutually disjoint, pinned to their own exact SPKI/DN/trust policies, and cannot sign a child row or one another's registry. The package child authorizer additionally requires the exact issuer-role matrix; its customer-maintenance-plan branch consumes only the private dual-control/window/checkpoint plan-finalization authorization described below. The generated implementation registry and architecture check reject any handwritten/unregistered impl or type-ID reuse before build; dynamic JSON never has an entry. Goldens prove a module re-export/refactor leaves the stable descriptor digest unchanged and reject every cross-bootstrap, cross-row, cross-kind and vendor-to-maintenance combination.

The authorization hash has no self-reference. `CmsIssuanceWindowProjectionV1` is the exact tagged union `INCLUSIVE{not_before_unix_ms,not_after_unix_ms}|STATIC_NONE`: inclusive requires `not_before<=not_after`, including the one-instant equality boundary; static-none has no time fields and is legal only for the signer-registry descriptor. Every inversion, wrong descriptor or attempted mixed/partial shape returns `InvalidIssuanceWindow` before operation allocation or provider journal access. Foundation canonicalizes that valid union and computes `issuance_window_sha256=SHA256(JCS(window))`, computes `provider_handle_sha256=SHA256(exact ProviderSignerHandleIdV1 bytes)`, constructs the exact nine-field `CmsAuthorizationBindingV1`, then sets `authorization_sha256=SHA256(JCS(binding))`. `CmsProviderSigningRequestV1` contains that binding and digest plus the exact window and handle; the provider recomputes all three digests and rejects any mutation. `sign_business_artifact_v1` consumes the private typed request, rechecks descriptor/payload/binding, calls only `DetachedCmsSignerV1::sign_authorized`, then foundation-validates canonical CMS base64url and exact result SPKI against the authorization before constructing the envelope. `VerifiedCmsSigningAuthorizationV1::provider_request`, the checked nonempty `ProviderSignerHandleIdV1::try_from_bytes` and its read-only `as_bytes` are the external adapter's complete construction/read surface; the typed provider result is never itself a verified envelope. Goldens mutate every descriptor, binding, window and provider-handle field and cover equal-bound, inversion, static-none misuse and integer extremes; real `ep-platform-release`, evidence-trust/KMS and adapter compile tests prove legal downstream payload implementation, decision production and signer-port implementation without a reverse dependency or private-field access.

The broker/provider contract is durably idempotent across response loss. Before a provider may sign, its protected operation journal commits `(signing_operation_id,authorization-digest,payload-digest,issuance-window-digest,signer-role)`; the first completed CMS/TSA bytes are then committed under that tuple. Repeating the identical operation queries/adopts and returns byte-identical CMS bytes, while any field drift returns `SigningOperationConflict`; a provider that cannot durably query/adopt an operation—including an existing enterprise signer or TSA path—is not compatible. Crash goldens cover loss before provider commit, after provider commit before broker receipt, after broker commit before caller receipt and after caller spool/object write. The signer must obtain the trusted CMS/RFC-3161 time and reject unless it lies inside the resulting inclusive window, and the offline verifier repeats the same derivation with archived chain and revocation state at the actual trusted signing time. No contract may require a payload field to equal a signing/TSA time that becomes known only after the payload digest exists.

The runtime-topology certification verifier exact-matches `candidate_run` and `candidate_manifest_ref` to the terminal P340 binding; the candidate's `runtime_topology_declaration_ref` to `topology_declaration_ref`; `capacity_certificate_ref` to the same soak's reachable capacity certificate; profile IDs, host fingerprint, `20` users and `259200` seconds across declaration, policy/input, soak and certificate; declaration storage-manifest identity to the candidate/G6 root binding and P340 DATA_HDD; declaration policy-definition ref to the P340 attestation's definition; and graph/generation digests to the candidate and active generation. A pre-P340 object, another terminal recipe, ref/profile/storage/policy/host/capacity drift, a declaration containing candidate/soak/capacity fields, or declaration-only production activation fails. Crash adoption accepts only the byte-identical checkpoint-derived plain certification.

The G6 topology-certification authority additionally exact-loads the final candidate's generation manifest, approval-registry and participant-ACK refs. It reconstructs `VerifiedGenerationManifestV1` only through the named approval verifier, proves the candidate generation is the same durable OBSERVED generation used by the declaration, exact-joins every ACK to the manifest/declaration and same activation attempt, and compares the fresh live participant/item readback before certification. A generic proof, missing bundle byte, desired-only generation, registry drift or an ACK set that is merely database-current but differs from the signed candidate fails closed.

The offline schema closure always contains generation manifest/reverse-plan/ACK plus participant apply/rollback-readback media, the pinned generation-approval registry, runtime topology, capability-package operational media, package trust registry, backup topology/topology-signing-trust-manifest/topology-signing-trust-current-pointer/storage-safeguard/checkpoint/recovery-cut media, PostgreSQL 16 Windows package-lock/install-contract/install-readback, UPS manifest/status/command/ACK, production-generation-admission/hold/execution-lease media, the exact production-admission-bypass registry, and client-common. From each signed-generation package item it follows desired item → package registry + desired package → implementation manifest → every implementation artifact/SBOM/schema/WIT/signature/migration/foundation ref, plus the concrete scope's tenancy snapshot. Reverse traversal is exhaustive by tag: `RESTORE_ARTIFACT` reaches the distinct prior desired item; `DEACTIVATE_RETAIN_DATA` reaches the original forward item, per-attempt transition, `ABSENT` installed-state readback and nonnull retained-data proof; `NO_OP` reaches the source desired item. Generation 1 `NO_OBSERVED_GENERATION` may use only the latter two policy-valid branches and never fabricates a predecessor. From each selected ACK it follows `participant_apply_readback_ref` → canonical item readbacks → nonnull package generation transition → execution-trust snapshot and typed operation/results/final installed readback; a maintenance transition additionally reaches reservation, signed historical plan, current execution authorization, both current decisions, source/target package implementations, admission hold, actual BACKUP checkpoint and full `AuthorityRecoveryCutManifestV1`. Production deltas additionally reach the exact admission predecessor/ACK/transition/resource envelope. No plan-finalization journal is copied or replayed offline: its crash behavior is tested operationally, while the certificate bundle closes only immutable artifacts/readbacks. No registry/path scan or developer allowlist exists. Missing/orphan/extra/wrong-media/cross-scope/cross-cut ref, target-only/current substitute, implementation byte outside its manifest, or package-local `APPLIED_VERIFIED` treated as OBSERVED/admitted fails the graph walk.

| Signed payload category | Sole issuance authority and exact inclusive window |
|---|---|
| intrinsic `issued_at_unix_ms,expires_at_unix_ms` | `[issued,min(issued+300000,expires)]` |
| `CapabilityPackagePayloadV1` without an intrinsic clock | exact private durable `PACKAGE_SIGNING_AUTHORIZATION_STARTED` record `[authorized_at_unix_ms,min(authorized_at_unix_ms+300000,verified_package_registry.expires_at_unix_ms)]`; verification additionally requires the registry row and complete signer chain current at trusted verification time |
| intrinsic `generated_at_unix_ms,expires_at_unix_ms` | `[generated,min(generated+300000,expires)]` |
| current-approved runtime configuration with intrinsic `issued_at_unix_ms` only | `[issued,issued+300000]` with checked arithmetic and `CURRENT_AT_VERIFICATION`; exact kinds are `SignedF57AuthorityStorageManifestV1\|SignedGenerationManifestV1\|SignedGenerationReversePlanV1` |
| header/slot/attempt `created_at_unix_ms,expires_at_unix_ms` | `[created,min(created+300000,expires)]` |
| carrier staging completion | exact verified `CARRIER_STAGING_COMPLETION_FINALIZATION_STARTED` window `[issued_at_unix_ms,expires_at_unix_ms]`; `completed_at_unix_ms` remains the independently derived physical finish and never selects CMS time |
| gate/architecture journal record with `recorded_at_unix_ms` only | `[recorded,recorded+300000]`, additionally bounded by the verified owning header expiry |
| raw carrier or nested physical readback with context but no own issue field | `[context.finished_at,min(context.finished_at+300000,context.expires_at)]` |
| G0 journal-finalized aggregate | exact verified `EVIDENCE_ENVELOPE_FINALIZATION_STARTED` issued/expiry window |
| candidate manifest | exact verified `CANDIDATE_MANIFEST_FINALIZATION_STARTED.issued_at_unix_ms` through the owning journal-header expiry |
| permanent client-stack decision | exact verified architecture `DECISION_FINALIZATION_STARTED` decided/signing-not-after window |
| reviewed non-expiring bootstrap/static artifact | exact static-none descriptor; currently the signer registry is the sole signed F57 exception |

Every addition to `SignedBusinessArtifactV1<T>` must add exactly one descriptor row before it compiles or verifies; overlapping rows or an unknown kind fail generation. All additions, minima and five-minute bounds use checked `i128`. A time-bearing payload can never select static-none. An inverted/empty window, signature before physical finish, signature after a finalization/input/header expiry, absent/unprovable trusted signing time, or crash-time attempt to alter a frozen payload/window fails closed. Per-category goldens cover both boundaries, before/after, missing authority, wrong category and overflow.

G0-01 solely owns `PrincipalKindV1|PrincipalRefV1` at `crates/foundation/src/principal.rs` and in the zero-import foundation schema; G1-02 consumes those nominals and solely owns grant/authorization semantics. G1-03 solely owns `VerifiedSecurityContextV1|SecurityContextPurposeV1|SecurityContextMacAlgorithmV1|SecurityContextMacV1|SecurityContextEnvelopeV1` at `crates/foundation/src/security/context.rs`, private `SecurityContextIssuerV1|IssuedSecurityContextEnvelopeV1` and the ticket/verifier at `crates/adapter/db-pg/src/context_ticket.rs`, and `AuthorizedPgTx` at `crates/adapter/db-pg/src/authorized_tx.rs`. `docs/schemas/f57-security-context-envelope.v1.schema.json` is the sole JSON-Schema owner for the complete security-context envelope wire and has exactly one import, `../evidence/f57-foundation.v1.schema.json`, for principal/UUID/digest definitions; exact media is `application/vnd.ep.f57-security-context-envelope-v1+json`. This internal transaction credential is not a `SignedBusinessArtifactV1`, evidence artifact, offline-schema descriptor or signer-registry row. The strict envelope fixes `schema_version=1`, purpose `EP-F57-SECURITY-CONTEXT-V1`, algorithm `HMAC_SHA_256`, positive `key_epoch|policy_version|authority_epoch`, nonnil issuer/key/principal/legal-entity/nonce UUIDs, nonzero generation digest and `issued_at_unix_ms < expires_at_unix_ms` with checked lifetime `1..=30000` ms. Issuer time, nonce and all authorization/version fields come only from private `SecurityContextIssuerV1::issue(&VerifiedSecurityContextV1)` plus the trusted context-issuer clock; an ingress/client payload or public caller can never construct or submit an envelope. `SecurityContextMacV1` has no public raw-byte constructor and accepts/serializes exactly one 64-lowercase-hex 32-byte value.

The MAC has one library-independent fixed preimage, never JCS, JSON text, PostgreSQL `jsonb`, a field-name map or a caller-supplied digest. It is the byte concatenation `ASCII("EP-F57-SECURITY-CONTEXT-MAC-V1\0") || u32be(schema_version) || purpose_u8 || issuer_uuid16 || key_uuid16 || u64be(key_epoch) || algorithm_u8 || principal_kind_u8 || principal_uuid16 || legal_entity_uuid16 || u64be(policy_version) || u64be(authority_epoch) || generation_sha256_32 || i64be(issued_at_unix_ms) || i64be(expires_at_unix_ms) || nonce_uuid16`. UUID bytes are RFC-4122 network-order bytes; signed integers are two's-complement big-endian. `purpose_u8=0x01`, `algorithm_u8=0x01`, and principal-kind bytes are exactly `USER=01,GROUP=02,TEAM=03,PROJECT=04,DEPARTMENT=05,SERVICE=06,AI=07,PLUGIN=08,CUSTOMER=09,SUPPLIER=0a`. The 32-byte signature is exactly `HMAC-SHA-256(the selected 32-byte issuer secret,preimage)` and is compared without variant-specific error leakage. The immutable context-binding digest used below is `SHA256(ASCII("EP-F57-SECURITY-CONTEXT-BINDING-V1\0") || preimage || signature32)`. Rust uses fixed-width `to_be_bytes`/UUID bytes; PostgreSQL uses the equivalent `int4send|int8send|uuid_send` bytea construction. Cross-language byte goldens must match before G1-03 can pass.

The G1-03 migration owns one closed `platform_core.security_context_issuer_keys` registry keyed by `(issuer_id,key_id,key_epoch)`, with exact key states `ISSUE_ACTIVE|VERIFY_ONLY|REVOKED`, a 32-byte secret, `valid_from_unix_ms < issue_not_after_unix_ms <= verify_not_after_unix_ms`, and a partial uniqueness constraint allowing exactly one `ISSUE_ACTIVE` row per issuer. Only the NOLOGIN SECURITY-DEFINER owner can read key bytes; business, context-issuer, migration, operations and recovery roles remain disjoint, and every function fixes `search_path=pg_catalog,platform_core` and uses no caller-resolved object or dynamic SQL. Private `SecurityContextIssuerV1::issue` accepts only `&VerifiedSecurityContextV1`, invokes the fixed issuer-pool SECURITY-DEFINER issuance function, revalidates the context's current policy/authority epoch/generation, samples trusted issue time and a fresh CSPRNG nonce, selects the sole current `ISSUE_ACTIVE` row itself, and requires issue time in `[valid_from_unix_ms,issue_not_after_unix_ms)`. The function returns the complete strict MACed envelope; only the strict parser plus exact field/preimage readback may wrap it as private `IssuedSecurityContextEnvelopeV1`. It has no overload accepting fields, JSON, an envelope, key ID, time or nonce. Rotation holds the issuer row lock, requires `new_epoch=old_epoch+1`, installs a fresh key, and atomically changes the previous key to `VERIFY_ONLY` with `verify_not_after=min(old_verify_not_after,rotation_time+30000)`; an epoch/key reuse, rollback, second active key or transition out of `REVOKED` is impossible. Verification selects the exact envelope tuple, accepts `ISSUE_ACTIVE` or `VERIFY_ONLY` only while trusted `now` lies in the checked intersection `[envelope.issued_at_unix_ms,min(envelope.expires_at_unix_ms,verify_not_after_unix_ms)]` and the original issuance time remains in that row's issuance interval, and always rejects `REVOKED`, unknown, expired or ambient/network keys. A rotation concurrent with issuance yields exactly either a complete old-key envelope that remains VERIFY_ONLY-valid for its frozen lifetime or a complete new-key envelope; no mixed key ID/epoch/MAC is representable. Key material is never returned to Rust, logged, placed in a GUC, copied to evidence or included in an error.

`PgUnitOfWork::begin_authorized(&VerifiedSecurityContextV1)` is the sole public constructor path and contains the complete order; no public/private sibling accepts `SecurityContextEnvelopeV1`. It first calls private `SecurityContextIssuerV1::issue`; only after obtaining one `IssuedSecurityContextEnvelopeV1` does it check out one business connection, execute `BEGIN`, obtain the exact `SecurityContextBackendBindingV1 {database_oid:u32,backend_pid:i32,backend_start_unix_us:i64,transaction_id_xid8:u64,database_role_oid:u32}`, and send that value plus the issuer product to the disjoint context-ticket pool. `backend_start_unix_us` is the checked signed microseconds from Unix epoch of the same connection's `pg_stat_activity.backend_start`; `transaction_id_xid8` is the positive full `pg_current_xact_id()` value, never the wrapping 32-bit XID. In one separate committed control transaction, the ticket function reconstructs and verifies the MAC/current policy-authority-generation tuple, inserts the unique nonce claim `(issuer_id,key_id,nonce)` and generates exactly 32 CSPRNG bytes for a backend ticket. The ticket row stores only `SHA256(ticket32)`, the context-binding digest, all five backend/transaction fields, and trusted `issued_at_unix_ms < expires_at_unix_ms=min(issued_at+5000,envelope.expires_at)`; presentation accepts trusted `now` only in that inclusive interval. It is durably marked single-delivery before the raw ticket is returned once. The nonce claim and ticket row commit together and their uniqueness tombstones remain until the selected key can no longer verify any envelope, so rollback of the later business transaction cannot resurrect either. Loss before/during envelope issuance returns no issuer product and retry re-issues from the same still-current private context with a fresh trusted time/nonce; loss after a complete envelope but before ticket commit leaves no nonce/ticket authority; loss after ticket commit burns that nonce/ticket and cannot adopt or replay it. Every retry restarts at `issue`, never accepts a retained/caller envelope. This durable burn, the exact xid8/backend-start/role binding and the unique verified-context row make the ticket one-use without pretending PostgreSQL has an autonomous subtransaction inside the business transaction.

The business connection then invokes only the fixed SECURITY-DEFINER apply function with typed envelope fields and the private ticket. That function independently reconstructs/verifies the MAC, hashes the ticket, exact-matches the durable ticket/context binding, expiry, nonce claim and current five-field backend tuple, and inserts exactly one `platform_core.verified_transaction_contexts` row keyed by `(database_oid,backend_pid,backend_start_unix_us,transaction_id_xid8)` before applying only transaction-local `set_config(...,true)` values. RLS helpers authorize only by exact-joining that current xid8/backend tuple to this verified row and comparing the binding digest; a raw `SET`, `SET LOCAL`, copied GUC, forged row or prior transaction's committed audit row is never authority. The function returns a typed readback of every envelope field, issuer row, binding digest and backend tuple. The adapter compares all fields byte-for-byte and only then constructs private `VerifiedSecurityContextEnvelopeV1` and `AuthorizedPgTx`; repositories accept only `&mut AuthorizedPgTx`, and no query/write repository call can occur earlier. A second apply, savepoint/control statement before authorization, readback difference or uncertain outcome rolls back and poisons the connection rather than returning a transaction.

Pool hygiene is part of the constructor contract, not a best-effort cleanup. Checkout requires protocol state `IDLE`, the expected session/current role and null F57 context GUCs. Every commit, rollback, cancellation, timeout, panic and constructor error runs an out-of-transaction `DISCARD ALL`, then rechecks role, protocol state and all context GUCs before check-in; if rollback, discard or readback is uncertain/fails, the socket is closed and never pooled. `SET LOCAL` therefore clears normally, while the verified-row join prevents even deliberate session residue from authorizing. G1-03 owns strict schema/serde and Rust↔SQL preimage goldens for all ten principal kinds, every field mutation, UUID/text/endianness aliases, invalid MAC length/case, both time boundaries/overflow, unknown/rotated/revoked keys, epoch rollback, nonce replay, ticket response loss/reuse, each backend/PID/start/xid8/role mismatch, direct function/row/GUC forgery, readback drift, and crash cuts before/after issue, active-key rotation, ticket commit and context apply. The issue matrix proves a caller-supplied/raw/replayed envelope is unrepresentable, loss before issuer commit yields no product, loss after response cannot be adopted by another invocation, and each rotation cut yields exactly one internally consistent old-or-new key tuple. Its pool matrix must reuse the same physical connection after commit, rollback, savepoint rollback, cancellation, timeout and panic and prove zero residue; no implementation may weaken these cases to a mock-only assertion.

`docs/evidence/f57-generation.v1.schema.json` is the sole schema owner and `crates/platform/release/src/generation.rs` the sole Rust nominal/wire owner of the generation family displayed above; `participant.rs`, `activation_attempt.rs`, `ep-platform-generation-activation::{coordinator,verified_graph}` and their stores import those nominals and own behavior only. No retired `release/src/activation.rs` exists. The schema imports `f57-foundation.v1.schema.json` directly, composes its detached-CMS envelope exactly once for each of the signed manifest and signed reverse-plan roots, and owns separate strict plain participant apply-readback, rollback-readback and ACK roots; it imports no topology, graph, storage, G1, P340 or release-evidence schema. Exact manifest/reverse-plan/ACK purpose/media pairs are `EP-F57-GENERATION-MANIFEST-V1` / `application/vnd.ep.f57-generation-manifest-v1+json`, `EP-F57-GENERATION-REVERSE-PLAN-V1` / `application/vnd.ep.f57-generation-reverse-plan-v1+json`, and `EP-F57-GENERATION-PARTICIPANT-ACK-V1` / `application/vnd.ep.f57-generation-participant-ack-v1+json`; those three strict roots have exactly 13, 9 and 14 fields as displayed. `GenerationManifestV1` and `GenerationReversePlanV1` are payloads, never signed-envelope aliases or nested wrappers.

`docs/schemas/f57-generation-approval-registry.v1.schema.json` and `crates/platform/release/src/generation_approval.rs` are the sole schema/Rust owners of the approval registry. The signed-root schema directly imports exact relative `$ref` `../evidence/f57-foundation.v1.schema.json`, composes its detached-CMS envelope exactly once, narrows only `payload` to the local strict type, closes with draft-2020-12 `unevaluatedProperties=false`, and imports no generation/topology/storage/G1/P340/release schema. Its signed payload has exactly seven fields `{schema_version,purpose,deployment_id,revision,rows,issued_at_unix_ms,expires_at_unix_ms}`; purpose/media are `EP-F57-GENERATION-APPROVAL-REGISTRY-V1` / `application/vnd.ep.f57-generation-approval-registry-v1+json`. It has exactly three canonical unique five-field rows `{artifact_kind,media_type,signer_subject,certificate_subject_dn,validity_rule}` for `GENERATION_MANIFEST_V1`, `GENERATION_REVERSE_PLAN_V1` and `MIGRATION_PLAN_V1`, with their exact media, nonempty DN, strict SPKI token and `CURRENT_AT_VERIFICATION`; there is no wildcard/default/other row. The registry envelope is bootstrap-verified only by the product-pinned deployment trust bundle and exact registry-authority SPKI/DN. The verified storage manifest's canonical `policy_ids` contains exactly one mandatory `generation-approval-registry-sha256:<64-lowerhex>` member; it pins the exact registry envelope at the fixed derived DATA_HDD source path `generations/trust/generation-approval-registry.v1.json`. The registry deployment ID must match, revision is positive, `issued_at_unix_ms < expires_at_unix_ms`, and its current chain/revocation plus pinned digest are checked before private `VerifiedGenerationApprovalRegistryV1` can be constructed. That fixed source path is bootstrap input only: G1-01 must create-new copy/fsync/reload the exact verified envelope into its authority-generation bundle at `inputs/<whole-envelope-sha256>.json`, and the wrapper provenance is the relocatable ref `evidence-relative://bundle/inputs/<whole-envelope-sha256>.json`. Rotation therefore requires a newer signed storage manifest that pins the new registry digest; an adjacent file, old valid registry, ambient Windows trust or registry self-root cannot authorize anything.

Registry rows sort in the artifact-kind order displayed above. Their media are respectively `application/vnd.ep.f57-generation-manifest-v1+json`, `application/vnd.ep.f57-generation-reverse-plan-v1+json`, and `application/vnd.ep.f57-migration-plan-v1+json`; their certificate DNs are respectively `CN=EP Generation Manifest Authority,O=Enterprise Platform`, `CN=EP Generation Reverse Plan Authority,O=Enterprise Platform`, and `CN=EP Migration Plan Authority,O=Enterprise Platform`. The registry envelope itself requires `CN=EP Generation Approval Registry Authority,O=Enterprise Platform`. Every `signer_subject` is the exact `spki-sha256:<64-lowerhex>` token recomputed from the provisioned nonexportable leaf matching that row; a DN, placeholder token, same-DN/different-key or same-key/different-DN substitution fails.

Production trust material is not an ambient prerequisite. G1-01 creates the one deployment-global `AuthorityStorageManifestRotationCoordinatorV1`: its port/state/schema are solely owned by `crates/platform/runtime/src/storage/manifest_rotation.rs`, its fixed DATA_HDD journal/store by `crates/adapter/file/src/storage_manifest_rotation_store.rs`, its recovery-tool composition by `apps/recovery-tool/src/storage_manifest_rotation.rs`, and its strict wire by `docs/schemas/f57-authority-storage-manifest-rotation.v1.schema.json`. `apps/recovery-tool/src/generation_trust.rs` is only the generation-domain typed adapter to that coordinator, while `crates/platform/runtime/src/secrets/generation_trust.rs` owns the private `GenerationTrustProviderV1` port. The port has exactly four disjoint roles: approval-registry authority, generation-manifest authority, generation-reverse-plan authority and migration-plan authority. Its two supported adapters—self-hosted Windows CNG/PIV and an approved existing enterprise signer—must produce the identical registry/SPKI/DN/CMS contract and implement the same durable `(signing_operation_id,authorization_digest) -> byte-identical CMS` query/adopt protocol; a signer or TSA that can only create a fresh signature after response loss is rejected at provisioning. Neither adapter may invent a root, export a private key, select a caller signer, or send a payload rather than its approved digest to a remote signer. In the local adapter the exact nonexportable key-container identities are `EP-F57-GENERATION-APPROVAL-REGISTRY-V1`, `EP-F57-GENERATION-MANIFEST-V1`, `EP-F57-GENERATION-REVERSE-PLAN-V1`, and `EP-F57-MIGRATION-PLAN-V1`; key/certificate import proves provider, nonexportability, usage, ACL, SPKI, DN and complete current chain. The online core process receives only manifest/reverse-plan role handles. Registry signing remains an explicit maintenance ceremony, and the migration role is reachable only through its separately approved migration workflow. The generation adapter builds/signs or verifies the exact registry, emits its whole-envelope digest for the independently signed storage-manifest policy pin, and submits one immutable typed domain change to the global coordinator. Initial install and rotation first create immutable revision bytes below `<data_root>\generations\trust\revisions\`; only the global maintenance lock, monotonic storage-manifest CAS and fsynced hash-chain journal may project the selected bytes to `generations\trust\generation-approval-registry.v1.json` and the canonical storage-manifest location. A crash resumes the same signed pair, never chooses latest files. Old revisions remain immutable. The fixed active path may be atomically replaced only by this global journal after a higher storage-manifest revision pins the new digest; “never edits in place” forbids byte mutation/overwrite outside this protocol. Missing role, non-idempotent remote provider, exportable/aliased key, cross-role ACL, self-root, half-installed pair, rollback or any second manifest writer leaves boot closed before any database connection.

G1-01 also owns the missing production reverse-plan path. Before signing a generation, private `GenerationReversePlanAuthorityV1` derives—not accepts—one action per canonical item from the verified prior durable OBSERVED item set and compiled rollback policy: an existing prior item uses `RESTORE_ARTIFACT` to that distinct prior artifact, a newly introduced safely deactivatable item uses `DEACTIVATE_RETAIN_DATA`, and `NO_OP` is available only when the compiled policy explicitly proves it safe; otherwise creation fails. `GenerationCreationAttemptStoreV1` is a DATA_HDD, final-handle-bound, create-new store whose exact root is `<verified-data-root>\generations\creation-attempts\<lowercase-hyphenated-deployment-id>\<20-digit-zero-padded-authority-epoch>\<20-digit-zero-padded-generation-number>\`. It owns only `creation-attempt.v1.jcs.jsonl`, `spool\reverse-plans\<GenerationItemIdV1>.signed.v1.json`, and `spool\generation-manifest.signed.v1.json`; the journal uses the common `len8<TAB>JCS<LF>` framing, contiguous hash chaining and fsync of file plus parent, while a spool path never enters a signed wire.

Before the first provider request, the ATTEMPT_FROZEN prefix commits the complete re-derivable verified inputs, one unpredictable creation-attempt ID and plan ID per item, every plan/manifest issued time, exact relocatable registry/storage/graph/projection/policy refs, the closed object-locator formula, and one unpredictable `signing_operation_id` per reverse plan plus one for the manifest. For each output, a strictly extending pre-request record then binds its operation ID, signer role, payload digest, issuance-window digest and authorization digest. It does **not** freeze an object digest/ref or “expected object destination” before CMS/TSA bytes exist. The provider/broker must durably query/adopt that exact operation and return byte-identical CMS after response loss. Only after the signed envelope is typed-reloaded from its fixed create-new spool does the authority compute the whole-envelope digest/ref, append the OBJECT_BOUND stage, ingest through the authority-lane `EvidenceObjectStoreV1`, and typed-reload/domain-verify that object. After every plan ref exact-matches the frozen item set, the manifest follows the same authorization → spool → object → reload sequence, and only that content-addressed ref may become the generation identity/declaration input.

Recovery follows only this attempt journal and exact fixed spool locators: it queries/adopts a provider-committed operation, adopts identical spool/object bytes, or creates only the next absent frozen stage. It never scans, regenerates an ID/time/action, invokes a second signing operation, overwrites, or selects a newer registry. The immutable order is `ATTEMPT_FROZEN -> per-output SIGNING_AUTHORIZATION_COMMITTED -> provider commit/adopt -> spool durable -> object ref computed/bound -> object typed reload -> manifest authorization/commit/spool/object/reload -> declaration object`; crash-cut goldens cover loss before and after provider commit, before and after broker response, and before and after every spool/object/reload edge. A conflicting authorization, CMS byte, spool, object/ref or re-derived input permanently fails that attempt while leaving prior OBSERVED intact.

Only `GenerationApprovalVerifierV1` configured by that private registry proof may turn a generic verified manifest into private `VerifiedGenerationManifestV1`; generation consumers accept the domain-specific wrapper, never the generic proof, raw payload or double-wrapped envelope. `GenerationItemIdV1` accepts only 3–160 byte lowercase `[a-z][a-z0-9._-]{2,159}` text. Items are canonical and unique by `item_id`; their closed kinds serialize exactly as `CAPABILITY_GRAPH|PROJECTION_SET|MIGRATION_PLAN|CAPABILITY_PACKAGE|POLICY_BUNDLE|UI_SCHEMA|PROVIDER_MANIFEST|RUNTIME_ARTIFACT`, and every forward artifact is typed-verified in its owning runtime trust domain. Every `reverse_plan_ref` typed-loads exact signed `GenerationReversePlanV1` under the registry's reverse-plan row and exact-matches its `item_id` and `source_artifact_ref` to the enclosing item. Reverse actions serialize exactly as `RESTORE_ARTIFACT|DEACTIVATE_RETAIN_DATA|NO_OP`; retention is always `RETAIN_ALL_GENERATION_DATA`. `RESTORE_ARTIFACT` requires a distinct nonnull target, `DEACTIVATE_RETAIN_DATA` requires null target, and `NO_OP` requires target byte-equal source; an unsafe item kind cannot use NO_OP unless its compiled rollback policy explicitly permits it. The manifest contains exactly one item whose artifact ref equals `capability_graph_ref` and exactly one whose artifact ref equals `projection_manifest_ref`. Required participants and each required-item set are canonical unique complete deterministic derivations of the compiled graph; `participant_definition_sha256=SHA256(JCS(the exact derived RuntimeParticipantV1 row))`, so no caller supplies a digest or participant subset.

Generation numbering is server-only and positive: generation 1 has `previous_observed_generation_digest_sha256=null`; every later manifest repeats the exact digest of the immediately prior durable OBSERVED signed envelope and cannot skip, fork or refer to a desired-only generation. The one generation identity is `generation_digest_sha256=SHA256(the exact complete canonical-JCS bytes of SignedBusinessArtifactV1<GenerationManifestV1>)`, byte-equal to `generation_manifest_ref.sha256`; it is never the payload hash, graph hash, generation number, reserialized envelope or a caller digest. Signing and verification use only the separately pinned generation/migration approval trust registry, never the 89-row F57 candidate-evidence registry. `VerifiedGenerationManifestV1` retains the authority-generation bundle's exact relocatable registry ref as non-wire provenance, exposes read-only accessors, and has no public/raw constructor; a fixed source path, proof created under another trust domain or ref to bytes not materialized under the current verified bundle root is a type mismatch. G0 owns parsing, validation, byte goldens, the approval-verifier boundary and pure digest helper but has no production signer/store/ACK call site. Only after G1-01 has verified the storage manifest and DATA_HDD may it copy/reload the signed storage manifest and approval registry into exact digest-named authority-bundle inputs, materialize graph/projection/policy and every other signed-generation dependency under their canonical relocatable refs, freeze inputs/IDs/times, derive/sign/ingest/reload the complete per-item reverse-plan set, and sign/ingest/reload generation 1. Only then may it obtain `VerifiedGenerationManifestV1` and pass that proof into its declaration authority. Later generations use the same G1 attempt/authority path after exact current OBSERVED-state and approval checks; no client, plugin or participant can submit a plan or manifest.

`GenerationParticipantV1` is a strict fourteen-field authenticated-internal ACK, not user-signed evidence. G1-05 alone constructs it after authenticated Service-SID IPC and a create-new stored/reloaded strict `GenerationParticipantApplyReadbackV1` exact-matches manifest, declaration and participant requirement under one durable `activation_attempt_id`. The readback's canonical `applied_items` exact-set matches `required_item_ids`; every package item has a nonnull typed `generation_transition_ref`, and `readiness_refs` close all operation results/final installed-state evidence. The ACK repeats `participant_definition_sha256`, recomputes `applied_item_set_sha256`, carries the exact `participant_apply_readback_ref`, and samples one trusted `acknowledged_at_unix_ms` only after successful readback and before the same serialized OBSERVED commit. It has no CMS/envelope. A failed/UNKNOWN readback produces no ACK. Rollback analogously persists/reloads `GenerationParticipantRollbackReadbackV1`; `ROLLBACK_COMMITTED` requires the exact tagged rollback target, canonical reverse item set, rollback ID and successful outcome. `PRIOR_OBSERVED_GENERATION` requires the exact predecessor manifest ref/digest; `NO_OBSERVED_GENERATION` is legal only while rolling back generation 1 and forbids a fabricated predecessor. OBSERVED moves only for exactly one bound ACK per required participant from the same attempt/generation/declaration. Desired, OBSERVED and production-admitted remain separate, and recovery adopts the original attempt/readbacks rather than replaying participant work.

`CapabilityGraphPurposeV1`, `RuntimeTopologyDeclarationPurposeV1`, `RuntimeTopologyCertificationPurposeV1`, `SignedArtifactRefPurposeV1`, `FreshPgEvidencePurposeV1`, and `CandidateBoundFreshPgReceiptRefPurposeV1` are closed single-variant enums whose exact serialized values are respectively `EP-F57-CAPABILITY-GRAPH-V1`, `EP-F57-RUNTIME-TOPOLOGY-DECLARATION-V1`, `EP-F57-RUNTIME-TOPOLOGY-CERTIFICATION-V1`, `EP-F57-SIGNED-ARTIFACT-REF-V1`, `EP-F57-CANDIDATE-BOUND-FRESH-PG-EVIDENCE-V1`, and `EP-F57-CANDIDATE-BOUND-FRESH-PG-RECEIPT-REF-V1`. Ownership is exact: the CapabilityGraph schema solely owns `CapabilityGraphPurposeV1`; runtime-topology solely owns `RuntimeTopologyDeclarationPurposeV1|RuntimeTopologyCertificationPurposeV1`; client-common solely owns `SignedArtifactRefPurposeV1`; `docs/evidence/f57-fresh-pg-evidence.schema.json` solely owns `FreshPgEvidencePurposeV1` and its signed payload; and foundation solely owns `CandidateBoundFreshPgReceiptRefPurposeV1` plus its plain ref. Exact runtime-topology media are `application/vnd.ep.f57-runtime-topology-declaration-v1+json` and `application/vnd.ep.f57-runtime-topology-certification-v1+json`; `docs/evidence/f57-runtime-topology.v1.schema.json` is sole owner only of those declaration/certification purposes and types. Both are strict plain JCS values stored by digest in `EvidenceObjectStoreV1`: declaration integrity is reached through the signed candidate, and certification integrity is reached through the signed release certificate, so neither invents a signer-registry row. G0 solely defines the two wires/schema plus a deterministic declaration builder and strict live-readback verifier; the G0 gate emits no deployment-specific declaration because no verified F57 storage manifest exists yet. After G1-01 verifies the signed authority storage manifest and DATA_HDD root, it first produces the exact signed generation under the generation/migration approval trust domain and then is the sole first-stage caller of the topology builder: it supplies the complete compiled graph, the verified signed generation selected for later G1-05 activation, the verified storage-manifest ref and the non-expiring P340 policy-definition ref, then create-new stores the declaration in `EvidenceObjectStoreV1`. Under the generation-transition lock, G1-05 exact-loads that ref/bytes and passes the runtime-owned sealed `RuntimeTopologyReadbackCollectorV1` to `TopologyVerifier::verify_declaration`; that call alone captures the fresh complete live readback, constructs private `VerifiedRuntimeTopologyDeclarationV1`, and exact-matches graph/generation/storage/policy before activation. No caller-built `ActualRuntimeReadbackV1`, stale wrapper or pre-lock readback crosses the coordinator boundary. The declaration deliberately contains no current candidate, soak or capacity-certificate ref. Its three private profile IDs accept only generated registry members; the current exact members are `THINKSTATION_P340_I5_10500_32GB_256GB_SSD_1TB_HDD`, `SINGLE_DISK_DEGRADED_PRODUCTION`, and `F57_P340_15_3_2_1__11_5_2_2_V1`. The release candidate binds only `runtime_topology_declaration_ref`. After the candidate-bound P340 carrier is terminal PASS and before POWER/Final L2, G6 alone produces `RuntimeTopologyCertificationV1` by typed-loading that declaration, the same candidate, the one P340 soak and its reachable `P340CapacityCertificateV1`; every profile, host, `20`-user capacity and `259200`-second interval must exact-match. The release certificate binds `runtime_topology_certification_ref`, and its expiry minimum includes the P340 soak/capacity certificate. Production activation requires the verified release certificate plus that certification and exact live topology readback; declaration-only activation is forbidden, while pre-release G1–G5 readiness may compare actual state only to the declaration. The mandatory one-way order is `G0 generation/topology contracts -> G1 verified storage manifest -> signed generation -> declaration -> G1 generation activation/ACK -> candidate -> P340 certification -> release certificate -> production activation`; an early generation/declaration, current-candidate capacity ref in the declaration, certification before P340, wrong profile/host/capacity, generic media or ref substitution fails closed. The dedicated plain typed Fresh-PG reference may point only to a verified signed `CandidateBoundFreshPgEvidenceV1` with media type `application/vnd.ep.f57-candidate-bound-fresh-pg-evidence-v1+json`; it exact-repeats candidate run, profile and through-version. It never binds the later outer signed-candidate digest, which would be circular; a generic artifact ref or a separately signed reference wrapper cannot substitute for it. `CompiledCapabilityGraphV1` never embeds generated files: compile retains `client_lifecycle_fixture_trust_roots`, `client_lifecycle_fixture_sources`, and the flattened canonical `semantic_contracts` vector byte-for-byte as validated typed values, and `project_all` derives a separate deterministic `Vec<ProjectionArtifactV1>` only from those compiled typed fields, including manifest-owned multi-member families; it never reparses `canonical_json`, rereads a Markdown table, or reads ambient fixture bytes. It retains the complete `GeneratorIdentityV1`, not just its display version, so every projection can bind the generator binary and graph-schema digests without rereading ambient state. Bootstrap compile has `activation_profile=None`, `activation_eligible=false`, and no active capability; profile-scoped activation fills the active/disabled partitions under the same digest. `RuntimeParticipantV1` is strict and includes participant/service identity, binary digest, carrier, Windows Service SID, IPC endpoint and DACL digest, dependency exact-set, readiness probes, resource/queue class and allowed persistence class. `DatabaseConsumerV1` includes identity, role, purpose, connection privilege class, steady/peak pool bounds, timeout and budget contribution; declaration verification compares every field to readback, and production activation repeats that comparison under the certification. `FieldIdV1` has no public raw-string constructor: only the active CapabilityGraph resolver can create it after exact object/field authorization lookup.

`IAAS_WINDOWS_SERVER_HDD_STRICT` is intentionally absent from the current three-member P340 topology registries and from current release acceptance. Enabling it requires a new graph/profile version and a provider-specific certification family with independent typed declaration, capacity, storage-media attestation, key-boundary, backup/restore, network-isolation, host/VM lifecycle and disaster-replacement evidence. The verifier must branch by profile before loading any hardware evidence, reject cross-profile refs and require every IaaS authority-data root to prove the signed HDD-backed storage contract; a provider that cannot make that property auditable cannot satisfy this product's HDD rule. No “same Windows Server” inference, copied P340 threshold or cloud snapshot alone can activate IaaS production.

The G6 topology-certification production path is exact. A private release-layer `RuntimeTopologyCertificationAuthorityV1`—not the G0 topology crate—consumes the verified final candidate, its exact declaration ref/bytes, the terminal same-run P340 result/soak and reachable capacity certificate, plus a fresh live readback. Only after those inputs exact-match may it call G0's pure certification builder, create-new store and typed-reload the strict JCS bytes, and return private non-wire `VerifiedRuntimeTopologyCertificationV1`. The G0 crate imports no release/P340 type and its pure builder cannot assert terminal-gate authority. The release-certificate constructor accepts only that verified wrapper/ref. Task 15 must execute this step after P340 PASS and before POWER/Final L2; pre-P340 construction, wrong candidate/run/declaration/storage/policy/profile/host/20-user/259200-second binding, stale live readback, partial/conflicting bytes, directory discovery or a second write fails closed.

The CapabilityGraph wire is closed by `docs/schemas/f57-capability-graph.v1.schema.json`, generated deterministically from the exact `deny_unknown_fields` Rust types above and golden-tested byte-for-byte. Root values are exactly `schema_version=1`, `graph_id="f57-core"`, and initially `graph_version=1`; later graph versions are strictly monotonic positive integers. `CapabilityIdV1` uses lowercase dot-separated segments matching `[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*`, which admits the frozen binding `f57.req.gov-001`; `GraphSymbolV1` deliberately remains narrower at `[a-z][a-z0-9_]*`. Both total 3–160 UTF-8 bytes. Schema names, evidence IDs, platform lanes, state values, objective kinds and obligation IDs must use their dedicated newtypes above; trigger, closure, effect, policy, compensation and workflow identifiers use their non-interchangeable uppercase-token newtypes and cannot be substituted merely because their strings are equal. Golden vectors include `ControlHumanEffectDecisionRequestV1`, `E-F57-GOV-001`, `windows-authority`, `ACCEPTED`, `CONTRACT_FULFILMENT`, `PURCHASE_AP_CLOSED`, `PROCUREMENT_DEMAND_READY`, `PROCUREMENT_QUANTITY_AND_OBLIGATION_COVERAGE_V1` and `PROCUREMENT_LEAD_TIME_V1`. `ErrorCodeV1` is 3–96 bytes of uppercase dot-separated segments, each `[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*`, so `PLATFORM.AUTHORITY.STALE_EPOCH` is valid; bare `NONE` is reserved and rejected except through `ImportedOperationErrorCodeV1` in the one historical discriminator column. `Sha256Digest` has private 32-byte storage, accepts and serializes exactly one 64-character lowercase hexadecimal JSON string, and rejects uppercase, prefix, whitespace, wrong length, number array or noncanonical encoding. `GeneratorIdentityV1` fixes `schema_version=1`, requires canonical SemVer 2.0 without build metadata, and binds both generator binary and graph-schema SHA-256. `CapabilityOwnerRefV1` is adjacently tagged as `owner_kind=FEATURE|PLATFORM` plus `owner_id`; `CapabilityKindV1` uses `kind=REQUIREMENT_BINDING|FEATURE_CAPABILITY|PLATFORM_MECHANISM|SLICE_PROBE|DEFERRED_BOUNDARY`; Requirement bindings carry only `schedule`, while SliceProbe carries both `schedule` and the exact `contract`. `CapabilitySemanticsV1` uses `semantics_kind=BOOTSTRAP_IMPORTED|ACTIVATION_READY` plus `details`; and `ImportedContractRowV1` uses `row_kind=API_DISCRIMINATOR|API_COMPONENT_SHAPE|API_COMPONENT_STATE_DOMAIN|API_STATE_DOMAIN|API_DIRECT_ROUTE` plus `row`. All other enum wires are their uppercase snake-case variant names unless this plan states another exact wire. Every array is canonical-sorted by its declared primary ID, duplicate-free, and set-like except lifecycle transitions, which sort by `(from,to,action_id,guard_ids,invariant_ids)`. `semantic_contracts` sort by `contract_id`; their projection targets sort by enum ordinal. `CapabilityCarrierKindV1` describes exposure/execution capability in the graph; `RuntimeCarrierV1` describes a concrete deployed participant. Neither is accepted where the other is required. A raw string capability/dependency ID, unknown JSON field/enum, noncanonical order, imported-and-ready field mixture, schema digest drift, or Rust/JSON-Schema golden-vector difference fails before compilation.

`semantic_contracts` closes the former expressiveness gap without creating a second truth or a generation cycle. The authored CapabilityGraph is the sole machine input: its root owns canonical `semantic_table_anchors` and `semantic_row_schemas`, while each `ActivationReady` node owns its typed `SemanticContractBindingV1` rows. A `CONTRACT_TABLE` provenance is legal for the eight non-workflow contract kinds only. Its `anchor_id` must resolve exactly once to a graph anchor whose `contract_kind` and `row_schema_id` equal the binding. `SemanticTableKeyV1` is lowercase ASCII `[a-z][a-z0-9_]{2,127}` and identifies exactly one marker pair in one registered document: `<!-- F57-SEMANTIC-TABLE:<table_key>:BEGIN -->` and the matching `:END`. The hashed table preimage is the exact UTF-8/LF bytes strictly between the two marker lines, beginning with the header `|` and including the final LF after the last row; blank/intervening prose, nested marker, duplicate marker, CRLF, BOM or a non-table line is invalid. The strict row parser treats only an unescaped `|` as a column delimiter and decodes `\|` to one literal pipe inside a cell; header width, delimiter width and every row width must be identical, and an unsupported escape or unterminated code span fails. Before graph bytes are accepted, the G0 authoring preflight exact-loads only that registered `document_path + table_key`, verifies this preimage against `table_sha256`, exact-matches every header/index/codec against the schema's `source_table_layout`, invokes the one contract-kind validator, canonicalizes its normalized typed rows, and exact-compares those rows with the authored binding. The compiler remains pure and performs no repository I/O: it validates the already-bound anchor identity/digest and typed rows, so a moved, edited, header-relabelled, codec-incompatible or unregistered table fails the authoring preflight while Markdown can never become a runtime fallback.

The current six contract-table adapters are frozen below. Header arrays are exact UTF-8 strings in physical column order; codec arrays have the same cardinality and order. A row decoder may emit only the stated normalized key/payload. It may never retain an unparsed policy/workflow/state rule as ordinary `UTF8`, invent a column alias or infer a mapping from `SemanticRowSchemaV1.fields` order.

| table key / contract kind | exact source headers | exact codecs | validator and normalized result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `objective_trigger_closure_registry_v1` / `OBJECTIVE_TRIGGER_CLOSURE_REGISTRY` | `ObjectiveKind`; `trigger_kinds exact-set`; `closure_rule_id`; `reopen_trigger_kinds exact-set`; `timeout_policy_id`; `termination_policy_id` | `OBJECTIVE_KIND`; `TRIGGER_KIND_SET`; `CLOSURE_RULE`; `TRIGGER_KIND_SET_OR_EMPTY`; `TIMEOUT_POLICY`; `TERMINATION_POLICY` | `OBJECTIVE_TRIGGER_CLOSURE_REGISTRY_V1`; key=`ObjectiveKindV1`, fields=`trigger_kind_ids,closure_rule_id,reopen_trigger_kind_ids,timeout_policy_id,termination_policy_id` |
| `objective_execution_registry_v1` / `OBJECTIVE_EXECUTION_REGISTRY` | `ObjectiveKind`; `obligations exact-set`; `responsibility capability`; `permitted typed effect intents`; `evidence exact-set` | `OBJECTIVE_KIND`; `OBLIGATION_SET`; `CAPABILITY`; `EFFECT_INTENT_SET`; `SCHEMA_REF_SET` | `OBJECTIVE_EXECUTION_REGISTRY_V1`; key=`ObjectiveKindV1`, fields=`obligation_ids,responsibility_capability_id,permitted_effect_intent_ids,evidence_schemas`; the CamelCase evidence cells are strict `SchemaRefV1`, never delivery `EvidenceIdV1` |
| `timeout_policy_registry_v1` / `TIMEOUT_POLICY_REGISTRY` | `timeout_policy_id`; ``canonical `TimeoutPolicyDefinitionV1` JSON`` | `TIMEOUT_POLICY`; `INLINE_CODE_CANONICAL_JCS_OBJECT` | `TIMEOUT_POLICY_REGISTRY_V1`; key=`TimeoutPolicyIdV1`, one `definition` field=`CANONICAL_JCS_OBJECT(TimeoutPolicyDefinitionV1)` |
| `termination_policy_registry_v1` / `TERMINATION_POLICY_REGISTRY` | `termination_policy_id`; `reason_codes exact-set`; `capability`; `decision_mode`; `guard_id` | `TERMINATION_POLICY`; `UPPER_TOKEN_SET_OR_EMPTY`; `CAPABILITY`; `UPPER_TOKEN`; `UPPER_TOKEN` | `TERMINATION_POLICY_REGISTRY_V1`; key=`TerminationPolicyIdV1`, typed fields=`reason_codes,capability,decision_mode,guard_id` |
| `compensation_command_registry_v1` / `COMPENSATION_COMMAND_REGISTRY` | `ObjectiveKind`; `compensation_commands exact-set` | `OBJECTIVE_KIND`; `COMPENSATION_COMMAND_SET` | `COMPENSATION_COMMAND_REGISTRY_V1`; key=`ObjectiveKindV1`, field=`compensation_command_ids` |
| `business_state_domain_registry_v1` / `STATE_INVARIANT_REGISTRY` | `StateDomain`; `语义种类与初态`; `允许边或唯一派生规则`; `终态` | `MARKDOWN_CODE_UPPER_TOKEN`; `UTF8_EXACT`; `UTF8_EXACT`; `UTF8_EXACT` | `STATE_INVARIANT_REGISTRY_V1`; the versioned decoder consumes the complete four-cell tuple and emits key=`SemanticTokenV1` plus one `definition=CANONICAL_JCS_OBJECT(StateDomainDefinitionV1)` containing typed mode, initial/output states, transitions or precedence clauses, guard/invariant IDs, terminal states and reverse-fact triggers.
