The 14 emitted objects are byte-golden; prose strings are never the compiled payload. |

For all future `CONTRACT_TABLE` bindings, an amendment must add an equally exact adapter row before use. `SemanticSourceTableLayoutV1.columns` is sorted by contiguous zero-based `column_index`, covers the source header exactly once, and has no ignored/display-only column. Its codec vector and `SemanticContractValidatorIdV1` are closed generated registries with a one-to-one validator↔`SemanticContractKindV1` mapping. The adapter's normalized row set, not the intermediate source cells, enters the graph. `CanonicalJcsObjectUtf8V1` accepts only a JSON object whose exact UTF-8 bytes already equal its RFC 8785 JCS, whose `value_schema` equals the field schema's non-null `canonical_jcs_value_schema`, and which passes that strict schema plus the selected validator. Every structured object's own identity (`policy_id`, `domain_id` or `workflow_id`) must byte-equal its enclosing typed row key; duplicating one object under another key is invalid. This is the only legal representation for nested timeout parameters, state definitions and graph-native workflow step/compensation graphs.

`GRAPH_NATIVE` provenance is legal only for `WORKFLOW_DEFINITION_REGISTRY` and only with `authoring_rule_id=f57.workflow_definition.graph_native.v1`. Its row schema has `validator_id=WORKFLOW_DEFINITION_REGISTRY_V1`, `source_table_layout=None`, row key `WorkflowDefinitionIdV1`, and one required `definition=CANONICAL_JCS_OBJECT(WorkflowDefinitionV1)` field; the strict object includes the complete typed step graph and compensation graph rather than an opaque string. Those workflow rows are authored directly in the CapabilityGraph under business contract §8.4 and are the sole workflow-definition machine authority; no Markdown workflow table, generated file, database row or handwritten Rust registry may substitute. Every activation-due ObjectiveKind references at least one graph-native workflow definition, and every referenced definition is content-bound and generation-pinned. A different contract kind using `GRAPH_NATIVE`, a workflow binding using `CONTRACT_TABLE`, an unknown authoring rule, a non-null source layout or a workflow definition encoded as `UTF8` fails compilation.

Every `SemanticRowSchemaV1` has `schema_version=1`, a unique canonical `schema_id`, one exact `contract_kind`, the exact one-to-one validator for that kind, one `row_key_kind`, provenance-compatible source layout and canonical unique fields sorted by `field_id`. For every row, `row_key.scalar_kind` must equal `row_key_kind`; row keys are unique and rows sort by RFC 8785 JCS bytes of `row_key`. Fields are unique and sorted by `field_id`; unknown fields are forbidden, all `required=true` fields are present, and an absent optional field has no synthetic value. `NULL` is legal only when the declared field is nullable. Every non-null scalar/set/ordered-list exact-matches the declared shape and nominal `scalar_kind`; sets are duplicate-free and sort by each scalar's JCS bytes, while ordered lists preserve authored order. `CANONICAL_DECIMAL` accepts only the single canonical base-10 text form frozen by the generated graph schema. `canonical_jcs_value_schema` is `Some` exactly for a scalar `CANONICAL_JCS_OBJECT` field and `None` otherwise; the value repeats and exact-matches that schema. A `reference_contract_kind` is legal only on a nominal reference scalar and every present value exact-resolves once in that kind. These checks occur before any graph digest is issued.

For each binding, `projection_path` is exactly `docs/generated/f57/semantic-contracts/<contract-id>.v1.json`; `exact_row_count` equals `rows.len()`; owner equals the containing node owner; projection targets are nonempty, canonical and unique. `projection_sha256` is SHA-256 of RFC 8785 JCS for the strict five-field `SemanticContractProjectionV1 {schema_version=1,contract_id,contract_kind,row_schema_id,rows}` and never a Markdown/table/file digest. The compiler reconstructs that payload, exact-checks path, digest, schema, count, provenance and all references, then flattens the complete unique set by `contract_id` into `CompiledCapabilityGraphV1.semantic_contracts`. `project_all` writes those identical payload bytes as members and generates the separate strict `SemanticContractsManifestV1` primary. The direction is therefore `registered authoring source -> authored graph -> pure compile -> projections`; a projection is never input to an earlier step.

State, authorization and Objective summaries are typed indexes, not parallel truth. A state machine's `semantic_contract_id` resolves exactly once to `STATE_INVARIANT_REGISTRY`. Each authorization row's `authorization_contract_id` resolves to `AUTHORIZATION_RULE_REGISTRY`; `query_use_id`, `candidate_query_schema` and `candidate_query_contract_id` are either all absent or all present, and the latter resolves to `CANDIDATE_QUERY_REGISTRY`. Each Objective has six separate non-interchangeable contract IDs resolving respectively to trigger/closure, execution, timeout, termination, compensation and workflow registries; every summarized trigger, obligation, closure, reopen, effect, timeout, termination, compensation and workflow ID exact-matches its bound row. Objective definitions plus the trigger/closure, execution and compensation registries each have exactly the UTF-8-byte-sorted `F57_BUSINESS_OBJECTIVE_KIND_V1_EXACT` row-key set—not merely 15 rows. The timeout and termination registries are deliberately keyed by their dedicated policy IDs: their complete row-key sets must respectively equal the distinct `timeout_policy_id` and `termination_policy_id` values referenced by the exact trigger/closure rows, with no missing, extra or unreferenced policy. Workflow rows are keyed by globally unique `WorkflowDefinitionIdV1`; their normalized `definition.objective_kind` coverage set equals `F57_BUSINESS_OBJECTIVE_KIND_V1_EXACT`, every kind has at least one definition, and every Objective summary ID resolves within the definitions for that same kind. OpenAPI, clients, ClosureRegistry, workflow runtime and tests consume projections of those rows. Missing/extra ObjectiveKind, missing/extra policy key, wrong workflow-kind membership, wrong nominal type, wrong contract kind, duplicate/orphan binding, schema/count/digest/owner drift, unresolved reference or summary disagreement fails compilation before output.

`CapabilityPackageArtifactV1 = SignedBusinessArtifactV1<CapabilityPackagePayloadV1>` is the only reusable signed package wire. Its strict payload has exactly thirteen fields `{schema_version=1,purpose,package_id,package_version,component_class,capability_subgraph_ref,implementation_manifest_ref,permission_ceiling,required_host_capabilities,migration_plan_ref,compatibility,data_retention_contract,hotplug_contract}`; purpose/media are `EP-F57-CAPABILITY-PACKAGE-V1` / `application/vnd.ep.f57-capability-package-v1+json`. The eight-field plain `CapabilityPackageImplementationManifestV1` is reached only through `implementation_manifest_ref`, uses purpose/media `EP-F57-CAPABILITY-PACKAGE-IMPLEMENTATION-MANIFEST-V1` / `application/vnd.ep.f57-capability-package-implementation-manifest-v1+json`, and is package-owned strict JCS. Its canonical nonempty `artifacts` vector and top-level SBOM close every native binary byte, schema/WIT/entrypoint, Authenticode readback, OCI signature bundle, migration bundle and foundation artifact ref; `implementation_set_sha256=SHA256(JCS(artifacts))`. The component-class-to-implementation-variant matrix is exact: `CONFIGURATION|UI|REPORT|RULE|WORKFLOW|MCP_CONFIGURATION -> DECLARATIVE_BUNDLE`; `WASM_EXTENSION -> WASM_MODULE`; `JOB_OBJECT_WORKER|CONNECTOR|AI_OCR_PROVIDER|RUST_KERNEL -> WINDOWS_NATIVE_BINARY`; `HYPER_V_CONTAINER -> HYPER_V_CONTAINER_IMAGE`; `POSTGRESQL_DATABASE_MIGRATION -> DATABASE_MIGRATION_BUNDLE`; and `CRYPTOGRAPHY_FOUNDATION|STORAGE_FOUNDATION -> FOUNDATION_ARTIFACT_SET`. `WindowsNativeBinary.abi_readback_ref` is mandatory with exact `AuthorityKernelAbiReadbackV1` media only for `RUST_KERNEL` and null for every other native class, so the signed package store can reconstruct all four code-slot files. No executor may stage bytes outside those typed refs. The three foundation classes require `migration_plan_required=true`, nonnull package `migration_plan_ref`, the exact implementation-contained migration/foundation plan and the generation-approval migration signer; no caller SQL, path or command is representable.

`PermissionCeilingV1` is imported one-to-one from the Task-4/ADR-0023 sole owners `crates/platform/provider/src/permission.rs` and `docs/schemas/f57-provider-permission.v1.schema.json`; package defines no look-alike. CapabilityGraph solely owns the closed 15-wire `CapabilityPackageComponentClassV1`, host-capability ID registry and canonical `capability_package_slot_templates` vector of strict ten-field `CapabilityPackageGraphSlotV1`, sorted by `slot_id`; the compiler preserves that vector byte-exact in `CompiledCapabilityGraphV1`. A slot contains only static `scope_mode`. At runtime the upper authority joins the current `platform.tenancy`-owned strict `TenancyAuthoritySnapshotV1` to produce the concrete tagged `CapabilityPackageScopeV1`, including tenancy/key-domain generation and, for deployment scope, the canonical complete impacted-legal-entity exact set and digest. Package repeats component class and the slot-bound subgraph/permission/host-capability/migration/retention facts, all of which exact-match their graph values or JCS digests. Package locally owns only the displayed compatibility, retention, hotplug and implementation-manifest types; platform version bounds are canonical SemVer with `minimum < maximum_exclusive`, host capabilities and namespaces are canonical unique, `legal_hold_precedence=true`, and retention mode is only `RETAIN_ON_DISABLE_ROLLBACK_AND_LICENSE_LOSS`. `ATOMIC_GENERATION_SWAP` requires a complete nonempty post-switch probe set. `DRAIN_AND_REPLACE` requires positive `drain_timeout_ms`, exact `COMPLETE_IN_PLACE|DURABLE_HANDOFF` and a complete nonempty post-switch probe set. `MAINTENANCE_UPGRADE` carries no deployment-specific plan ref; it requires exact `SIGNED_MAINTENANCE_PLAN_REQUIRED`, `maximum_approved_window_ms` in `1..=86400000`, `VERIFIED_RECOVERY_CHECKPOINT_REQUIRED`, and exactly five complete nonempty canonical action probe vectors. Keeping per-attempt authorization outside the reusable package and desired item avoids customer-window re-signing and every package↔plan or generation↔attempt hash cycle.

`docs/evidence/f57-capability-package.v1.schema.json` and `crates/platform/package/src/manifest.rs` are the sole schema/Rust owners for the thirteen-field package payload, eight-field implementation manifest, hotplug family, strict 30-field maintenance plan, strict nine-field plain desired-state `CapabilityPackageGenerationItemV1`, strict sixteen-field plain authorization decision, reservation, authorization scope, execution-trust snapshot, execution authorization, per-attempt generation transition, operation request/result and installed-state readback. Every plain root has its displayed `EP-F57-*` purpose and the mechanically derived lower-case vendor media `application/vnd.ep.f57-<artifact-name>-v1+json`; schema and Rust media registries are byte-golden, so an unregistered or ambiguous media fails. The Task-7 schema direct-imports only then-existing foundation, generation, capability-graph and provider-permission owners, composes the signed envelope exactly once for each of its two signed roots, and never envelops a plain operational readback. Backup checkpoint/cut, tenancy snapshot and production hold remain media-constrained `ArtifactRefV1` fields in the lower package schema; Task 14's upper verifier imports their sole owners, typed-loads them and exact-joins the bindings without a lower package→backup/tenancy dependency. `docs/evidence/f57-package-recovery-control.v1.schema.json` and recovery-tool own the separately recovery-domain-signed `SignedAuthorityKernelSlotPointerV1` plus authenticated `PackageRecoveryContinuationCapsuleV1`; they are not package-trust signed roots. The generation item is authenticated by the signed generation; the post-sign transition and operation/readback closure is authenticated by the participant apply-readback ref carried in the server ACK and, after production, by `ProductionGenerationAdmissionV1`. `docs/schemas/f57-capability-package-trust-registry.v1.schema.json` and `crates/platform/package/src/trust.rs` solely own the seven-field signed registry, exact media `application/vnd.ep.f57-capability-package-trust-registry-v1+json`, and six-field rows. Rows are canonical unique, wildcard-free and `CURRENT_AT_VERIFICATION`; at least one package row is mandatory, and any graph containing a maintenance-grade slot also requires at least one current `CUSTOMER_MAINTENANCE_AUTHORITY` row. Package artifacts accept only product/approved-customer package authorities; plans accept only a customer maintenance authority. Package, maintenance-plan and registry `CmsSignableArtifactV1` implementations are emitted only into `crates/platform/package/src/generated_cms_artifacts.rs` and registered by package `lib.rs`; foundation's generated registry owns stable descriptors/type IDs only and never implements a foreign package type. One generator atomically regenerates both sides, and freshness/dependency tests reject a handwritten impl or package↔foundation cycle.

The package registry has no undefined roster bootstrap. The verified storage manifest contains exactly one `capability-package-trust-registry-sha256:<64-lowerhex>` pin and exactly one `capability-package-trust-registry-signer-spki-sha256:<64-lowerhex>` pin. Registry CMS verification uses the same already authenticated `AuthorityStorageTrustBootstrapV1` chain/revocation/checkpoint closure, requires its leaf SPKI to equal the second pin and leaf DN exactly `CN=EP F57 Capability Package Trust Registry Authority,O=Enterprise Platform`, and then requires the envelope digest to equal the first pin, deployment to match and revision/current window to be valid. The fixed bootstrap source is only `<data_root>\packages\trust\capability-package-trust-registry.v1.json`; after verification it is create-new copied/fsynced/reloaded through the authority-generation `EvidenceInputStoreV1` at portable `evidence-relative://bundle/inputs/<whole-envelope-sha256>.json`. Every package generation item carries that exact portable ref, so final freeze and the offline walker find the registry without a scan.

Every trust-domain change is serialized by that one G1-owned global `AuthorityStorageManifestRotationCoordinatorV1`, never by an independent generation or package writer. The displayed `AuthorityStorageManifestRotationRecordV1|DomainChangeV1|EventV1` definitions are the normative Rust/JSON wire; exact media is `application/vnd.ep.f57-authority-storage-manifest-rotation-v1+json`. Both domain variants have the same eleven explicitly typed fields but remain separate tags so cross-domain substitution cannot deserialize. On initial install all three old-registry option fields are null, `old_signer_pins=[]`, and its digest is `SHA256(JCS([]))`; on rotation all three are nonnull, old pins are canonical nonempty and exact-match the base manifest/current registry. New revision is positive and exactly old+1 when old exists; new pins are nonempty canonical unique, both pin-set digests recompute over JCS vectors, and registry envelope digests equal their refs. `portable_registry_ref` must resolve the byte-identical new envelope at the authority input locator and never the fixed active path.

Every record repeats one immutable rotation tuple. `sequence` is exactly `0..3`; sequence zero has null predecessor and later rows carry `SHA256(JCS(the complete immediately prior record))`. `staged_fixed_path_refs` is the canonical exact two-row set of immutable new registry-revision bytes and resulting storage-manifest-revision bytes; resulting revision is checked `base+1`, and both manifest digests equal whole signed-envelope refs. `trust_domain` must equal the domain-change tag. The generation event chain is exactly `GENERATION_TRUST_ROTATION_STARTED -> STORAGE_MANIFEST_BOUND -> REGISTRY_PROJECTED -> ROTATION_COMMITTED`; the package chain differs only at `PACKAGE_TRUST_ROTATION_STARTED`. Event payload refs must be members of the frozen staged set and the projected fixed-path ID is the sole domain-specific active locator. No failed event rewrites the chain: a failure leaves the last valid prefix held for exact recovery. Record codecs deny unknown fields and hash canonical JCS bytes, not a partial/event-only projection. A single global lock/CAS advances the monotonic storage-manifest revision across every trust domain; stale bases, cross-domain concurrent wins, independent manifest writes and partial/conflicting pairs fail closed, while crash recovery adopts the same immutable bytes. Cross-domain crash goldens interleave generation/package requests before and after every frame and prove exactly one winner followed by a clean rebase, with no forked storage-manifest revision. Package provisioning is idempotent through a private `CapabilityPackageTrustProviderV1` with exactly two adapters—self-hosted nonexportable Windows KSP/PIV/TPM-backed handles or an approved existing enterprise signer—and the same durable signing-operation query/adopt rule. Registry-bootstrap, package, customer-maintenance and recovery-bootstrap roles have pairwise-disjoint fixed SPKI/container/ACL/DN values; one key or certificate cannot occupy two roles. Ambient roots, adjacent/newest files, self-roots, vendor maintenance signers and cross-kind reuse fail. None of the three package-domain signed payloads enters the 89-row candidate-evidence registry.

Every `GenerationItemRefV1{item_kind=CAPABILITY_PACKAGE}` points to the strict nine-field plain desired-state object `{schema_version,purpose,item_id,package_id,desired_package_ref,desired_package_version,desired_lifecycle_state,package_trust_registry_ref,scope}`. It never carries a one-use plan, decision, checkpoint, window or activation attempt. A generation reverse plan therefore restores a prior pure desired-state item—or uses `DEACTIVATE_RETAIN_DATA` for a newly introduced item—without reviving expired authority. `CapabilityPackageGenerationTransitionV1` is the separate post-sign, per-activation-attempt operational edge. It exact-binds source/target desired-item refs, action and, only for maintenance, reservation/plan/execution-authorization/checkpoint/admission-hold refs. It is create-new stored before the first package mutation and becomes reachable through the package participant's typed apply readback and the ACK's `participant_apply_readback_ref`, avoiding both a generation hash cycle and unauthenticated offline discovery.

`VERIFY_UNCHANGED` is universal and is not a maintenance action: source and target desired-item refs, package/version/state and scope are byte-identical; all maintenance refs and operation IDs are null; a fresh typed installed-state readback alone permits `TUPLE_BOUND -> APPLIED_VERIFIED`. Mutation edges are exact: `INSTALL=(ABSENT/null -> INSTALLED_DISABLED/target)`, `ENABLE=(INSTALLED_DISABLED/same package -> ENABLED/same package)`, `DISABLE=(ENABLED/same package -> INSTALLED_DISABLED/same package)`, `UPGRADE=(same lifecycle in INSTALLED_DISABLED|ENABLED, nonnull source -> same lifecycle, distinct higher target)` and `ROLLBACK=(same lifecycle in INSTALLED_DISABLED|ENABLED, nonnull source -> same lifecycle, distinct lower target)`. There is no uninstall/delete action. The eleven ordinary classes through `AI_OCR_PROVIDER` allow all five mutations. `RUST_KERNEL|POSTGRESQL_DATABASE_MIGRATION|CRYPTOGRAPHY_FOUNDATION|STORAGE_FOUNDATION` allow production runtime only `UPGRADE|ROLLBACK`; their initial install is the signed release/recovery bootstrap. `INSTALL|ENABLE|UPGRADE|ROLLBACK` probes come from the target contract; `DISABLE` probes come from the source; upgrade/rollback caps use the checked minimum of source, target and deployment caps. Installed-state nullability is closed: `ABSENT` requires package/version/implementation/subgraph/permission/retention/pin fields all null, one nonnull typed absence readback, empty runtime identities and `admission_open=false`; `INSTALLED_DISABLED|ENABLED` require those artifact fields all nonnull, absence null and exact package/implementation equality. Disabled requires closed admission, retained data and pinned rollback bytes; enabled requires open admission only after the matching production admission plus complete runtime identities/probes.

The graph slot's `scope_mode` is authoritative. All four global classes require concrete `DEPLOYMENT` scope, the complete current impacted-legal-entity exact set, and deployment-level dual control; ordinary classes may use `LEGAL_ENTITY` or `DEPLOYMENT` only as declared by the slot. Desired item, reservation, plan, decision, execution authorization, transition, checkpoint, installed-state readback, SQL projection and production admission must exact-match the same tagged scope. For atomic/drain mutations, plan/authorization/checkpoint/hold refs are null. For maintenance mutations they are all nonnull, but the actual checkpoint and execution authorization are created only after admission hold and the write barrier as defined below.

The 30-field signed plan binds the graph-derived reservation, concrete scope, positive epoch/generation, participant/item, action, graph-derived executor/rollback strategy, package identity, complete source/target state tuple, approved initial window, `recovery_checkpoint_policy_ref`, action-selected probes, two principals, exactly two initial typed decision refs, minimum authorization deadline and issue/expiry. It never binds an actual checkpoint created before drain. Initial decision refs are ordered exactly `[INITIATOR,APPROVER]`; each sixteen-field object is create-new materialized only from a private current `VerifiedSecurityContextV1`, fixes `ALLOW`, matching capability, MFA/reauth times and deadline, and is historical evidence for signing the plan. Every decision, initial or later, computes `decision_scope_sha256 = SHA256(JCS(CapabilityPackageMaintenanceAuthorizationScopeV1))`. That complete scope includes all immutable reservation/plan/source/target/scope/action/executor/probe/policy facts plus the current two principals, window/times and positive `authorization_ordinal`; decision refs themselves are excluded to avoid a cycle. Initial plan authorization uses ordinal `1`. Both principals are distinct current humans with current MFA/reauthentication, SoD and exact `f57.package.maintenance.initiate|approve` capabilities. Checked time rules remain `issued < expires`, trusted CMS/RFC3161 time in `[issued,min(issued+300000,expires,authorization_not_after)]`, and `issued <= window_not_before < window_not_after <= min(expires,authorization_not_after)`.

Plan authoring is a graph-to-package-to-generation handshake, not caller-proposed identity. Under the generation transition lease, the upper generation authority derives a complete `CapabilityPackageMaintenanceReservationV1` from the compiled static slot, current tenancy snapshot, current OBSERVED predecessor, action and next generation; it allocates unpredictable reservation/finalization/plan/signing IDs and a positive `reservation_attempt_ordinal`. Only the production composition adapter may pass that reservation, two private security contexts, fresh sealed source-state readback and typed source/target packages into the plan authority. The plan authority constructs the ordinal-1 authorization scope and both decisions, samples trusted times once, durably freezes the complete reservation, source readback, registry/packages, decisions and unsigned plan before creating an object, then create-new materializes/adopts the decisions and signs/adopts the plan. It returns a verified structural plan binding to the reservation projection; the independently created nine-field desired-state item remains reusable and contains no short-lived authorization.

`PackageMaintenancePlanFinalizationStoreV1` is the sole plan-authoring journal. Its DATA_HDD root is `<validated-data-root>\packages\maintenance-plan-attempts\<deployment-id>\<20-digit-epoch>\<20-digit-generation>\<item-id>\<plan-id>\`; it owns only `attempt.v1.jcs.jsonl` and `spool\maintenance-plan.signed.v1.json`. Strict records have `{schema_version,purpose=EP-F57-CAPABILITY-PACKAGE-MAINTENANCE-PLAN-FINALIZATION-RECORD-V1,finalization_attempt_id,sequence,previous_record_sha256,recorded_at_unix_ms,event}` and success path `INPUTS_FROZEN -> DECISIONS_STORED -> SIGNING_AUTHORIZATION_COMMITTED -> PROVIDER_COMMITTED -> PLAN_STORED -> PLAN_BOUND`. Sequence zero embeds the complete `PackageMaintenancePlanFrozenInputsV1`: full reservation, source readback, registry/source/target refs, both exact decisions and unsigned 30-field plan containing checkpoint policy—not an actual checkpoint. It freezes tuple/payload digests and every repeated value byte-exact; only afterward may decisions and CMS be created/adopted. The journal is an operational crash-recovery structure and is deliberately not part of the final offline certificate bundle.

Authorization binds descriptor/window/authorization digests; provider commit is queried/adopted by the same operation ID. `PLAN_STORED` binds the create-new spool/object ref and `PLAN_BOUND{reservation_ref,plan_ref}` binds only the historical structural plan to the current reservation row; it does not require a still-current execution window. After `SIGNING_AUTHORIZATION_COMMITTED`, `EXPIRED_UNBOUND` is legal only if provider query proves uncommitted. Valid committed CMS bytes are always adopted/stored and may be bound later because their trusted historical signing time is fixed; `UNKNOWN` stays unresolved without resend. Frames use `len8<TAB>JCS<LF>`, contiguous sequence/hash, OS-exclusive lease and fsync of file/parent. Every durable recovery uses only its self-contained prefix and fixed object locators, never resampling, scanning or requesting caller inputs.

`platform_meta.package_maintenance_reservations` is the fixed current projection keyed by `(deployment_id,authority_epoch,generation_number,item_id)`. Its exact columns are `{deployment_id,authority_epoch,generation_number,item_id,scope_jcs,current_reservation_attempt_ordinal,reservation_id,finalization_attempt_id,reservation_ref_jcs,plan_id,plan_ref_jcs,admission_hold_ref_jcs,write_barrier_id,execution_authorization_ordinal,execution_authorization_ref_jcs,state,forward_intent_committed,cas_version,row_sha256,created_at_unix_ms,updated_at_unix_ms}`; state is exactly `RESERVED|PLAN_BOUND|EXECUTION_AUTHORIZED|FORWARD_INTENT_COMMITTED|SUPERSEDED_UNEXECUTED|TERMINAL`. `row_sha256` covers every displayed column except itself, and serializable CAS plus the positive ordinals are the sole lookup/recovery authority. Before any external forward intent, an expired live authorization may keep the same pure desired item and historical plan, increment only `execution_authorization_ordinal`, and create fresh decisions plus execution authorization. Once `forward_intent_committed=true`, no reauthorization or new forward operation is legal; only query/adopt, measure and coordinator-authorized rollback may proceed.

The production-admission hold store is keyed by `(deployment_id,hold_id)` with a unique live-overlap exclusion over canonical scope; it is never keyed by a package reservation. Every immutable record prefix repeats the byte-identical tagged `cause`, scope and admitted predecessor and follows only the cause-specific graph and nullability frozen beside `ProductionAdmissionHoldV1`. Package-maintenance projection stores its current hold ref and barrier ID; current-roots rotation, disaster-replacement and UPS-loss authorities store the same hold ref under their exact successor tuple, recovery attempt or runtime-loss episode respectively, so boot recovery uses the typed cause reference and never scans or guesses a reason. Every step is create-new/CAS under the common deployment lock. A crash after closing routes resumes the same hold; UNKNOWN, missing or cross-cause proof remains closed, and no new hold or request lease may overlap its scope.

Maintenance execution is two-phase and lossless. First, the historical signed plan plus current deployment-level or entity-level dual control authorizes a scoped `ADMISSION_HELD`; the production-admission authority closes the exact routes, drains all accepted work and persists a full `write_barrier_id`. Second, Task 11 freezes `AuthorityRecoveryCutManifestV1` at that barrier and returns `VerifiedBackupCheckpointV1` binding the same reservation, checkpoint policy and full cut. Only then may the upper authority create `CapabilityPackageMaintenanceExecutionAuthorizationV1` from a fresh source-state readback, current decisions, current `CapabilityPackageExecutionTrustSnapshotV1`, hold, checkpoint and recovery-cut manifest; create-new store/reload the transition and commit the first privileged intent. This prevents writes between checkpoint and switch. Plan CMS time proves historical validity; execution authorization time and ordinal prove live authority.

Before the first package mutation, `CapabilityPackageMaintenanceVerifierV1` exact-matches reservation, scope, deployment/epoch/generation/participant/item/action/source/target/probes/executor/rollback, checkpoint policy, actual post-barrier checkpoint, complete recovery-cut manifest, hold, source readback, current execution-trust snapshot and current decision scope. Atomic and drain also freeze a `CapabilityPackageExecutionTrustSnapshotV1` in the same CAS as their first external intent, with null plan. Later registry rotation/revocation/expiry cannot authorize a new forward operation for any grade, but the frozen snapshot remains historical authority for the same named operation's query/adopt, measurement and reverse path. No path rebuilds a current wrapper to repeat an effect.

Package code never starts rollback. A failed/UNKNOWN forward apply returns that measured outcome to the upper coordinator. The coordinator first durably appends its existing `ROLLBACK_STARTED{rollback_execution_attempt_id}`, derives the exact reverse subset and only then dispatches release-owned private `VerifiedGenerationParticipantRollbackRequestV1`. The package handler binds that rollback ID and executes only under this request. `ARTIFACT_STATE_RESTORE` applies the reverse plan's prior desired-state item through the package protocol of the installed broker. `RECOVERY_CHECKPOINT_RESTORE` sends the exact checkpoint/cut/operation ID to the recovery-domain worker, which alone restores and returns a fresh typed predecessor-state proof. A newly introduced item's `DEACTIVATE_RETAIN_DATA` removes admission/code activation but retains all data/evidence. Its rollback item readback is the tagged `DEACTIVATED_RETAIN_DATA` variant: it has no fictitious predecessor item, names the rolled-back forward item and transition, and points to an `ABSENT` installed-state readback with nonnull absence/retained-data proof. Apply readbacks accept only `DESIRED_ITEM`; rollback readbacks accept `DESIRED_ITEM` for a real predecessor or `DEACTIVATED_RETAIN_DATA` for a new item. The canonical set digest includes each variant tag and every displayed field. No forward handler, timeout or local health result can synthesize a rollback attempt.

A foundation restore may roll PostgreSQL back across its own generation/package rollback rows, so recovery never trusts restored SQL as the continuation authority. Before restore, the recovery worker freezes `SignedPackageRecoveryContinuationCapsuleV1` outside the restore set at fixed runtime-SSD path `C:\ProgramData\EnterprisePlatform\continuation-control\package-maintenance\<rollback-id>\`, mirrored by the off-host target and protected by the recovery-domain CMS plus TPM/off-host monotonic head. The capsule contains no business data and binds generation/activation/item/reservation/plan/execution authorization/checkpoint/full recovery cut, rollback/restore operation IDs, pre-restore row hashes, the tagged `RESTORED_ARTIFACT|DEACTIVATED_RETAIN_DATA` predecessor target and a content-addressed `PackageRecoveryTerminalResealPayloadV1`. That payload contains the exact canonical terminal package/generation projections, expected restored hashes, terminal activation prefix, verified rollback request/result and predecessor readback refs; `terminal_projection_set_sha256` covers the complete set. Its exact chain is `CAPSULE_FROZEN -> RESTORE_INTENT_COMMITTED -> RESTORE_PROVIDER_COMMITTED -> RESTORE_VERIFIED -> SQL_STATE_RESEALED -> CAPSULE_RETIRED`; every frame is independently recovery-signed, create-new, predecessor-linked and query/adopted. Each transition writes/fsyncs the new capsule frame, then appends/fsyncs its signed operation-journal row, then advances the typed TPM/off-host head; recovery query/adopts only the same `(deployment,epoch,restore_operation_id,capsule_id)` tuple. `CAPSULE_RETIRED` frame, journal row, head and authenticated HDD/off-host mirrors all become durable before the SSD operation directory is deleted. On boot all business admission remains held while the recovery reconciler verifies the signed capsule/journal/head before restored SQL, typed-reloads the reseal payload and external completion/readback, exact-matches the restored hashes, then performs one idempotent expected-restored→terminal CAS for both projections. Hashes validate; they are never used as missing reconstruction data. The reconciler never reconstructs or replays a forward operation.

The package-recovery-control owner freezes four concrete contracts that the SSD policy may name. `PACKAGE_RECOVERY_CONTINUATION_CAPSULE_FRAME_V1` is exactly the existing signed capsule envelope—no wrapper—with payload purpose `EP-F57-PACKAGE-RECOVERY-CONTINUATION-CAPSULE-V1` and media `application/vnd.ep.f57-package-recovery-continuation-capsule-frame-v1+json`. The six filenames use sequences `00000000000000000000..00000000000000000005` in the displayed state order; frame zero has null predecessor, later `previous_capsule_sha256` hashes the complete prior signed-envelope file bytes, and the immutable twenty-field identity tuple repeats. `PACKAGE_RECOVERY_OPERATION_JOURNAL_V1` has purpose/media `EP-F57-PACKAGE-RECOVERY-OPERATION-JOURNAL-V1` / `application/vnd.ep.f57-package-recovery-operation-journal-v1+jsonl`; it contains exactly six signed records with sequence `0..5`, the common `<8 lowercase hex length>\t<exact JCS signed-envelope>\n` framing, state/time/tuple equality to the named capsule, `capsule_frame_sha256` over that complete capsule file, null prior-record hash only at zero and otherwise SHA-256 of the complete preceding framed journal record. The external monotonic-head purpose/media are `EP-F57-PACKAGE-RECOVERY-EXTERNAL-MONOTONIC-HEAD-V1` / `application/vnd.ep.f57-package-recovery-external-monotonic-head-v1+json`; its two terminal digests bind the complete latest journal frame and capsule frame. It lives only in TPM NV/DATA_HDD/off-host authorities and adds no SSD path class.

`AUTHORITY_KERNEL_SLOT_HEAD_V1` has purpose/media `EP-F57-AUTHORITY-KERNEL-SLOT-HEAD-V1` / `application/vnd.ep.f57-authority-kernel-slot-head-v1+jsonl` and uses the same framed signed-record codec, but `slot-head.v1.jcs.jsonl` contains exactly one current signed frame; immutable predecessor heads live on DATA_HDD/off-host. Ordinal one is `BOOTSTRAP_BUILD` with null previous pointer/head; a later ordinal is prior+1, has both predecessor fields and exact-matches its binding/kernel/time to the new pointer. Construction is `head -> pointer -> WindowsAuthorityArtifactSet`: `AuthorityKernelSlotPointerV1.recovery_journal_head_ref` typed-loads that immutable one-frame head, its digest is the ref's digest, and the fixed SSD head bytes must be byte-identical. The head never refers to the new pointer, so there is no cycle.

`AUTHORITY_KERNEL_ABI_READBACK_V1` has purpose/media `EP-F57-AUTHORITY-KERNEL-ABI-READBACK-V1` / `application/vnd.ep.f57-authority-kernel-abi-readback-v1+json`. It is strict plain JCS authenticated by the signed pointer/head/artifact-set or later package implementation ref. Exact offsets are `[0,4,8,16,24,32,40]`; the function-RVA set is the six-row set: `GetApi` plus the five callback functions, nonzero/in-module, and the section set is seven rows in enum order. The API table section is readable, nonwritable and nonexecutable; every function section is readable/executable and nonwritable. Export, ABI and size are exactly `ep_authority_kernel_get_api_v1`, `1`, `48`; `module_sha256` hashes reopened PE file bytes, never relocated memory. `docs/evidence/f57-package-recovery-control.v1.schema.json` solely owns all four roots and composes the foundation signed envelope once per signed record; JSONL framing/cardinality/hash chains are codec/golden obligations. Release imports it once and never reverse-defines these names.

All recovery-signed capsule/journal/head/pointer bytes verify against one exact recovery-bootstrap trust role: leaf DN `CN=EP F57 Recovery Bootstrap Authority,O=Enterprise Platform`, storage-manifest pins `recovery-bootstrap-signer-spki-sha256:<64-lowerhex>` and the current chain/revocation/checkpoint, and local container identity `EP-F57-RECOVERY-BOOTSTRAP-V1`. The supported signing adapters are a self-hosted nonexportable PIV or TPM persistent handle, or an approved enterprise signer; both implement durable `(signing_operation_id,authorization_digest)->byte-identical CMS` query/adopt. A software CNG private-key container whose unique bytes live on the runtime SSD is unsupported. This role is disjoint from package, maintenance, evidence, backup-checkpoint and local broker-authorization keys. Verification remains offline from pinned public material after SSD loss; ambient roots, newest-file selection, role reuse or non-idempotent signing fail closed.

`AuthorityRecoveryCutManifestV1` is the sole strict fourteen-field ransomware/foundation recovery boundary, not a PostgreSQL-plus-attachments shortcut. Its canonical row exact-set equals every enabled authority-data class/root in the signed storage manifest, including PostgreSQL/base/WAL, attachments, audit, Outbox, generation/package trust and execution state, vault, identity/authz/tenancy, admission holds/tombstones, flow/automation state and every other enabled DATA_HDD authority class. The cut header carries the exact private request's `BackupSetIdV1`, `BackupCheckpointContextV1` and common `write_barrier_id`; each row exact-binds authority class/root identity, that barrier, immutable source ref/digest/size and complete off-host target-receipt refs. After the immutable cut is stored and before draft construction, the backup authority uses the narrow safeguard collector to obtain a new `BACKUP_CHECKPOINT_PREPARATION` readback bound to the exact cut, backup set, context, prior head and sequence. `BackupCheckpointDraftPayloadV1` and signed `BackupCheckpointPayloadV1` both carry that readback ref, the same backup set/context/barrier, the previous-checkpoint option, checkpoint sequence and the cut/storage-manifest refs and digests; the checkpoint signer re-loads and exact-verifies the entire relation. Each of the three clean-hardware recovery runs restores and exact-verifies every row from one common cut; missing, extra, duplicate, cross-backup-set, cross-context, cross-barrier, stale-safeguard, chain-fork or cross-cut data fails, even if PostgreSQL alone starts.

`crates/platform/backup/src/topology_signing_trust.rs`, `crates/platform/backup/src/safeguard.rs` and their three Task-11 strict schemas solely own five anti-ransomware roots. Signed `BackupTopologySigningTrustManifestV1` has purpose/media `EP-F57-BACKUP-TOPOLOGY-SIGNING-TRUST-MANIFEST-V1` / `application/vnd.ep.f57-backup-topology-signing-trust-manifest-v1+json`; signed `BackupTopologySigningTrustCurrentPointerV1` has `EP-F57-BACKUP-TOPOLOGY-SIGNING-TRUST-CURRENT-POINTER-V1` / `application/vnd.ep.f57-backup-topology-signing-trust-current-pointer-v1+json`; signed `BackupTopologyV1` has `EP-F57-BACKUP-TOPOLOGY-V1` / `application/vnd.ep.f57-backup-topology-v1+json`; strict plain `StorageSafeguardReadbackV1` has `EP-F57-STORAGE-SAFEGUARD-READBACK-V1` / `application/vnd.ep.f57-storage-safeguard-readback-v1+json`; and closed `StorageSafeguardSupportEvidenceV1` has `EP-F57-STORAGE-SAFEGUARD-SUPPORT-EVIDENCE-V1` / `application/vnd.ep.f57-storage-safeguard-support-evidence-v1+json`. Every signed envelope uses the one strict JCS/detached-CMS verifier; every support signature is strict RFC-4648 padded CMS over the exact JCS bytes of `{schema_version,purpose,payload}`, re-encodes byte-identically, and its vector is strictly sorted and unique by `(signer_principal_id,signer_spki)`. A `TARGET_RECEIPT` has exactly one signature: `signer_principal_id` byte-equals the current topology's `role_bindings[BACKUP_TARGET_AGENT].principal_id` rather than the literal role wire, `signer_spki` byte-equals `continuous_target.target_server_spki`, and `SHA256(JCS(signer_spki))` byte-equals that role binding's `credential_identity_sha256`. Either offline branch has exactly the two topology-pinned human custodian signatures. These five roots add no candidate-evidence signer row.

Currentness is explicit, independent and acyclic. The deployment bootstrap pins exactly one trust-manifest authority DN `CN=EP F57 Backup Topology Trust Manifest Authority,O=Enterprise Platform`, one SPKI and its offline verification policy; only that authority can sign the trust manifest and current pointer. The trusted monotonic active configuration carries `backup_topology_signing_trust_current_ref` and `backup_topology_ref`; both must byte-equal the supplied envelopes, so no caller, directory scan, filename, timestamp or merely still-valid older object selects either. Pointer and manifest genesis are each generation 1 with null predecessor; every successor generation is checked prior+1, names the exact immutable prior signed-envelope ref, retains deployment identity, never decreases authority epoch, has strictly later issue time and cannot fork or overflow. The current pointer typed-loads exactly one manifest with the same positive `trust_generation`, deployment and valid time window. That manifest fixes the topology signer to the literal DN `CN=EP F57 Backup Topology Authority,O=Enterprise Platform`, exactly one leaf `SignerSpkiTokenV1`, and exact typed offline certificate-chain, revocation-snapshot and transparency-checkpoint refs. `BackupTopologyAuthorityV1` has no public raw-wrapper constructor and can be composed only from private `VerifiedBackupTopologySigningTrustCurrentV1`; it verifies a topology only against that current manifest, never against fields in the topology, storage manifest, support evidence, candidate signer rows, ambient Windows roots, `ApplicationRecoveryDomainManifestPayloadV1`, its ADR-0020 `PIV_SHAMIR_2_OF_3_V1` recipient roster, `BackupRecoveryDomainManifestPayloadV1`, or any backup-key-envelope share roster. Verification checks exact CMS content, current offline chain/revocation/checkpoint, `issued_at_unix_ms < expires_at_unix_ms`, trusted `now` inside the inclusive validity window, certificate validity, and CMS signing time inside both certificate validity and `[issued_at_unix_ms,min(issued_at_unix_ms+300000,expires_at_unix_ms)]`. Each topology exact-repeats the current pointer ref, its manifest ref and trust generation. Topology genesis is `revision=1` with null predecessor; a successor is create-new with revision prior+1, exact prior signed-envelope ref, same deployment, nondecreasing authority epoch/generation and strictly later issue time. `authority_storage_manifest_ref` byte-equals the current trusted `F57AuthorityStorageManifestV1`; deployment and authority epoch exact-match, topology generation exact-matches the current signed generation, `backup_target_ids` is exactly `[continuous_target.target_id]`, and `policy_ids` contains exactly one `backup-topology-signing-trust-current-sha256:<64-lowerhex>` entry whose suffix is the current pointer envelope digest. A rotation reuses the already verified current trust tuple or, when topology-signer trust changes, first writes and independently verifies the successor trust manifest/pointer; it then writes and verifies a storage-manifest successor when storage or its trust pin changes and always writes a topology successor referencing the resulting current tuple; one serialized active-config CAS advances the pointer/topology/storage tuple and opens the typed `CURRENT_ROOTS_ROTATION` transition below. This ordering creates no self-authentication or content-addressed cycle. Missing/expired/untrusted material, wrong DN/SPKI/media/purpose, pointer/manifest generation or predecessor error, fork, time rollback, trust/root substitution, epoch/generation rollback, manifest/target/policy-pin mismatch, stale config or old-topology substitution fails closed.

Canonical topology vectors have one representation: `role_bindings` contains exactly the six `BackupRoleV1` values in enum order with unique principal and credential identities; `offline_media` is exactly `[ROTATION_A,ROTATION_B]`. `BACKUP_WRITER.credential_identity_sha256=SHA256(JCS(continuous_target.writer_client_spki))` and `BACKUP_TARGET_AGENT.credential_identity_sha256=SHA256(JCS(continuous_target.target_server_spki))`; observed writer/target SPKIs and every target-receipt signer exact-join those values. One off-host continuous HDD target and both offline HDD rows exact-declare host/media, failure, administration, credential, custody and physical-location domains. Let the protected entity set be exactly `E={PRODUCTION,CONTINUOUS,ROTATION_A,ROTATION_B}` and the domain set exactly `D={FAILURE,ADMINISTRATION,CREDENTIAL,CUSTODY,LOCATION}`. Every topology and fresh support readback carries one nonempty domain ID for every `(entity,domain)` pair; for each `d in D` and every unordered distinct pair `{x,y} subset E`, the verifier directly proves `domain(d,x) != domain(d,y)`. That is five groups of six, exactly 30 pairwise inequalities. A `shared_*=false` summary, “different device” Boolean, different display name or different path is never source evidence. Same tenant/root/management group, reused SPKI/secret/recovery credential, common host/rack/room/power failure boundary, overlapping custody roster or same physical location is a required negative and blocks production. Across A/B, each pair of `media_id`, `hardware_serial_sha256`, `volume_identity`, `volume_guid`, and live `volume.physical_disk_identity_sha256` is additionally nonempty and unequal; each live row's role/media ID/hardware serial/volume identity/volume GUID byte-equals its topology row, so two volumes on one physical HDD cannot satisfy A/B. Continuous and production live domain rows, plus offline live domain rows, byte-equal their topology rows and come from topology-pinned signed support receipt/observation projections. Each media row has exactly two `custodian_bindings`, strictly sorted by principal ID, distinct in principal/SPKI/administration domain, disjoint from every six-role principal/credential/administration domain, and current because the selected topology is current; the live vector byte-equals it. Zero, one, duplicate, three, unsorted or stale-topology custodians fail.

Every `capacity_calculation_input_ref|quota_exhaustion_probe_ref|emergency_reserve_probe_ref|partial_timeout_probe_ref|expired_partial_cleanup_probe_ref|bulk_work_suspension_readback_ref|retention_policy_readback_ref|just_written_create_receipt_ref|just_written_exact_readback_ref` typed-loads the exact corresponding `TARGET_RECEIPT` kind; every permission row's `denial_receipt_ref` typed-loads `PERMISSION_DENIAL`. Each repeats topology/target/nonce/session/probe, has `subject_projection_sha256=SHA256(JCS(the schema-defined complete containing-field projection))`, and exact-matches before/after/outcome/times. Offline `state_transition_ref` typed-loads `OFFLINE_MEDIA_TRANSITION`; `safe_eject_readback_ref|physical_disconnection_attestation_ref|custody_record_ref|health_readback_ref` typed-load the matching `OFFLINE_MEDIA_OBSERVATION` kind and exact-bind topology/media/current transition/state/nonce/session and the complete containing-row projection. Wrong kind/media/signer/ref or field substitution fails offline verification.

The offline transition chain is deterministic. Sequence 1 has null predecessor/previous state and enters `BLANK`; every successor is prior+1, names the exact prior evidence ref, has `previous_state=prior.current_state`, and uses only the eight edges `BLANK->ENROLLED`, `ENROLLED->ACTIVE_APPEND`, `ACTIVE_APPEND->VERIFIED_DISCONNECTED`, `VERIFIED_DISCONNECTED->ROTATION_DUE`, `ROTATION_DUE->ACTIVE_APPEND`, `ACTIVE_APPEND->SEALED_VERIFIED`, `SEALED_VERIFIED->RETIRED_PENDING_DISPOSAL`, and `RETIRED_PENDING_DISPOSAL->DESTROYED`. `SEALED_VERIFIED` can never return to a writable state and `DESTROYED` is terminal; reuse of destroyed physical media requires a new `media_id` and a new sequence-1 `BLANK` chain. Live `transition_sequence` byte-equals the head payload sequence, `state_transition_ref` is that head, and `transition_chain_head_sha256` equals the ref's complete-object SHA-256. Gap, fork, illegal edge, state mismatch, ID reuse or hash substitution fails.

Every install, checkpoint preparation, PITR, activation and every retry uses a new unpredictable 32-byte/64-lowerhex nonce, new authenticated session binding, new support receipts/observations and current boot/attempt; reuse fails even for the same activation ID or checkpoint set. `maximum_safeguard_readback_age_seconds` is checked nonzero and at most 300. Top-level expiry checked-equals `observed_at_unix_ms + maximum_safeguard_readback_age_seconds*1000` without overflow, every live support object is valid through that expiry, the topology remains the selected current head through it, and a consumer verifies trusted `observed_at <= now <= expires_at`. Every consumer typed-loads `backup_topology_ref` as the signed current `BackupTopologyV1`, requires `StorageSafeguardReadbackV1.topology_signing_trust_current_ref` to exact-equal the topology field and active-config current pointer, typed-loads that pointer plus its independent current trust manifest into private `VerifiedBackupTopologySigningTrustCurrentV1`, and verifies the topology signer only through that value, typed-loads the exact current `F57AuthorityStorageManifestV1` and every support-evidence ref, and reconstructs the checkpoint chain rather than trusting repeated scalar fields. `latest_backup_checkpoint_ref` is respectively the service-install binding's explicit expected option, the checkpoint-preparation binding's `expected_prior_backup_checkpoint_ref`, `Some(Postgres16Pitr.backup_checkpoint_ref)`, or `Some(ProductionActivation.certified_latest_backup_checkpoint_ref)`; activation's value also equals the certificate/recovery chain's certified latest current checkpoint. Inference from a “newest” storage object is forbidden. `AuthorityRecoveryCutManifestV1.backup_topology_ref` exact-loads this same topology throughout target receipts, checkpoint, PITR and activation, and its storage-manifest ref/digest, deployment, epoch, generation, backup set, context and barrier exact-join the checkpoint request, draft and payload.

Checkpoint bootstrap and chaining are total rather than circular. `protection_transition` is not a caller-supplied explanation: the sole authority projects one immutable transition object from the monotonic active configuration, and later readbacks repeat it byte-for-byte rather than mutating a stored “next sequence.” `HEALTHY` requires it to be `None`; `INITIALIZING|BOOTSTRAPPING|TRANSITIONING` require `Some` with the exact current transition ID/generation/targets, while `NON_SUPPRESSIBLE_RISK` preserves that `Some` iff an active transition exists but never grants an operation. A clean `WindowsServiceInstall` with `expected_latest_backup_checkpoint_ref=None` still verifies the independent current trust pointer/manifest, current topology, singleton-target storage manifest, fresh support evidence and every permission/capacity/lifecycle invariant. It requires top-level latest/head/continuous/A/B vectors all empty and `INITIALIZING + INITIAL_POPULATION`: all five prior/anchor fields are `None` and all three target refs equal the active current tuple. This can PASS infrastructure installation but never PITR, release, recovery certification or production activation. `BackupCheckpointPreparation` is collected only after the immutable recovery-cut manifest exists and before draft construction; its binding exact-repeats backup set, positive sequence, context, barrier, cut ref and expected prior head. Draft and signed payload byte-repeat those values and the exact fresh safeguard ref. The sole first-checkpoint exception accepts that exact `INITIALIZING` shape, derives sequence 1 from the empty chain, fixes prior `None`, and creates a checkpoint under the current trust/topology/storage tuple. Thereafter a fresh readback becomes `BOOTSTRAPPING + INITIAL_POPULATION` with the identical immutable transition object and a nonempty current chain. `BOOTSTRAPPING + INITIAL_POPULATION` authorizes another checkpoint only while the distinct continuous and A/B-union sequence counts are still below `minimum_retained_generation_count`, both A and B are already nonempty verified subsets, their union includes the current head, every other `HEALTHY` invariant passes, and the requested sequence is the checked current-head sequence plus one with prior equal to that head. Thus with the required minimum of two, checkpoint 1 is first copied and verified into both A/B, checkpoint 2 can then be made, and its verified offline copy closes the minimum; larger configured minima iterate the same derived-head rule without changing the transition object. As soon as the complete healthy formula is true, the next fresh readback must be `HEALTHY` with `protection_transition=None`; remaining in `BOOTSTRAPPING` is invalid. No readback is required to contain the not-yet-created checkpoint, avoiding a reference cycle.

Every checkpoint ref is typed-loaded as `BackupCheckpointV1`: deployment is constant; historical topology/storage/trust/recovery-domain refs are retained and must be fully verified ancestors on their respective predecessor chains; epoch, release generation and config generation never decrease; and `backup_set_id` is nonnil and unique. Continuous refs are strictly sorted and unique by `(checkpoint_sequence,uri,sha256)`, begin at sequence 1, increment exactly one, and every predecessor is the immediately prior ref; head equals the last row or is `None` iff empty, and top-level latest byte-equals head. In `HEALTHY|BOOTSTRAPPING`, the head exact-binds the current topology, storage manifest and topology-signing current pointer. The sole old-head exception is a serialized current-root rotation begun from a fresh `HEALTHY` readback. Before any active-config CAS, the upper admission authority must create one deployment-wide `ProductionAdmissionHoldV1{cause=CURRENT_ROOTS_ROTATION{target_backup_topology_ref,target_authority_storage_manifest_ref,target_topology_signing_trust_current_ref}}`, close new request and long-running-job admission, drain every accepted execution lease, and durably commit one `write_barrier_id`; the transition, cut and bridge all exact-bind that same hold/cause/barrier. Only after independently verifying the successor trust manifest/pointer, storage manifest and topology may one active-config CAS advance that tuple and open one immutable `CURRENT_ROOTS_ROTATION` with a new transition ID/generation; its five prior/anchor fields are all `Some` and exact-load the prior healthy readback, old head, old topology, old storage manifest and old trust pointer, while its three target refs byte-equal the hold cause's new tuple. A fresh readback is then `TRANSITIONING`. It permits exactly one bridge checkpoint whose sequence is derived as checked `anchored_old_head.sequence+1`, whose previous ref is that anchor and whose cut, draft, payload and safeguard bind the new active tuple plus the same hold/barrier; response loss adopts the same signing operation and cannot create a second bridge. Once that checkpoint is signed, `TRANSITIONING` is illegal: the next readback is `BOOTSTRAPPING + CURRENT_ROOTS_ROTATION` while the new head awaits required offline verification, and that state authorizes no additional checkpoint—only exact A/B copy/verification can advance it to `HEALTHY/None`. The hold remains active for the entire `TRANSITIONING|BOOTSTRAPPING` interval and no local router or old lease can bypass it. Reopening requires one admission CAS that observes fresh `HEALTHY`, `protection_transition=None`, a head exact-bound to the new tuple, the current authority epoch/OBSERVED generation and zero pre-barrier leases, then appends `REOPENED` for that same tagged cause. A second topology, storage or trust rotation is rejected until that CAS; no caller may reset the transition ID/generation or substitute a different anchor/target. In `HEALTHY`, continuous and both A/B vectors are nonempty; each offline vector is a strictly sequence-sorted unique subset with support evidence verified through that media/custodian chain, their union includes latest, and both continuous and A/B-union distinct counts meet the minimum. Only a shortage of retained generations during `INITIAL_POPULATION`, or a pending exact offline copy after the bridge, with all trust, chain, permission, capacity, lifecycle and freshness checks passing is a bootstrap deficiency. Any malformed transition, wrong current/ancestor relation, gap/fork, stale or duplicate head/set/sequence, failed security/resource probe, one-sided media, transition collision or state that should already be healthy yields `NON_SUPPRESSIBLE_RISK` and authorizes no checkpoint. `INITIALIZING|BOOTSTRAPPING|TRANSITIONING|NON_SUPPRESSIBLE_RISK` are categorically ineligible for ordinary PITR, release/recovery certification and production activation; those consumers accept only a fresh explicit `HEALTHY` head and never a valid ancestor or inferred newest object.

Dead-disk takeover is a different, closed protocol rather than an impossible special case of normal rotation. `DATA_HDD_DISASTER_REPLACEMENT` does not require the failed old disk to emit a fresh `HEALTHY` readback and never discovers a local “latest” file. Its only inputs are the server-external current configuration/trust roots and the last certified checkpoint plus complete recovery cut. Two distinct recovery custodians authorize one immutable recovery attempt; the authority then establishes the deployment-wide `ProductionAdmissionHoldV1{cause=DATA_HDD_DISASTER_REPLACEMENT{recovery_attempt_ref}}`, whose cause exact-loads that attempt, fences the old authority/disk, checked-increments `authority_epoch` and storage generation, provisions a different physical disk/volume GUID/volume identity with GPT/NTFS and the exact BitLocker protector policy, signs/verifies a successor storage manifest, and performs clean restore plus PostgreSQL PITR and complete reconciliation of every authority-data class in the cut. On the new tuple, continuous backup and both A/B chains bootstrap from the explicit empty state to fresh `HEALTHY`; the current first-release carrier then repeats P340 capacity/durability certification. A future graph-versioned IaaS profile must substitute its own independent disaster-replacement and carrier recertification branch and cannot reuse this P340 terminal. This one recovery-authorized PITR is legal only while admission remains held and does not grant ordinary PITR to `NON_SUPPRESSIBLE_RISK`. The sole takeover point is the final admission CAS after fencing, full reconciliation, safeguard health and P340 recertification; that CAS appends `REOPENED` for the same recovery-attempt cause, and every earlier cut keeps business routes closed. Crash goldens cover every boundary and adopt only the same recovery attempt/IDs/bytes.

All capacity arithmetic is performed in checked `u128` and rejected unless representable as `u64`. Continuous `resources.quota_policy` byte-equals the topology policy; all four quota maxima and the partial timeout are nonzero. `required_total_capacity_bytes` equals retained ciphertext + restore-validation workspace + 30-day growth + emergency reserve; physical total is at least required total, free is at least validation + growth + reserve, `maximum_stored_bytes + reserve <= total`, `used_object_count <= maximum_object_count`, `used_bytes <= maximum_stored_bytes`, `observed_ingress_bytes_per_second <= maximum_ingress_bytes_per_second`, `active_upload_count <= maximum_concurrent_uploads`, and `reserve <= emergency_reserve_free_bytes <= free`. The four `*_limit_enforced` values are all true and are not trusted alone: `quota_exhaustion_probe_ref` is the signed `QUOTA_EXHAUSTION` target receipt whose schema-defined projection exact-binds this policy, these live counters and four isolated boundary probes; each dimension accepts a checked in-policy request, denies the first checked out-of-policy request, leaves completed/pinned history unchanged and leaves no partial probe object. Each offline required total equals recoverable set + validation workspace + growth; physical total is at least it and free is at least validation + growth. Expired partial count/bytes are zero; active count zero iff active bytes zero and oldest age is `None`, while positive count requires positive bytes and `Some(age < partial_object_timeout_seconds)`. Completed/pinned history is unchanged and exhaustion suspends bulk work. Every volume is GPT/NTFS/HDD/BitLocker software XTS-AES-256/100%; continuous protectors are exactly `{PUBLIC_KEY,RECOVERY_PASSWORD}`, offline exactly `{RECOVERY_PASSWORD}`. Retention checked-equals `max(site_legal,7776000,2*detection_lag_p99+clean_restore_validation_window,2*rotation_interval)`, offline age is at most 604800 seconds, retained generations at least two, and `bundle_contains_recovery_material=false` for both A/B in every binding and any PITR leaf.

`permission_negative_probes` is the exact vector sorted by `(actor_role,operation)`: writer denies history enumeration/read/re-read, overwrite/delete/rename, ACL/ownership, retention/quota/reserve and partial cleanup; target-agent denies **every** `BackupPermissionProbeOperationV1` direct/unbound operation (normal append is only the private capability path below); partial-maintenance denies cleanup of non-expired/completed/pinned objects; retention-custodian denies shortening/create/restore; checkpoint-signer denies create/enumerate/content-read/delete; recovery-custodian denies source-retention mutation/source-delete. Every row's signed target receipt exact-matches actor/operation/probe and unchanged before/after digest. Production A/B must be `VERIFIED_DISCONNECTED|SEALED_VERIFIED`, zero-attached at authority and target, authorization revoked, safely ejected, physically disconnected, healthy and dual-custodied under the current transition. Any unknown, stale, incomplete, insufficient-capacity, shared/mismatched-domain or probe failure yields `NON_SUPPRESSIBLE_RISK`. `AppendOnlySinkV1` exposes only authenticated append, a private affine just-written capability consumed by exactly one exact-object verification read, and seal; response-loss adoption returns the persisted signed receipt without a second content read, and no list/history/rename/delete/ACL/retention API exists. Schema/crash goldens cover every support kind/ref substitution, signer/quorum/custodian mutation, topology rollback/fork, A/B media/serial/volume/physical-disk alias, every illegal lifecycle edge or destroyed-ID reuse, all four quota boundaries/flags, domain/SPKI mismatch, arithmetic overflow/shortfall, partial optionality, recovery-material bit and permission row.

The compiler applies one closed minimum-grade/executor/rollback table to the graph-owned component class. Minimum grades are `CONFIGURATION|UI|REPORT|RULE|WORKFLOW|MCP_CONFIGURATION -> ATOMIC_GENERATION_SWAP`, `WASM_EXTENSION|JOB_OBJECT_WORKER|HYPER_V_CONTAINER|CONNECTOR|AI_OCR_PROVIDER -> DRAIN_AND_REPLACE`, and `RUST_KERNEL|POSTGRESQL_DATABASE_MIGRATION|CRYPTOGRAPHY_FOUNDATION|STORAGE_FOUNDATION -> MAINTENANCE_UPGRADE`. If the selected grade is elevated to maintenance, the complete executor table is: every class through `AI_OCR_PROVIDER -> WINDOWS_CONTROL_BROKER/ARTIFACT_STATE_RESTORE`; `RUST_KERNEL -> RECOVERY_TOOL/ARTIFACT_STATE_RESTORE`; and the three foundation classes -> `RECOVERY_TOOL/RECOVERY_CHECKPOINT_RESTORE`. A signed package may request a stronger grade but never a weaker one, and its component class must equal the slot.

The executor/strategy pair deterministically selects one closed forward/compensation operation pair: broker artifact restore uses `PACKAGE_ARTIFACT_STATE_SWITCH/PACKAGE_ARTIFACT_STATE_RESTORE`; recovery-tool artifact restore uses `PACKAGE_RUNTIME_SLOT_SWITCH/PACKAGE_RUNTIME_SLOT_RESTORE`; recovery-tool checkpoint restore uses `PACKAGE_FOUNDATION_MAINTENANCE_APPLY/PACKAGE_RECOVERY_CHECKPOINT_RESTORE`. The package handler only authorizes, dispatches and measures; it has no SCM/self-update/database-restore/key/storage mutation primitive. The already permanent `EPAuthorityControl` service exposes two discriminated protocols over its fixed authenticated pipe: the existing POWER protocol and a package protocol accepting only the first pair from `EPAuthorityServer` under a distinct capability. The same exact 18-object SDDL model is retained by treating the existing control-operation root as tagged `POWER|PACKAGE` subroots; no new broad ACE appears, POWER remains unable to issue package operations, and package requests cannot invoke shutdown, continuation or signer operations. Static manifest, Task-10/14/15 goldens and dynamic challenge tests exact-freeze both allowlists.

`RECOVERY_TOOL` remains a non-SCM, on-demand component but is not an ambient administrator executable. Task 11 registers exactly one task at `\EnterprisePlatform\F57\RecoveryToolV1`. The static build row carries a principal **policy**, never a deployment-specific numeric SID: `DEDICATED_LOCAL_S4U`, local account name `EPF57Recovery`, logon `S4U`, and run level `LEAST_PRIVILEGE`. Assigned account rights sort exactly `[SeBackupPrivilege,SeBatchLogonRight,SeChangeNotifyPrivilege,SeManageVolumePrivilege,SeRestorePrivilege]`; Task Scheduler `<RequiredPrivileges>` sorts exactly `[SeBackupPrivilege,SeChangeNotifyPrivilege,SeManageVolumePrivilege,SeRestorePrivilege]` and never contains the logon right. Denied rights sort exactly `[SeDenyInteractiveLogonRight,SeDenyNetworkLogonRight,SeDenyRemoteInteractiveLogonRight,SeDenyServiceLogonRight]`. Direct local-group membership is exactly `[S-1-5-32-545]` (Users); prohibited effective group SIDs sort exactly `[S-1-5-32-544,S-1-5-32-547,S-1-5-32-548,S-1-5-32-549,S-1-5-32-550,S-1-5-32-551,S-1-5-32-555,S-1-5-32-556,S-1-5-32-569,S-1-5-32-578,S-1-5-32-580,S-1-5-32-582,S-1-5-32-583]`. Ordinary implicit token groups such as Everyone/Authenticated Users are not falsely declared absent; live readback requires the prohibited-group intersection empty. The installer creates or exact-adopts that dedicated local account, resolves its numeric SID once, grants only the listed account rights and file/key ACLs, and freezes account enabled, required and exact allowed user-flags mask `0x00010240=UF_NORMAL_ACCOUNT|UF_DONT_EXPIRE_PASSWD|UF_PASSWD_CANT_CHANGE`, forbidden diagnostic mask `0x00840032=UF_ACCOUNTDISABLE|UF_PASSWD_NOTREQD|UF_PASSWORD_EXPIRED|UF_SMARTCARD_REQUIRED|UF_LOCKOUT`, expiry never and unrestricted logon hours. On fresh install or explicit admission-held reinstall/rotation, SYSTEM generates one high-entropy one-use password, creates/rotates the account, supplies it only to that same `TASK_LOGON_S4U` registration operation, then zeroizes/discards it; Task Scheduler stores no password for the S4U task and installer argv/environment/log/temp/dump/LSA-task-secret residue count is zero. The SAM credential verifier required for the enabled local account is expected account state and is not misreported as reusable plaintext. An already exact account+task is readback-adopted without UPDATE. Existing account plus missing/drifted task and no ceremony password fails into the explicit reinstall/rotation flow; it is never silently repaired. MSI extraction exact-matches the policy; live readback exact-matches the resolved SID, enabled/exact-flags/expiry/logon-hours, `task_scheduler_stored_password_present=false` and zero scoped installer-plaintext residue, assigned rights, direct/effective groups and task privileges. The RequiredPrivileges XML is only desired input, never least-privilege proof. The authenticated no-side-effect task self-test returns the live token user SID; canonical SID/attribute rows; canonical privilege-name/attribute rows; MEDIUM integrity; DEFAULT elevation; AppContainer=false; restricted-token=false; and their digests over its existing pipe. Allowed groups are exactly the semantic rows `EVERYONE|LOCAL|BATCH|AUTHENTICATED_USERS|BUILTIN_USERS|LOCAL_ACCOUNT|THIS_ORGANIZATION|SERVICE_ASSERTED_IDENTITY|NTLM_AUTHENTICATION` when present under their fixed well-known SIDs plus one dynamic logon SID; the clean WS2022 S4U fixture freezes exact presence/attributes, requires `SERVICE_ASSERTED_IDENTITY=S-1-18-2`, and rejects `AUTHENTICATION_AUTHORITY_ASSERTED_IDENTITY=S-1-18-1` as a credentialed-user substitute; the task-account SID is the token user, not a group row. The privilege-name set is exactly the four Task RequiredPrivileges, with the WS2022-qualified required attributes; any additional privilege, prohibited/admin/operator group, duplicate SID/privilege, integrity/elevation drift or desired-only echo fails. `ProcessTokenSidType` is absent. Account recreation with a new SID is an explicit admission-held reinstall transition that updates every dependent ACL before the task can run, never silent drift.

The fixed action is executable `C:\Program Files\EnterprisePlatform\Authority\recovery-tool.exe` with the sole source-order argument `--scheduled-task-server`, working directory `C:\Program Files\EnterprisePlatform\Authority`, and no caller value. Its executable DACL template is exactly `O:SYG:SYD:P(A;;0x001F01FF;;;SY)(A;;0x00120089;;;{SID_EP_AUTHORITY_SERVER})(A;;0x001200A9;;;{SID_EP_F57_RECOVERY})`. The authenticated pipe is exactly `\\.\pipe\EnterprisePlatform.F57.RecoveryTool.v1`. The parent-folder policy has exactly two ordered rows. Shared root `\EnterprisePlatform` uses `SHARED_REQUIRED_ACE_INVARIANT`: it must retain SYSTEM ownership/protected DACL, contain the narrow AS read/execute ACE from template `O:SYG:SYD:P(A;;0x001F01FF;;;SY)(A;;0x001200A9;;;{SID_EP_AUTHORITY_SERVER})`, and contain no non-SYSTEM ACE granting create/delete/write-DAC/write-owner to the F57 leaf; unrelated pre-authorized read ACEs may remain and therefore its whole descriptor is not exact-hashed. Exclusive leaf `\EnterprisePlatform\F57` and the task object both use `EXCLUSIVE_EXACT_DESCRIPTOR` with exactly that template after placeholder resolution. Pipe DACL template bytes are exactly `O:{SID_EP_F57_RECOVERY}G:{SID_EP_F57_RECOVERY}D:P(A;;0x001F01FF;;;SY)(A;;0x001F01FF;;;{SID_EP_F57_RECOVERY})(A;;0x00120183;;;{SID_EP_AUTHORITY_SERVER})`. `0x00120183` deliberately grants pipe-client read/write data, read/write attributes, read-control and synchronize while omitting `FILE_CREATE_PIPE_INSTANCE`; the client opens with that concrete mask, never `GENERIC_WRITE`. The SYSTEM-installed task/folders may be SYSTEM-owned; the runtime-created pipe is owned by the S4U principal that can actually create it. Neither template forces a High mandatory label.

The normalized registration projection is exact: principal `UserId=<resolved numeric RT SID>`, `LogonType=S4U`, `RunLevel=LeastPrivilege`, zero triggers, one Exec action, the command/arguments/working-directory above, `AllowStartOnDemand=true`, `Enabled=true`, `Hidden=false`, `MultipleInstancesPolicy=IgnoreNew`, `StartWhenAvailable=false`, `RunOnlyIfIdle=false`, `RunOnlyIfNetworkAvailable=false`, `WakeToRun=false`, `DisallowStartIfOnBatteries=false`, `StopIfGoingOnBatteries=false`, `AllowHardTerminate=true`, `ExecutionTimeLimit=PT0S`, and no `RestartOnFailure`. Create flags are exactly `[TASK_CREATE,TASK_DONT_ADD_PRINCIPAL_ACE]`, update flags exactly `[TASK_UPDATE,TASK_DONT_ADD_PRINCIPAL_ACE]`; `RunEx` uses flags `0`, zero parameters and no user override. The runner exits after `60` seconds with no authenticated request, while each durable operation is bounded by its signed plan deadline/watchdog. Task Scheduler's reserialized XML is not hashed; build/extraction/live COM readback hash the same normalized typed projection. Installation resolves placeholders from one live SID registry, canonicalizes every descriptor, writes once and persists both canonical text/digest. Unknown placeholder, inherited/broad ACE, unexpected principal ACE, field/flag drift or OS-canonicalization disagreement fails installation and is never auto-repaired during a release attempt.

The request-verb allowlist is exactly `[ADOPT,QUERY,START]`; the operation allowlist is the canonical six-row set `[AUTHORITY_STORAGE_MANIFEST_ROTATION_APPLY,PACKAGE_FOUNDATION_MAINTENANCE_APPLY,AUTHORITY_RECOVERY_CHECKPOINT_RESTORE,PACKAGE_RUST_KERNEL_SLOT_RESTORE,PACKAGE_RUST_KERNEL_SLOT_SWITCH,RUNTIME_SSD_CONTROL_SET_REBUILD]`. The package action formerly described as `PACKAGE_RECOVERY_CHECKPOINT_RESTORE` maps only to the general `AUTHORITY_RECOVERY_CHECKPOINT_RESTORE{authorization_kind=PACKAGE_ROLLBACK}`; the other closed kinds are `SECURITY_INCIDENT` and `DISASTER_RECOVERY_CERTIFICATION`, each requiring its own typed dual-control authority and full-cut manifest. Every START has a nonnull typed execution-authorization ref; the checkpoint kind is nonnull iff the operation is the general restore. `QUERY|ADOPT` accept only the authenticated operation ID. `EPAuthorityServer` alone may invoke the task. No argv, filesystem path, task/service name, SQL, shell, arbitrary command, signer handle or raw secret crosses the pipe, and every result is journaled before response so response loss can only query/adopt the same operation. A full-cut request carries one `RecoveryServiceLifecycleClosureV1` derived—not accepted—from the signed runtime-deployment closure, fresh complete installed readback, server-component set, fixed G0 evidence-signer-broker row and fixed PostgreSQL service row. Its exact set is five Authority services, `EPF57EvidenceSignerBroker`, `EPF57BackupWriter`, `EPF57BackupCheckpointSigner`, `ep-postgres16`, every additional `ACTIVE` graph participant whose carrier is `WINDOWS_SERVICE`, plus `EPF57DataVolumeUnlockBroker` as the sole `KEEP_RUNNING` row; aliases and duplicates fail. Every `STOP_THEN_START` row's installed service DACL grants RT only concrete `0x00020035`, while the unlock broker remains mounted and never enters either order. Stop order is writer/checkpoint first, then additional graph services in reverse dependency topology, then Authority continuation/facades/control/server in reverse dependency topology, then `EPF57EvidenceSignerBroker`, and `ep-postgres16` last; start order is PostgreSQL first, then the evidence broker, then Authority in dependency topology, then additional graph services, and writer/checkpoint last. An operation needing a strict subset uses the uniquely derived dependency-closed subsequence, never a caller list. Every service config, DACL, dependency, state, process identity and held executable is read back before and after effect; a cycle, missing/extra active service, wrong broker/Postgres identity or retained file handle blocks recovery. DATA_HDD unlock is intentionally absent from this least-privilege task and is owned only by the dedicated broker contract below.

All five Authority services permanently share one immutable executable at `C:\Program Files\EnterprisePlatform\Authority\ep-core-server.exe`; package maintenance never calls `ChangeServiceConfig` and never overwrites that PE. The SCM `ImagePath`/`BINARY_PATH_NAME` is not the bare executable: it is the frozen Windows-quoted executable followed by the role's exact `ServiceInstall.Arguments`, with quote/parser round-trip equality. The five canonical raw command lines are respectively `"C:\Program Files\EnterprisePlatform\Authority\ep-core-server.exe" authority-server --service-mode windows-scm`, `"C:\Program Files\EnterprisePlatform\Authority\ep-core-server.exe" power-shutdown-continuation --activation-source scm-parameter`, `"C:\Program Files\EnterprisePlatform\Authority\ep-core-server.exe" power-shutdown-control-broker`, `"C:\Program Files\EnterprisePlatform\Authority\ep-core-server.exe" power-shutdown-signing-broker --role raw-evidence`, and `"C:\Program Files\EnterprisePlatform\Authority\ep-core-server.exe" power-shutdown-signing-broker --role gate-run-journal`. Manifest stores executable path plus token vector; MSI extraction and live readback reconstruct and compare both the canonical raw command line and the final-handle executable identity.

A Rust-kernel package stages its signed implementation at `C:\Program Files\EnterprisePlatform\Authority\versions\<implementation-set-sha256>\ep-authority-kernel.dll`; the recovery tool verifies final handle/SSD identity/AuthentiCode/binary/SBOM digests and atomically query/adopts `SignedAuthorityKernelSlotPointerV1` at the fixed runtime-SSD control path. The pointer has one tagged binding. `BOOTSTRAP_BUILD` is legal only for slot ordinal 1 with null predecessor; it binds the clean build's candidate run, execution attempt, source tree, Authority manifest, kernel SBOM and ABI readback and contains no generation/transition/package ref. It is signed first and then referenced by `WindowsAuthorityArtifactSetV1`, never the reverse, so no content-addressed cycle exists. `GENERATION_TRANSITION` is legal only for ordinal greater than 1 with a nonnull exact predecessor and binds target generation manifest/digest, transition, kernel package and implementation manifest; it deliberately does not claim production admission before the upper admission record exists. Both variants bind the selected kernel bytes and recovery-journal head. The same head is TPM-sealed and mirrored to DATA_HDD plus the off-host recovery target; boot rejects rollback/fork, and SSD loss rebuilds only from the quorum-matching highest authenticated head. On process start the launcher verifies the recovery-domain CMS, head chain and target bytes before loading the DLL. The tool restarts and measures the exact affected dependency-closed service set, retains the previous pointer and slot until global OBSERVED plus production admission, and restores that pointer on failure. Launcher/recovery-tool TCB upgrades themselves use only the separately signed Windows build/install recovery transaction while all business admission is held. Atomic pins each accepted request to one generation and swaps once; drain durably closes admission and accounts every durable execution lease as complete-in-place or exact-once handed off; UNKNOWN/timeout never authorizes a switch. Disable retains data, attachments, audit, recovery and package bytes.

The DLL has exactly one named, non-forwarded export and no unnamed ordinal-only export: `ep_authority_kernel_get_api_v1(requested_abi_version: u32, out_api: *mut *const EpAuthorityKernelApiV1) -> EpStatusV1`. The displayed V1 `#[repr(C)]` definitions are normative.
