Windows Server 2022 x64 is the only production ABI target: little-endian, 64-bit pointers, `EpByteSliceV1 size/alignment=16/8`, `EpMutableByteSliceV1=24/8`, and `EpAuthorityKernelApiV1=48/8`, with exact API-table offsets `0,4,8,16,24,32,40`; `struct_size` must be exactly `48`, not merely at least 48. Status integers are exactly `OK=0`, `INVALID_ARGUMENT=1`, `ABI_UNSUPPORTED=2`, `BUFFER_TOO_SMALL=3`, `VERIFY_FAILED=4`, `ROLE_DENIED=5`, `PROTOCOL_DENIED=6`, `INTERNAL=7`, `PANIC_CAUGHT=8`, and `SHUTDOWN=9`. Role integers are exactly `AUTHORITY_SERVER=1`, `POWER_SHUTDOWN_CONTINUATION=2`, `AUTHORITY_CONTROL=3`, `RAW_EVIDENCE_SIGNER=4`, `GATE_RUN_JOURNAL_SIGNER=5`; `dispatch_typed_control` protocol integers are exactly `POWER=1` and `PACKAGE=2`, and its sole allowed matrix is `AUTHORITY_CONTROL × {POWER,PACKAGE}`. For dispatcher classification the frozen precedence is: an unknown or non-control role returns `ROLE_DENIED`; only `AUTHORITY_CONTROL` with an unknown protocol returns `PROTOCOL_DENIED`; only then does zero/never-issued handle return `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, and a consumed or panic-poisoned handle returns `SHUTDOWN`. `run_service_main` applies role before handle-state classification; functions without role apply invalid-handle then consumed/poisoned precedence. Pointer safety checks that are required before any dereference still occur first and return `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Authority health/recovery/admission endpoints, continuation work and the two frozen signer operations execute inside their role's `run_service_main`; they never enter the control dispatcher, so POWER cannot issue a signer operation and PACKAGE cannot issue POWER, shutdown, continuation or signing work.

All input bytes are immutable for the call and must be canonical JCS UTF-8. A null input pointer is legal only when `len=0`; a null output byte pointer is legal only when `capacity=0`; `written` and every scalar/table out-pointer are always nonnull. `get_api` first writes `*out_api=null`; `initialize` first writes `*out_kernel_handle=0`; every output-buffer call first writes `*written=0`, all before validation or any effect. On `get_api` success, `*out_api` names one process-lifetime, naturally aligned static table in a read-only/non-writable section. Request/response/error limits are respectively `1_048_576/1_048_576/65_536` bytes. `run_service_main` has no output buffer and is invoked once per SCM dispatch; normal return is terminal service exit, never a buffer-sizing retry. Only `dispatch_typed_control|copy_last_error` may return `BUFFER_TOO_SMALL`: a zero-capacity probe is legal, the callee writes no response byte or NUL terminator, sets `*written` to the exact required byte length, and guarantees that length is within the applicable fixed maximum and `<=capacity` before any `OK`. An effectful dispatch retry must carry the same authenticated `operation_id`; an effectful first call may already have durably committed, so retry is query/adopt and returns the byte-identical result rather than repeating the effect. On every other failure, `*written=0`. `initialize` creates one nonzero handle, `shutdown` consumes it exactly once, and later use returns `SHUTDOWN`. Rust traits, `Vec|String`, compiler-layout enums, exceptions, panics and allocator ownership never cross the ABI. Every DLL boundary catches a Rust panic, records only a bounded diagnostic, returns `PANIC_CAUGHT`, permanently marks that handle poisoned, closes admission and causes the service process to exit so SCM starts a fresh process; a poisoned handle never continues serving.

Last-error state is not shared across service threads. It is keyed by `(kernel_handle,GetCurrentThreadId())`; `handle=0` exists only for an `initialize` failure after the launcher has already obtained the table and therefore can call `copy_last_error`. A `get_api` failure returns only its numeric status because no copy function is then available. Only the same OS thread may call `copy_last_error`, only immediately after a failed non-copy ABI call and before its next non-copy ABI call. Copying does not clear the bytes, but the next non-copy call replaces/clears that thread's slot. A different thread/handle, stale generation or absent error returns `INVALID_ARGUMENT` with zero written bytes. Release profile fixes `panic=unwind`, and every exported/function-table boundary wraps its Rust body with `catch_unwind`; Windows SEH faults, allocator abort and OOM abort remain process failures handled by SCM/supervision and are never falsely claimed as caught.

`crates/platform/authority-kernel/src/abi.rs` solely owns this table and export. One generator invoked only as `cargo run -p authority-kernel-abi-gen --locked -- --check` emits/checks `apps/core-server/src/kernel/abi.rs`, `include/ep_authority_kernel_api_v1.h` and `crates/platform/authority-kernel/ep-authority-kernel.def`; none is handwritten, and the `.def` names only `ep_authority_kernel_get_api_v1`. The independent golden freezes symbol count/name, numeric constants, field offsets, sizes/alignments, calling convention, header/DEF freshness and a C-built round trip under the pinned MSVC x64 toolchain. The launcher loads only the signed pointer's final-handle DLL, calls `GetProcAddress` for that one ASCII symbol, verifies version/size/offsets and every nonnull function pointer, uses `VirtualQuery` plus PE section bounds to prove the API table object itself lies wholly in a committed read-only/non-writable module section and every function pointer lies wholly inside an executable/non-writable section of that same held module, then pins the module handle until shutdown. It never compares ASLR-dependent raw pointer or relocated image bytes. The candidate/live ABI readback digest instead hashes the stable projection `{reopened_mapped_file_identity,reopened_file_sha256,export_name,abi_version,struct_size,field_offsets,function_rvas,section_characteristics}`; the memory image contributes only checked RVA/section/protection facts. Build/install tests reject a second/forwarded/unnamed export, missing/null/extra pointer, writable table/function page, unsupported version/size, pointer outside the held module/RX section, unknown role/protocol, invalid UTF-8/JCS, aliasing or overrun, retry without the same operation ID, unwind continuation, use-after-shutdown, TOCTOU file replacement or launcher/kernel allocator crossover.

The Windows loader has one exact TOCTOU-resistant sequence. It opens the pointer-selected DLL with `CreateFileW` on the canonical final path using read access and share mode `FILE_SHARE_READ` only, rejects reparse traversal, and keeps that handle open. Before loading it verifies volume identity, 128-bit file ID, size, SHA-256, Authenticode chain/revocation, x64 PE machine/section bounds, exactly one named non-forwarded export, no unnamed/extra export, no TLS callback, an empty delay-import table, and the generated exact import allowlist. Every allowed dependency is a Microsoft-signed System32/KnownDLL identity from the candidate-bound `AuthorityKernelSystemImportAllowlistV1`; a sibling/private dependency is forbidden in ABI v1. The clean service process first rejects any already-loaded same-basename module outside that set, then calls `LoadLibraryExW` on the same absolute final path with exactly `LOAD_LIBRARY_SEARCH_DLL_LOAD_DIR|LOAD_LIBRARY_SEARCH_SYSTEM32`. Immediately afterward it compares `GetModuleFileNameW` and the loaded module's reopened volume/file identity plus file SHA-256 to the still-held file, enumerates all newly loaded dependency modules and exact-matches their final System32 identities, then validates the export/API table/function RVA/section/protection projection. It does not hash relocated in-memory bytes as though they were the file. All file and module handles stay held for the kernel lifetime. On failure it may attempt only the pointer's explicit, verified `previous_pointer_ref` under the same anti-rollback head and sequence; it never scans `versions`, chooses latest, follows a neighboring file or overwrites the fixed launcher.

`crates/adapter/db-pg/src/platform_meta/package_store.rs` is the sole execution store. Migration `V20261025092100` creates the CAS-updated authoritative projection `platform_meta.package_activation_attempts` with exact columns `{activation_attempt_id uuid,item_id text,deployment_id uuid,scope_jcs bytea,authority_epoch bigint,generation_number bigint,participant_id text,package_id uuid,generation_item_ref_jcs bytea,generation_transition_ref_jcs bytea,package_trust_registry_ref_jcs bytea,hotplug_grade text,execution_action text,maintenance_reservation_ref_jcs bytea null,maintenance_action text null,plan_ref_jcs bytea null,execution_authorization_ref_jcs bytea null,execution_trust_snapshot_ref_jcs bytea null,source_package_ref_jcs bytea null,target_package_ref_jcs bytea,source_lifecycle_state text,target_lifecycle_state text,recovery_checkpoint_ref_jcs bytea null,authority_recovery_cut_manifest_ref_jcs bytea null,admission_hold_ref_jcs bytea null,reverse_plan_ref_jcs bytea,authorization_decision_refs_jcs bytea null,executor_kind text null,rollback_strategy text null,state text,drain_operation_id uuid null,drain_result_ref_jcs bytea null,switch_operation_id uuid null,switch_result_ref_jcs bytea null,probe_operation_id uuid null,probe_result_ref_jcs bytea null,applied_state_readback_ref_jcs bytea null,rollback_execution_attempt_id uuid null,rollback_operation_id uuid null,rollback_result_ref_jcs bytea null,predecessor_state_readback_ref_jcs bytea null,cas_version bigint,row_sha256 bytea,created_at_unix_ms bigint,updated_at_unix_ms bigint}`, primary key `(activation_attempt_id,participant_id,item_id)`, unique nonnull `(participant_id,plan_ref_jcs)`, and unique nonnull `(rollback_execution_attempt_id,participant_id,item_id)`. Scope and transition are always nonnull and exact-match every typed object. A many-to-many generation item therefore executes and measures independently for each required participant; no participant borrows another participant's trust snapshot, operation result or ACK. Every mutation freezes a nonnull execution-trust snapshot no later than its first external intent; `VERIFY_UNCHANGED` keeps it null. The maintenance-only group `{maintenance_reservation_ref_jcs,maintenance_action,plan_ref_jcs,execution_authorization_ref_jcs,recovery_checkpoint_ref_jcs,authority_recovery_cut_manifest_ref_jcs,admission_hold_ref_jcs,authorization_decision_refs_jcs,executor_kind,rollback_strategy}` is jointly nonnull exactly for maintenance mutation and jointly null otherwise.

Every `*_result_ref_jcs` typed-loads `CapabilityPackageOperationResultV1` and is nonnull only after that named operation completes; every readback ref typed-loads `CapabilityPackageInstalledStateReadbackV1`. `APPLIED_VERIFIED` requires `applied_state_readback_ref_jcs`; `PREDECESSOR_VERIFIED` requires both rollback result and predecessor readback. `VERIFY_UNCHANGED` alone takes `TUPLE_BOUND -> APPLIED_VERIFIED` with a fresh applied readback and zero operation IDs/results. All stored JCS is canonical and every repeated scope/attempt/item/operation/package/state field byte-matches. `row_sha256=SHA256(JCS(PackageActivationAttemptRowProjectionV1{all displayed columns except row_sha256}))`; every transition uses serializable CAS on `(activation_attempt_id,participant_id,item_id,cas_version,row_sha256)`. The execution-trust snapshot, operation binding/result, generation transition and readbacks repeat and exact-match the full deployment/epoch/generation/manifest/attempt/participant/item tuple. No table is described as append-only, and atomic/drain rows never fabricate maintenance authority.

The closed CAS graph is `TUPLE_BOUND -> DRAIN_INTENT_COMMITTED -> DRAIN_COMPLETED -> SWITCH_INTENT_COMMITTED -> SWITCH_COMMITTED -> PROBING -> APPLIED_VERIFIED`; any nonterminal forward state may enter `FORWARD_FAILED|UNKNOWN`. `VERIFY_UNCHANGED` uses only the direct edge stated above. Only a release-owned coordinator rollback request permits `FORWARD_FAILED|UNKNOWN|PROBING|APPLIED_VERIFIED -> ROLLBACK_BOUND -> ROLLBACK_INTENT_COMMITTED -> ROLLBACK_COMMITTED -> PREDECESSOR_VERIFIED`; including `APPLIED_VERIFIED` is mandatory because another participant may fail before global OBSERVED. Atomic operations may skip drain only through `TUPLE_BOUND -> SWITCH_INTENT_COMMITTED`.

Before every external call, the store create-new materializes `CapabilityPackageOperationRequestV1`, verifies `binding_sha256=SHA256(JCS(binding))`, and commits its unpredictable globally unique operation ID, exact transition, scope, trust snapshot, optional execution authorization and exact implementation/checkpoint/slot-pointer target in the same CAS. Forward operation kinds require null rollback fields. Every restore kind requires nonnull `rollback_execution_attempt_id`, `rollback_request_binding_sha256` and `reverse_plan_ref`, all derived only from the release-owned verified rollback request after durable `ROLLBACK_STARTED`; the result repeats that rollback ID. Only the private verified request crosses the broker/recovery IPC. Each executor durably enforces `(operation_id,binding_sha256)` uniqueness and implements only `begin_or_adopt|query_exact`; a repeated ID with any changed byte is `OPERATION_CONFLICT`. The typed result repeats request ref/digest, transition, operation kind/ID and exact executor receipt/evidence, and is create-new stored/reloaded before its SQL ref is committed. The participant apply readback's canonical item rows contain the nonnull package `generation_transition_ref`, installed-state readback ref and readiness closure; the server ACK carries that apply-readback ref. `APPLIED_VERIFIED` is package-local and never aliases generation-global OBSERVED or production admission.

The CapabilityGraph schema has exactly one direct import of `../evidence/f57-foundation.v1.schema.json` for its shared digest/path/delivery/client nominals; foundation never imports the graph. `client_lifecycle_fixture_trust_roots` contains exactly four rows in UTF-8 platform order `android,ios,macos,windows`; each row binds one fixed public DER certificate path, its exact byte digest and root SPKI token. `client_lifecycle_fixture_sources` contains exactly 16 rows, canonical-sorted by `(platform,role)`, with one row for every four-platform × four-role pair and the fixed role/outcome bijection below. Each fixture's `fixture_trust_root_der_sha256` exact-matches its platform's sole trust-root row; package version is nonempty canonical native-package text with no surrounding whitespace or control character, and path/package ID/digest/leaf-SPKI/root-digest use foundation owners. A duplicate platform/pair, missing/extra root or fixture, favorable-role/root substitution, leaf chain not terminating at that exact DER root, or local duplicate of a foundation definition fails the graph-schema/DAG golden.

Scheduling is authored only on `RequirementBinding { first_due_profile, release_due_profile }` and `SliceProbe { probe_profile, contract }`. Every such bookkeeping node is owned exactly by `platform.capability-graph`; it never claims a business fact. For a resolved `(RequirementID,probe_profile)`, `PROFILE_TOKEN` is the profile wire with every `_` replaced by `-`; contract ID, fixture ID and evidence ID derive exactly as `PC-F57-<RequirementID>-<PROFILE_TOKEN>`, `FIX-F57-<RequirementID>-<PROFILE_TOKEN>` and `E-F57-PROBE-<RequirementID>-<PROFILE_TOKEN>`. `rationale_sha256` hashes the exact UTF-8 bytes of the joined override-row rationale with no newline, and `assertions` is exactly `[PROBE_CAPABILITY_CONFORMS,PARENT_REQUIREMENT_REMAINS_UNSATISFIED]`. The SliceProbe node's activation-ready evidence exact-set must contain that one generated evidence ID on the registry platform lane; empty or additional probe evidence IDs fail compilation. Feature, platform-mechanism and deferred-boundary child nodes carry the real 18/35-registry owner. Their effective first-due profile is not authored: the compiler deterministically computes the minimum profile of every incoming reachable Requirement binding or slice probe, verifies the full dependency closure, and exposes that derived value only in `DisabledCapabilityV1`. A child unreachable from any binding/probe, a binding/probe with another owner, an authored child due value, a parent activated by a slice probe, or a derived value differing from recomputation is rejected. This makes shared dependencies activate at their earliest real consumer without letting an importer or developer choose the partition.

`compile` always receives the exact `DeliveryRegistryV1` beside graph, generator identity and mode. It exact-joins all 185 Requirement bindings and every slice probe to that registry before computing activation; graph scheduling fields are validated assertions, not a second scheduling authority. Thus neither the importer nor a child task may silently move a due profile.

The schema/golden suite freezes these canonical payload-enum shapes (one complete JCS value per JSON Lines row):

```jsonl
{"owner_id":"platform.capability-graph","owner_kind":"PLATFORM"}
{"kind":"REQUIREMENT_BINDING","schedule":{"first_due_profile":"G0_BOOTSTRAP","release_due_profile":"G6_RELEASE"}}
{"kind":"FEATURE_CAPABILITY"}
{"contract":{"assertions":["PROBE_CAPABILITY_CONFORMS","PARENT_REQUIREMENT_REMAINS_UNSATISFIED"],"contract_id":"PC-F57-CLI-001-G3-CLIENT-SHELL","fixture_id":"FIX-F57-CLI-001-G3-CLIENT-SHELL","probe_evidence_id":"E-F57-PROBE-CLI-001-G3-CLIENT-SHELL","rationale_sha256":"57fc5ce01c46d61a8c8434fb8ba79a5d776d6901a327beb10e9245aed09d7053"},"kind":"SLICE_PROBE","schedule":{"probe_profile":"G3_CLIENT_SHELL"}}
{"details":{"authorization":[],"carriers":[],"commands":[],"configuration_items":[],"data_objects":[],"errors":[],"events":[],"evidence":[],"facts":[],"impact_rules":[],"imported_contract":null,"lifecycle":null,"metrics":[],"objective":null,"queries":[]},"semantics_kind":"ACTIVATION_READY"}
{"row":{"state_domain":"ACCEPTANCE_V1","state_values":["ACCEPTED","REJECTED","SUBMITTED","WITHDRAWN"]},"row_kind":"API_STATE_DOMAIN"}
{"owner_id":"capability-index.tsv","owner_kind":"FAMILY"}
{"owner_kind":"REQUIREMENT_TEST_FACADE"}
```

The Bootstrap form is likewise exact: `semantics_kind=BOOTSTRAP_IMPORTED`, and `details` contains only `source_bindings` plus `imported_contract`. The JSON Schemas require the displayed tag/content keys, reject a content key on a unit variant, and reject a missing content key on a data-carrying variant.

All stable-interface vectors use the following closed canonical sort table before JCS/hashing. Scalar strings/newtypes compare their exact UTF-8 wire bytes; enums compare their serialized wire; compound keys compare lexicographically left-to-right. No implementation may use locale, insertion, filesystem, hash-map or database order.

Exactly seven stable-interface vector families preserve source order: `ExplicitFieldSetV1` defines schema field/presentation order; `BootSecurityReadbackPayloadV1.observed_boot_order` is the measured firmware boot order and must begin with `windows_boot_manager_entry_id`; `PowerShutdownContinuationInstalledServiceV1.exact_argv`; every `PowerShutdownBrokerServiceV1.exact_argv`; every `PowerShutdownServiceInstallPlanRowV1.exact_argv`; `ClientStackDecisionArchiveTrustProofV1::CertificateChain.certificate_sha256s_leaf_to_root`, whose order is the one authenticated certificate path from signer leaf through the unique root; and every semantic-contract `ORDERED_LIST.values`, whose order is part of its declared meaning. All argv families are the exact token sequence consumed without a shell. All seven families are validated duplicate-free where duplication is semantically forbidden, but are never sorted. Raw byte vectors such as `canonical_json`, `envelope_jcs` and signatures are byte strings, not sortable element sets. The GateRunJournal is a framed append-only record stream, not a vector inside a signed payload, and therefore follows its own sequence/hash-chain contract below rather than this sort table. Any future vector requires an amendment adding its key here before it can enter a signed/digested wire.

The one-time API import is lossless and self-contained. `BootstrapImported.imported_contract.rows` stores every typed field of the exact five source TSV families; source bindings prove provenance but are never treated as reconstructable content. When an imported node becomes `ActivationReady`, it retains the same `imported_contract=Some(...)`; a native node uses `None`. The seven legacy CAS wires remain the closed `ImportedCasModeV1` set and are not collapsed into the three runtime `CasModeV1` variants. Historical `NONE` values become the typed `None` alternatives and are re-emitted as `NONE`; `explicit_field_set` preserves its semicolon field order because that order is schema presentation order, while state values and route error-code sets are canonical-sorted. `project_all` receives only `CompiledCapabilityGraphV1` and must reproduce all five accepted seed byte streams with the seed files renamed/unavailable in the golden test. It is forbidden to reread a seed, infer a row from its hash/key, drop/reorder original import fields during activation, or make a live API projection depend on the historical snapshot after G0.

`ProjectionManifestV1` is closed by `docs/schemas/f57-projection-manifest.v1.schema.json`; its purpose serializes exactly as `EP-F57-PROJECTION-MANIFEST-V1`, `schema_version=1`, and every JSON type uses `deny_unknown_fields`; its exact artifact media is `application/vnd.ep.f57-projection-manifest-v1+json`. It contains exactly the 30 family IDs in G0 Task 3's `PROJECTION_IDS`, sorted by UTF-8 wire bytes. Every family has one `primary`, whose owner is exactly `FAMILY(the same family_id)`; simple families have `members=[]`. Only `rust/manifest.v1.json` and `requirement-test-facades.v1.json` may have members outside `docs/generated/f57/`: Rust members use only their exact `FEATURE|PLATFORM` graph owner, facade members use only `REQUIREMENT_TEST_FACADE`, and no other family has either member-owner kind. `client-conformance-manifest.v1.json` is the third multi-member family and has the exact sole member `docs/generated/f57/client-platform-lifecycle-policy.v1.json`, owned by `FAMILY(client-conformance-manifest.v1.json)`. `semantic-contracts/manifest.v1.json` is the fourth and only remaining multi-member family. Its primary bytes are the strict `SemanticContractsManifestV1` JCS at `docs/generated/f57/semantic-contracts/manifest.v1.json`, with `schema_version=1`, purpose `EP-F57-SEMANTIC-CONTRACTS-MANIFEST-V1`, the compiled graph/generator identities and the exact canonical binding set. Its members are the one-to-one projection of `CompiledCapabilityGraphV1.semantic_contracts` at each `projection_path`; every member byte-equals `JCS(SemanticContractProjectionV1)`, its descriptor digest equals `projection_sha256`, and its descriptor owner is `FAMILY(semantic-contracts/manifest.v1.json)`. The primary binding records exactly `(contract_id,contract_kind,projection_path,projection_sha256,row_schema_id,exact_row_count,owner,projection_targets)` and is checked against both the compiled binding and member descriptor. No 31st family or fifth multi-member family is legal. `ProjectionOutputOwnerV1` uses exact adjacent fields `owner_kind=FAMILY|FEATURE|PLATFORM|REQUIREMENT_TEST_FACADE` and `owner_id`; only `REQUIREMENT_TEST_FACADE` omits `owner_id`. All other family primaries and members remain below the generated root. Within each family, members sort by `output_path`, and all paths across primaries and members are globally unique. Media wires are exactly `application/json|application/yaml|text/tab-separated-values|text/typescript|text/x-rust|application/vnd.ep.f57-p340-certification-policy-definition-v1+json|application/vnd.ep.f57-client-platform-lifecycle-policy-v1+json`. Every descriptor hashes its exact output bytes; JSON outputs are JCS, and all text outputs are UTF-8 without BOM and LF-only.

The projection manifest is the non-circular root envelope for those outputs: it is not itself a 31st family, no descriptor points to `docs/generated/f57/projection-manifest.v1.json`, and the manifest never includes its own digest. The manifest bytes are separately hashed by staging/candidate evidence after construction. `project_all` returns primary/member artifacts with bytes, graph digest and full generator identity; `ProjectionManifestV1::from_artifacts` verifies those shared identities, descriptors and hashes before dropping bytes into the manifest. First-creation staging independently compiles the staged graph, recreates the 30-family manifest, exact-compares every descriptor, hashes every actual member, and only then treats `GENERATED_MANIFEST_SET` as an allowlist. Missing/extra family, duplicate path, self-reference, stale digest, media/owner mismatch, unsorted member, unmanifested write or manifest-only edit fails closed.

`SignedBusinessArtifactV1<T>` is byte-for-byte the already frozen F-56 four-field detached-CMS envelope. Its misleadingly historical field name `signer_subject` has exactly one security wire: `spki-sha256:<64-lowerhex>`, where the digest is over the signer leaf's exact DER `SubjectPublicKeyInfo`; the verifier recomputes and byte-compares it. An X.509 subject DN is derived from that same verified leaf and may satisfy an additional `certificate_subject_dn` constraint, but it is never an identity, authorization key or JCS substitute. Purpose is a required typed enum/value inside each payload `T` and is checked through the verifier's typed expectation; no second outer `purpose`, raw key-id, DN-as-subject, or raw-signature variant is allowed.

`CandidateBoundFreshPgEvidenceV1` is the sole persisted candidate Fresh-PG wire. Its signed payload requires `evidence_class=CANDIDATE_BOUND`, `outcome=PASS`, PostgreSQL major `16`, `baseline_count+f57_count=total_count`, the exact profile/through-version closure, the current `CandidateRunIdentityV1`, all five migration/source/check-registry digests, trusted issue/expiry, and a precursor journal checkpoint. Its envelope `signer_subject` is the registry row's canonical SPKI token and its additional certificate-subject-DN constraint is `CN=EP F57 Fresh PostgreSQL Evidence,O=Enterprise Platform`; the schema and signed byte-golden are G0-owned.

The `(profile,through_version)` pair is legal only when `through_version` is the baseline terminus for G0 or a reservation endpoint owned by that same profile. Applicable checks are exactly the rows satisfying both `profile_ordinal(row.delivery_profile) <= profile_ordinal(requested_profile)` and `row.activation_through_version <= requested_through_version`; this supports the child plans' incremental endpoints without running a not-yet-delivered same-profile handler. The closed dispatcher invokes only the row's compiled `handler_id`; it never executes an argv, SQL, script, or symbol read from the historical seed. `checks` exact-joins every applicable row once, repeats its task/profile/version/handler/contract, sets `registry_row_sha256=sha256(exact UTF-8 source-row bytes without LF)`, and requires PASS with canonical distinct evidence refs. `fresh_pg_check_registry_sha256` must equal the full current registry digest above. Missing/extra/duplicate/FAIL check, wrong row or registry digest, a handler not yet delivered, mismatched task/profile/version/contract, nonempty database, PostgreSQL !=16, count/version/profile/digest/run mismatch, unsigned engineering output, signer mismatch, expiry extension, or unknown field fails closed. `docs/f57-fresh-pg-task-profiles.seed.tsv` remains `HISTORICAL_DETAIL_INPUT`: it may be consulted only by G0's reviewed one-time registry authoring test and is never a runtime authority or executable command source.

There is exactly one such envelope per candidate run, at the `EvidenceEnvelopeStoreV1` location `evidence-relative://bundle/<RUN_DIR_REL>/fresh-pg/candidate-bound.v1.json`, where `RUN_DIR_REL` is the canonical bundle-relative parent of the explicit run journal and is empty only when that parent is the bundle root. The `maximal_profile` recorded in the immutable journal header selects its endpoint: standalone G0/G1/G2/G3, G4, G5 and final G6 use respectively their current profile/through-version. CandidateBound Fresh-PG is the sole `EvidenceEnvelopeKindV1` with a side-effecting operation state: before creating or touching the disposable database, the producer freezes one unpredictable `execution_attempt_id` in durable `EVIDENCE_OPERATION_STARTED{CandidateBoundFreshPg,...}` and passes that exact ID into the signed payload. It then create-new/fsyncs and typed-reloads the envelope before `EVIDENCE_OPERATION_COMPLETED`. Recovery from STARTED resolves only that fixed output and the original disposable database identity: it records `EVIDENCE_OPERATION_UNKNOWN`, then may adopt exact bytes or reconcile the still-identifiable database through `EVIDENCE_OPERATION_RECONCILED`; if neither proves the original attempt, UNKNOWN remains and the database operation is never rerun. The candidate manifest and every freshly emitted G0…current gate receipt in that aggregate carry a `CandidateBoundFreshPgReceiptRefV1` that byte-for-byte names this same envelope and exact-repeats its run/profile/through-version. An earlier-profile receipt does not trigger a second database rehearsal. This single superset proof prevents contradictory Fresh-PG receipts inside one candidate run.

`RequirementEvidenceBindingV1` is the one canonical result wire named by all 185 delivery-registry `evidence_schema` cells and is closed by `docs/evidence/f57-requirement-evidence-binding.v1.schema.json`. Its purpose serializes exactly as `EP-F57-REQUIREMENT-EVIDENCE-BINDING-V1`; outcome wires are `PASS|FAIL|NOT_COVERED|NOT_DELIVERED`, and only `PASS` satisfies a due row. `requirement_bindings` is the exact nonempty DeliveryRegistry subset for its TestID, sorted by `(requirement_id,evidence_id)` with no missing/extra pair. `candidate_run`, `execution_attempt_id`, provenance, platform lane, runner and carrier are typed and exact-verified; `SIGNED_CANDIDATE` requires the current manifest ref while `PRE_INTEGRATION` has no content field. Logs/artifacts are signed refs with canonical order, issue time is trusted, and expiry cannot outlive any referenced time-bearing evidence/carrier result or the journal run; immutable candidate/static content refs have no expiry and do not participate in that minimum. A due-set `TestCompleted|TestReconciled.result_ref` and every `TestResultRefV1.artifact` must typed-load this exact signed envelope, repeat the same TestID/candidate run/execution-attempt ID, and exact-match the terminal journal record. The six auxiliary release-carrier TestIDs instead typed-load the separately closed `ReleaseCarrierResultV1` and can never directly satisfy a Requirement row. Unknown/unsigned payloads, empty/mismatched bindings, PASS with missing required evidence, wrong provenance, duplicate ref, or expiry extension fail closed. The generated schema, golden vector, all four outcome vectors and negative cross-product are G0-owned.

`SliceProbeEvidenceBindingV1` is the separate signed result wire for the 78 override-derived slice probes and is closed by `docs/evidence/f57-slice-probe-evidence-binding.v1.schema.json`; its purpose serializes exactly as `EP-F57-SLICE-PROBE-EVIDENCE-BINDING-V1` and outcomes as `PASS|FAIL|NOT_DELIVERED`. For each ordered pair `(RequirementID,probe_profile)` in the resolved override registry, G0 deterministically creates exactly one descriptor: `probe_id=P-F57-<RequirementID>-<PROFILE_WIRE>`, `test_id=T-F57-PROBE-<RequirementID>-<PROFILE_WIRE>`, and `probe_capability_id=f57.probe.<lowercase-requirement-id>.<lowercase-profile-wire>`. It exact-repeats the parent Requirement's canonical TestID but its own TestID must differ. The frozen profile counts are `G0/G1/G2/G3/G4/G5 = 2/6/26/5/36/3`. A result repeats `probe_contract_sha256=sha256(JCS(SliceProbeContractV1))` and has exactly two sorted `assertion_results`, one for each frozen assertion. The generic dispatcher, not a handler-supplied Boolean, determines PASS: `PROBE_CAPABILITY_CONFORMS` passes only when the compiled contract evaluator verifies the graph node's exact generated probe evidence ID against its fixed fixture and typed handler artifacts; `PARENT_REQUIREMENT_REMAINS_UNSATISFIED` passes only when the canonical parent Requirement evaluator, run against that same evidence closure, returns `NOT_COVERED`. Overall `PASS` requires both assertion outcomes PASS; any missing/extra assertion, empty graph evidence, custom bypass, direct `Ok(true)`, parent PASS, rationale/contract/fixture drift or untyped evidence fails closed. A `SliceProbeResultRefV1` typed-loads only this envelope and exact-matches its probe ID, TestID, candidate run, journal terminal result and scheduled profile. Even `PASS` only proves the named seam: it never enters `test_results`, satisfies a DeliveryRegistry row, mutates the parent descriptor, changes `first_due_profile`, or contributes to the 185-row release due-set.

The exact G0 result-schema edges are `requirement-evidence-binding -> foundation`, `slice-probe-evidence-binding -> foundation + requirement-evidence-binding`, and `fresh-pg-evidence -> foundation`. The slice edge reuses only canonical `RequirementCandidateProvenanceV1`; foundation owns the two generic result-ref shapes and Fresh-PG plain receipt ref, while each result schema owns only its signed payload/purpose/outcome family. Every signed result root composes the foundation envelope directly. The DAG golden rejects a copied provenance/assertion/identifier/ref/envelope, a missing direct foundation edge, a result-to-gate/client/release edge or any reverse edge/cycle.

The journal's closed executable-ID registry is the disjoint union of 185 canonical Requirement TestIDs, 78 derived probe TestIDs, three auxiliary client-conformance TestIDs, four auxiliary client-validation TestIDs and six auxiliary release-carrier TestIDs, exactly 276 IDs. No runner may invent an ID. `GateReceiptPayloadV1.test_results` contains only canonical Requirement results whose `first_due_profile` equals that receipt's own gate/profile; `probe_results` contains only the probes whose `probe_profile` equals it. The exact per-profile Requirement counts are `2/19/0/0/2/126` through G5 and probe counts are `2/6/26/5/36/3`; the fresh prerequisite chain plus current receipt is the cumulative proof. `due_result_set_sha256=sha256(JCS(canonical Vec<TestResultRefV1>))` and `probe_result_set_sha256=sha256(JCS(canonical Vec<SliceProbeResultRefV1>))`; the typed verifier re-sorts, rejects duplicates, JCS-serializes the complete ref tuples and exact-recomputes both. The empty vector is the exact two bytes `[]`, never null or an omitted field. Missing/extra/duplicate probes, reuse of a parent TestID, a probe in `test_results`, a Requirement result in `probe_results`, an auxiliary result in either lane, digest drift, or any cross-profile/run result fails closed. G0 owns empty/single/multi-row digest goldens, the schemas, all outcomes and this complete negative cross-product.

`docs/f57-slice-probe-execution.v1.tsv` is the canonical 78-row dispatch registry, not a runtime guess. Its exact header is `probe_id	test_id	parent_requirement_id	parent_test_id	probe_capability_id	probe_profile	owner_task	test_target_path	test_symbol	handler_id	platform_lane	carrier_id	reconciler_id	evidence_schema`; rows sort by `probe_id`, use the ID formulas above, copy `parent_test_id` and `platform_lane` from the exact 185-row registry, set `test_symbol=t_f57_probe_<lowercase_requirement_with_hyphen_as_underscore>_<lowercase_profile_wire>`, `handler_id=slice_probes::<lowercase_profile_wire>::<test_symbol>`, `carrier_id=rust-testkit`, `reconciler_id=RECONCILE_SLICE_PROBE_RESULT_V1`, and `evidence_schema=SliceProbeEvidenceBindingV1`. Contract/fixture/evidence IDs, rationale digest and the exact two assertions are deliberately derived from the row plus the joined override/graph rather than duplicated as mutable TSV columns; generation exact-compares the derived `SliceProbeContractV1` in every graph node before accepting the row. The initial exact UTF-8/LF registry bytes therefore remain SHA-256 `2e2ba21c33941c901867155458c78335793b800e069e496bd43a19a594a1995e`. Owner and target are the following closed profile map:

| Probe profile | Owner task | Exact target |
|---|---|---|
| `G0_BOOTSTRAP` | `G0-06` | `testkit/tests/f57_slice_probes_g0_bootstrap.rs` |
| `G1_AUTHORITY_SPINE` | `G1-07` | `testkit/tests/f57_slice_probes_g1_authority_spine.rs` |
| `G2_CTC_DATA` | `G2-07` | `testkit/tests/f57_slice_probes_g2_ctc_data.rs` |
| `G3_CLIENT_SHELL` | `G3-02` | `testkit/tests/f57_slice_probes_g3_client_shell.rs` |
| `G4_CTC01` | `G4-03` | `testkit/tests/f57_slice_probes_g4_ctc01.rs` |
| `G5_INTEGRATION` | `G5-09` | `testkit/tests/f57_slice_probes_g5_integration.rs` |

Each profile owner creates its one frozen target facade plus the matching module `testkit/src/f57_cases/probes/<lowercase_profile_wire>.rs` containing precisely its registry symbols. G0 creates only the 78 descriptors and generic dispatcher shell; until the owning target/module lands, those rows are `NOT_DELIVERED` and return 70. These six profile targets are probe-only and are not counted among the 22 canonical Requirement facades. At its gate every profile row must be linked, compiled and `DELIVERED`. Missing/extra path, symbol, handler, platform lane, carrier, reconciler, schema, byte hash or dispatch binding fails generation before a test starts.

`CandidateIdentityV1` above is the unique wire also reproduced in `docs/ci-pipeline.md` §4; either document changing a field requires the same amendment. Its `migration_manifest_sha256` is exactly `sha256(JCS(MigrationClosureIdentityV1{schema_version:1,...}))`, so the immutable baseline registry/apply manifest, mutable current F57 reservation status, and legacy disposition seed have independent owners but one candidate identity. The baseline apply manifest never contains or is regenerated for F57 rows. `CandidateRunIdentityV1` is exactly `sha256(JCS(CandidateIdentityV1))` plus one unpredictable `gate_run_id`; it exists before a signed candidate manifest and is the non-circular execution identity. `ArtifactRefV1.uri` accepts only a canonical scheme registered by the owning evidence store, never a raw filesystem path or credential; `sha256=SHA256(the exact referenced bytes)` and `size_bytes=the exact referenced byte length`, and typed load recomputes both independently. Every candidate/evidence producer receives an explicit validated `--bundle-root`, and every output/journal/checkpoint path must resolve below it. For an offline evidence bundle, chain refs use `evidence-relative://bundle/<canonical-segments>` with no empty, dot, parent or encoded-separator segment. A consumed signed input outside the root is typed-verified, then create-new/atomically copied byte-for-byte to `inputs/<exact-envelope-sha256>.json`; an existing exact copy is adopted and a conflict fails. Its signed ref always targets that in-bundle copy. There is no ambient store or parent-directory inference. `evidence verify` also requires explicit `--bundle-root`; with `--offline` that root must be absolute. The supplied receipt itself must resolve below that root. Starting from that receipt, the verifier resolves only signed relative URIs below the exact root and exact-checks media type, size and digest; it never scans a directory, guesses a sibling/ancestor filename, or treats the receipt parent as an implicit root. Every vector in a signed payload is canonical-sorted and duplicate-free except the exact seven source-order families frozen in the canonical-sort section above; those seven are validated under their dedicated order contracts and are never silently sorted. `IntegrationArtifactIdV1` serializes exactly as `windows-authority|windows-client|macos-client|ios-client|android-client`; a development-slice candidate contains exactly the first two, while an integration candidate contains all five, sorted by wire bytes. Empty, duplicate, unknown, wrong-tree, wrong-graph, wrong-toolchain, missing authority, or cross-candidate artifact manifests are rejected. `GenerationNumberV1` is the unique deployment desired/observed/expected generation number type: its wire is an unsigned 64-bit integer, `0` is legal only in client `BOOTSTRAP`, and it is never a digest. Command `expected_generation` must equal `generation_report.observed_generation`; graph/generation/package digests remain separate lowerhex fields verified by the server. `ObjectiveGenerationV1` is a different strict-positive u64 nominal owned by foundation and advances only when that one business objective mutates or reopens. Equal numeric values are not interchangeable: a deployment-generation change cannot synthesize an objective revision, and an objective reopen cannot advance deployment state. Review, query, result and closure bindings use only `ObjectiveGenerationV1`; typed/schema/four-context goldens reject either nominal substituted for the other. `ClientIntentV1` fixes `schema_version=1`; its closed single-variant `ClientIntentPurposeV1` serializes exactly as `EP-F57-CLIENT-INTENT-CARRIER-V1`. Four-platform golden vectors exact-check it and reject an unknown/free-form purpose. `envelope_jcs` is the already canonical, device-signed Employee command exact bytes, while the monotonic marker and opaque draft handles never enter authority or extend server time. `TargetGateV1` is exactly `DEV_SLICE_GREEN|INTEGRATION_GREEN|RELEASE_CERTIFIED` and is never parsed as `DeliveryProfileV1`.

Every stored artifact first belongs to one generated, stable `EvidencePlacementClassV1`; every concrete `ArtifactRefV1` occurrence then binds to exactly one such class by `(containing root type, all relevant closed discriminants/tags, JSON pointer, vector item kind)`. This two-layer model is mandatory because reverse plans, generation manifests, participant ACKs, runtime declarations, the generation-approval registry, the signed storage manifest and the 89-row signer registry must be materialized before a later containing root exists. A producer resolves its type-owned placement class before writing; when a containing root is built or loaded, its occurrence binding must name that same class. No producer borrows a future receipt/candidate field merely to obtain a media/path contract. A class that points to any named typed artifact, signed envelope or checkpoint in this plan—including the static P340 policy definition, signer registry, offline-schema manifest and canonical signed storage manifest—uses that target type's exact declared media wire; every genuinely opaque package, log, archive, untyped readback, framed sample series or binary class uses exactly `application/octet-stream`. Recipe-conditioned carrier vectors, selector-conditioned conformance vectors and kind-conditioned P340 measurement vectors therefore have one exact class per concrete item even though the source Rust field is a vector. Generated class/occurrence registries and schema goldens reject an unclassified class or occurrence, a class-to-lane/media/trust mismatch, a second class for one concrete semantic type, or cross-envelope substitution. Typed consumers still parse and validate opaque bytes according to the class-selected closed parser; `application/octet-stream` is storage metadata, not permission to skip semantic verification.

`EvidenceObjectStoreV1` closes every in-bundle `ArtifactRefV1` that is not owned by `TestResultStoreV1`, `EvidenceEnvelopeStoreV1`, `CandidateManifestStoreV1`, `JournalCheckpointStoreV1`, `ArchitectureDecisionStoreV1`, `OfflineSchemaManifestStoreV1`, `AuthorityStorageBootstrapArchiveStoreV1`, or `EvidenceInputStoreV1`. Its bytes may be signed JSON, plain JCS, opaque binary, logs, time series, packages, ordinary manifests or subordinate carrier/P340 envelopes; “object” describes immutable content-addressed placement, not an envelope prohibition. The generated placement-class registry is the only constructor of `EvidencePlacementClassV1`; `resolve_class` is the creation-time path, while the generated occurrence registry is the only constructor of `EvidenceObjectFieldBindingV1` and `resolve` proves that a later field names the same class. Given either private contract and complete bytes, `create_or_adopt` computes SHA-256 and size first, derives only `objects/sha256/<64-lowerhex-digest>` / `evidence-relative://bundle/objects/sha256/<64-lowerhex-digest>`, writes create-new through a same-directory temporary file, fsyncs bytes and parent, and adopts an existing object only when size and digest exact-match. `load_exact` reopens by the expected canonical ref, rejects reparse/path escape, recomputes size/digest, and exact-matches the same class/media contract before returning bytes. Alternate extension, caller path/media, overwrite, unclassified class/field, class drift, symlink/reparse escape or hash collision returns the closed `EvidenceStoreErrorV1`. The offline schema store's generated `schemas/repo/<canonical-repository-schema-path>` copies plus its one fixed signed manifest are the only schema-copy exception. Objects are immutable and have no intrinsic expiry: any time-bearing assertion remains inside a typed signed envelope that references the object. A crash may leave an unreachable immutable object, but recovery follows only authenticated refs and never scans or garbage-collects during a run; retention cleanup may delete an object only after an offline graph walk proves no retained signed root reaches it.

`EvidenceInputStoreV1` is the distinct external signed-envelope materialization lane. The generated placement-class registry supplies signed-input class/media/trust-domain invariants, and the generated occurrence registry solely constructs `EvidenceInputFieldBindingV1`. Creation has no field-before-root cycle: the three stable bootstrap class IDs are exactly `RUN_BOOTSTRAP_ARTIFACT_SIGNER_REGISTRY_V1`, `AUTHORITY_BOOTSTRAP_STORAGE_MANIFEST_V1`, and `GENERATION_BOOTSTRAP_APPROVAL_REGISTRY_V1`; every later signed-input class likewise exists before any occurrence and later fields must exact-bind it. Domain verification never depends upward on runtime: foundation's `ArtifactVerifierV1::bootstrap_product_pinned` validates caller-supplied raw bootstrap bytes only against the product-embedded deployment pins, and `ArtifactVerifierV1::verify` is the sole constructor of read-only `VerifiedSignedEnvelopeBytesV1`. There is no public descriptor constructor or descriptor-only verifier: the verifier derives the exact nine-field policy descriptor from its actual configured root or already verified typed registry selection, the generated artifact type/purpose/media, verified leaf/chain/revocation/checkpoint and the applicable trusted-time rule. `crates/platform/evidence-trust` is the sole production composition caller of the product-pinned factory; xtask may use only the same factory with fixture pins under tests. A forged descriptor, arbitrary bundled root, wrong deployment, wrong registry selection, cross-domain token or current-versus-historical validity substitution cannot construct a proof.

Signed-input cold load is deliberately two-stage. `resolve_location` (or bootstrap `resolve_class_location`) returns only a private canonical locator/class/media contract; `load_exact_unverified` uses it to read the digest-named bytes and returns `LoadedEvidenceInputV1`, which cannot authorize semantic use. Composition passes those exact bytes and expected ref to the owning `ArtifactVerifierV1`; only after it returns `VerifiedSignedEnvelopeBytesV1` may `verify_trust` bind the verified dynamic policy digest and `finalize_loaded` exact-compare the loaded ref/bytes/class/media against that proof. Materialization always starts with verified bytes, calls the same `verify_trust`, and derives only `inputs/<whole-envelope-sha256>.json` / `evidence-relative://bundle/inputs/<whole-envelope-sha256>.json` through the shared create-new/adopt/fsync/reparse-safe engine. This closes the offline proof-before-read cycle without weakening trust. A same-media proof from another policy, another verified envelope's policy reused for loaded bytes, a cold load treated as verified, or class drift is `ContractMismatch`; dedicated goldens cover all four. `NotFound` means only that the canonical target does not exist; permission/share/read failure is `Io` or `PartialWrite`, wrong existing bytes are `DigestMismatch|ExistingConflict`, and callers may branch only on this closed result. The lane accepts canonical signed JSON envelopes only. The six detached/binary G6 bootstrap members remain under the separately owned fixed `inputs/storage-root/*` archive and never pass through this port. A source path, unsigned JSON, caller filename/media, verification from another trust domain or conflicting copy fails closed.

Source ownership and dependency direction are closed. Foundation solely owns `VerifiedSignedEnvelopeBytesV1` and the product-pinned verifier factory; `crates/platform/runtime/src/evidence/placement.rs` solely owns generated placement classes plus occurrence-to-class bindings; `crates/platform/runtime/src/evidence/object_store.rs` solely owns `EvidenceObjectStoreV1`; and `crates/platform/runtime/src/evidence/input_store.rs` solely owns the placement-only `EvidenceInputStoreV1`, two-stage input resolver and private location/full contracts. `crates/adapter/file/src/evidence_object_store.rs` and `crates/adapter/file/src/evidence_input_store.rs` are the only filesystem implementations, `FileEvidenceObjectStoreV1` and `FileEvidenceInputStoreV1`. `xtask/src/f57/run_artifact_store.rs` owns only run-scoped composition and receives both ports by dependency injection; neither `apps/core-server` nor any production crate may import, copy, path-include or feature-enable `xtask`. Delivery is staged without a forward type reference: G0 implements both ports, their shared byte engine and only private `ValidatedBundleRootV1` tooling constructors; once G1-01 creates `ValidatedDataRootV1`, that task extends both adapter files with separate authority constructors and wires them into `core-server`. Each final adapter therefore has exactly two private-token construction lanes. The authority lane derives one exact relocatable authority-generation bundle root `<verified-data-root>\generations\authority-evidence\`; object and signed-input locations are respectively `objects\sha256\<digest>` and `inputs\<envelope-digest>.json`, all on verified DATA_HDD. A raw path, SSD authority root, ambient current directory, caller-selected filename/media, or conversion between tooling/authority tokens is impossible. Both lanes share the same create-new/adopt/readback engine and byte goldens. Workspace metadata enforces that runtime never verifies trust by itself: foundation plus evidence-trust establish proofs, runtime handles placement, `adapter-file` depends on runtime, and `xtask` plus `core-server` consume `adapter-file`; every production edge to `xtask` and every runtime edge to adapters/apps/release is rejected.

`F57_EVIDENCE_MAX_LIFETIME_MS` is the single closed lifetime cap `7_776_000_000` (90 days) for every run, architecture slot/attempt/checkpoint/platform evidence, signed package wrapper, Fresh-PG envelope, client validation/artifact set, offline schema manifest, L2/L3, carrier staging plan/completion/result, Requirement/probe result and gate receipt. Unless a narrower signed input expires first, each producer sets `expires_at_unix_ms = issued_or_created_or_completed_at_unix_ms + F57_EVIDENCE_MAX_LIFETIME_MS` with checked integer arithmetic; an aggregate uses the minimum of that value and every consumed time-bearing typed expiry. No deployment setting or signer chooses a different cap. `ClientStackDecisionV1` and immutable candidate/static content are the deliberate non-expiring exceptions described below.

`docs/f57-artifact-signer-registry.v1.json` is the one canonical F57 candidate-evidence signer registry, owned by G0 and closed by `docs/schemas/f57-artifact-signer-registry.v1.schema.json`. That G0 schema is also the sole owner of `ClientStackDecisionArchiveCertificateChainRoleV1`, `ClientStackDecisionArchiveTrustAnchorPolicyPurposeV1`, `ClientStackDecisionArchiveTrustAnchorRoleV1` and `ClientStackDecisionArchiveTrustAnchorPolicyV1`; its schema and byte goldens cover the policy's exact purpose, roles, canonical order and root-digest cardinality before any G5 archive exists. The registry is a signed `F57ArtifactSignerRegistryV1` with `schema_version=1`, purpose `EP-F57-ARTIFACT-SIGNER-REGISTRY-V1`, media `application/vnd.ep.f57-artifact-signer-registry-v1+json`, exactly 89 canonical signer rows and no wildcard/default row. Every scalar row contains both `signer_subject`, an exact `spki-sha256:<64-lowerhex>` token recomputed from the provisioned role certificate's exact DER SPKI, and `certificate_subject_dn`, the displayed DN constraint shown in the table below. The DN never authorizes; a missing provisioned certificate, placeholder token, token/SPKI mismatch, DN/leaf mismatch or one token silently reused for a different role fails registry construction. Its payload additionally embeds exactly one static `ClientStackDecisionArchiveTrustAnchorPolicyV1` with `schema_version=1`, purpose `EP-F57-CLIENT-STACK-DECISION-ARCHIVE-TRUST-ANCHOR-POLICY-V1`, and exactly two sorted role rows `DECISION_SIGNER|TSA`; each role has a nonempty sorted unique exact set of complete-DER root-certificate SHA-256 digests. This policy adds no bootstrap anchor for the registry itself: before any registry lookup or policy extraction, the registry envelope must independently chain to the deployment's pinned corporate trust root, its envelope token must byte-equal the independently verified `DeploymentManifestV1.manifest_signer_subject`, and its verified leaf DN must equal `CN=EP F57 Artifact Signer Registry Authority,O=Enterprise Platform`. The token plus ACTIVE chain authorizes; the DN is only an additional leaf constraint. The policy only authorizes which already provisioned root certificate bytes may terminate the two later archive roles, and the archive cannot edit or self-authorize that set.

The registry is a non-expiring candidate-bound bootstrap/static artifact: its generated issuance descriptor is exact `static-none`, payload `issued_at_unix_ms` is audit metadata only, and its bootstrap certificate chain must be `CURRENT_AT_VERIFICATION` during ordinary/current use and at architecture finalization. No other time-bearing artifact may borrow this exception. Its exact signed-envelope bytes are hashed into `CandidateIdentityV1.artifact_signer_registry_sha256`, create-new copied to the canonical external-input location `inputs/<exact-envelope-sha256>.json` in every evidence bundle, and referenced there as `evidence-relative://bundle/inputs/<exact-envelope-sha256>.json` by every candidate and gate receipt. `archive_trust_anchor_policy_sha256=sha256(JCS(the embedded policy))`; the architecture attempt, trust closure and archive manifest repeat that digest. Permanent replay first verifies the archived registry's signature math, exact SPKI authority token, additional leaf DN and chain to the independently pinned corporate root, extracts only this policy, and uses the trusted decision time to verify that the original run had enforced the then-current registry rule; it does not require the registry signer certificate to remain currently valid forever and does not use the decision signer to authenticate the registry bytes. An existing exact copy is adopted; conflicting bytes fail. A registry signed by another token—even under an otherwise trusted certificate/DN—an unsigned registry, empty/extra policy role, arbitrary self-signed archive root, role/root swap, policy/source/bundle drift or identity/ref/policy digest mismatch fails before any F57 evidence signature or archived decision chain is accepted.

The 89 rows are the exact expansion below. `NONE` means the serialized discriminator is the empty string; `×` means one concrete row for every displayed closed value, never a pattern in the file. The four client rows and six carrier rows import runner plus certificate-DN constraints byte-for-byte from the normative tables below; registry construction resolves their actual SPKI tokens from the exact provisioned leaves and writes every expanded scalar row. All rows use `CURRENT_AT_VERIFICATION` except the one `CLIENT_STACK_DECISION_V1` row, which uses `VALID_AT_TRUSTED_SIGNING_TIME` as specified by the permanent-decision rule.

`CURRENT_AT_VERIFICATION` governs every row whenever its artifact is used as independent current evidence, including all architecture/platform artifacts at initial decision finalization. The permanent archive has one narrow notarized-history exception: after `DECISION_BOUND`, later `require|compile|validate-selected` authorizes only `CLIENT_STACK_DECISION_V1` at its archived RFC-3161 trusted signing time. It strict-parses every archived subordinate, replays its hash chain/state machine and payload issue/expiry predicates, and verifies exact CMS mathematics, JCS/purpose/media, envelope SPKI token, additional certificate DN, runner and discriminator against the archived registry bytes plus ref/digest/cardinality. It relies only on the trusted decision signer's authenticated finalization assertion for the fact that each subordinate certificate/registry/revocation check was current inside the frozen window; it does not pretend the limited two-role trust closure independently preserves those subordinate PKIs. Historical replay therefore does not reapply current certificate validity, current revocation or the 90-day expiry to those subordinate bytes. They are notarized inputs, not present-day authorization. A subordinate artifact used outside that exact decision archive remains `CURRENT_AT_VERIFICATION`; a verifier that silently upgrades an archived subordinate into current evidence, independently invents missing historical PKI proof, or requires it to remain current and thereby invalidates permanent history fails its golden. Every current package/validation run is freshly signed and follows ordinary current rules.

Registry construction rejects an unexpanded group token, duplicate/missing pair, an invalid/empty SPKI token, empty DN/role, unknown runner, DN drift from either normative platform/carrier table, token/SPKI mismatch, a validity rule other than the one-row exception, or a total other than 89. Except for the single pinned-root registry-bootstrap signing call above, every F57 candidate-evidence `sign_business_artifact_v1` call defined by this master receives a verified registry row selected by exact `(artifact_kind,discriminator)`; a caller cannot supply a signer token, DN, runner or validity rule. That bootstrap call is hard-limited to the registry's exact type/purpose/SPKI token/DN/root and cannot sign any other artifact kind. Goldens cover illegal DN-as-`signer_subject`, upper/malformed/wrong SPKI tokens, same-DN/different-key, same-key/different-DN, registry-bootstrap token drift, the registry's `None` issuance window, a time-bearing artifact attempting `None`, and a cross-kind bootstrap call. User-installed candidate-evidence certificates are usable only after a separately approved signed registry revision is committed and candidate-bound; there is no ambient “any trusted certificate” fallback.

Candidate-evidence trust material is likewise not an ambient prerequisite. G0-05 owns the sole `F57EvidenceTrustCoordinatorV1` in production-linkable crate `crates/platform/evidence-trust`, the sole OS/enterprise adapters in `crates/adapter/kms/src/f57_evidence_trust.rs`, the maintenance CLI `apps/evidence-trust-tool`, and the least-privilege local `apps/evidence-signing-broker`. From the frozen 89-row descriptor it deterministically expands `F57EvidenceCredentialRequirementV1` rows by exact `(producer_role,runner_id,certificate_subject_dn)` and adds only the separate registry-bootstrap authority and archive TSA requirements; a committed golden fixes the complete expansion and every source-row mapping. There are exactly two provider modes: recommended low-cost `SELF_HOSTED_OS_KEYSTORE_PIV_V1`, which uses Windows CNG/KSP, macOS Keychain/PIV or Linux PKCS#11/PIV nonexportable keys under one offline product-pinned corporate issuer, and `EXISTING_ENTERPRISE_SIGNER_V1`, which imports verified leaf/chain identities and sends only the approved digest/context to an explicitly pinned mTLS signer. Both modes expose identical private `VerifiedEvidenceSignerHandleV1` values, SPKI/DN/CMS/RFC-3161 output and error semantics. They may not create an unpinned root, export a private key, accept an ambient OS root, choose a row/runner/DN at request time, or send canonical payload/business bytes to a remote signer.

Provisioning is an explicit crash-safe ceremony, not part of ordinary gate execution. One protected state root and one exclusive fsynced journal freeze a CSPRNG ceremony ID, provider mode, exact deployment-bootstrap inputs, prior registry digest for rotation, complete credential-requirement digest, per-role key/certificate locators, verified SPKI/DN/chain/revocation/EKU/nonexportability/ACL results, the two archive-root sets and the registry payload's one `issued_at_unix_ms`. The registry-bootstrap handle must byte-equal the product-pinned `DeploymentManifestV1.manifest_signer_subject` and exact registry-authority DN; it can sign only `F57ArtifactSignerRegistryV1`. All 89 row subjects are filled only from the verified mapped handles. `prepare -> verify -> seal-registry -> install-broker` writes immutable session revisions and atomically projects one active broker configuration; every crash resumes the same frozen ceremony and exact output bytes. Rotation additionally requires the prior signed-registry digest and an approved clean task, produces a new signed source file/commit, and never mutates an already candidate-bound bundle. Missing/extra role, partial install, exportable key, ACL/runner/chain/revocation/TSA drift, differing complete registry bytes, placeholder token, newest-file discovery or an unjournaled active projection fails closed.

Ordinary signing uses only the fixed authenticated local broker endpoint selected by the compiled runner platform—Windows named pipe `\\.\pipe\EnterprisePlatform\F57EvidenceSignerV1` or Unix socket `/var/run/enterprise-platform/f57-evidence-signer-v1.sock`. The client submits only a deterministic authorization key derived from the owning durable attempt/finalization, registry-selected row identity, exact payload digest, private verified issuance-window digest and candidate/run context. The broker first create-new allocates or adopts the protected CSPRNG `signing_operation_id`, returns the private `VerifiedCmsSigningAuthorizationV1`, independently loads the installed signed registry/session, authenticates the calling OS identity and runner, exact-matches the mapped handle, and signs only that authorization's digest. A lost authorization response is recovered by the same deterministic key; a lost signing response is recovered by the same operation ID and byte-identical committed CMS. No CLI key path, endpoint, signer token, DN, wildcard, caller operation ID or arbitrary payload-signing method exists. In existing-enterprise mode the broker is the only network-capable component and its sole egress is the session-pinned signer/TSA endpoints; both remote endpoints must implement the same durable operation-ID query/adopt contract. Self-hosted mode has zero network egress. G0-05 must complete/seal this trust closure before committing `docs/f57-artifact-signer-registry.v1.json`, and G0-06 must observe the same active session/registry digest before the first journal or receipt signature. If the product-pinned deployment signing handle or an approved enterprise equivalent is not yet available, the command returns `F57_EVIDENCE_TRUST_PREREQUISITE_MISSING` and no placeholder registry, key, journal or green receipt is created.

On Windows Server 2022 the local broker is one fixed G0-owned SCM service outside both the five-row Authority role set and the six-row backup/recovery component set. Its exact identity is EPF57EvidenceSignerBroker / Enterprise Platform F57 Evidence Signer Broker / NT SERVICE\EPF57EvidenceSignerBroker; executable C:\Program Files\EnterprisePlatform\EvidenceTrust\f57-evidence-signing-broker.exe; source apps/evidence-signing-broker/src/main.rs#windows_service_main; argv ["--service-mode","windows-scm","--endpoint","F57EvidenceSignerV1"]; AUTO_START; UNRESTRICTED; RESTART_ON_FAILURE_MAX_THREE; dependencies [CryptSvc,EventLog,KeyIso,RpcSs]; privileges exactly [SeChangeNotifyPrivilege]; endpoint \\.\pipe\EnterprisePlatform\F57EvidenceSignerV1. Its service-object descriptor is O:SYG:SYD:P(A;;0x000F01FF;;;SY)(A;;0x00020005;;;{SID_EP_AUTHORITY_SERVER})(A;;0x00020035;;;{SID_EP_F57_RECOVERY}); its executable descriptor grants SYSTEM full, the broker SID read/execute, AS read and RT read, with no non-SYSTEM write/delete/DACL/owner right. Its pipe is owned by the broker service SID, grants SYSTEM and that SID full instance rights, and grants only concrete 0x00120183 client data rights to the dedicated EPF57EvidenceSignerClients local group; group membership is the exact canonical SID set derived from the sealed active broker session's Windows runner identities plus AS and the two keyless facade SIDs. Membership, group-object ACL, resolved pipe descriptor and digest are installation/readback fields, not ambient administrator choice; a client opens with 0x00120183, never GENERIC_WRITE, and cannot create a first, second or replacement pipe instance. The executable and immutable signed bootstrap inputs are reproducible no-customer Set-A bytes; every ceremony/session revision, active projection, signing authorization, operation journal and committed CMS result is create-new below the storage-manifest-derived DATA_HDD evidence-trust root with an authenticated off-host mirror. Before that exact volume/root is mounted and verified the service may be RUNNING/WAITING_FOR_DATA_HDD but the pipe returns only NOT_READY and creates no mutable SSD fallback.

F57EvidenceSignerBrokerWindowsInstallReadbackV1 is the sole strict plain readback; its purpose/media are EP-F57-EVIDENCE-SIGNER-BROKER-WINDOWS-INSTALL-READBACK-V1 / application/vnd.ep.f57-evidence-signer-broker-windows-install-readback-v1+json and fixes the static row digest, final-handle binary identity and Authenticode ref, parsed canonical ImagePath/argv, resolved account/service/client-group SIDs, SID type, start/recovery/dependencies/privileges, canonical service/executable/pipe/group descriptors and hashes, exact group-member SID-set hash, active session/registry digests, authenticated nonce/session binding, PID/start key/held-image identity, provider mode, readiness state, storage-manifest ref, final-handle DATA_HDD volume/root binding, state-closure ref and zero mutable SSD fallbacks. SELF_HOSTED_OS_KEYSTORE_PIV_V1 requires an explicit program-and-service outbound block and zero sockets. EXISTING_ENTERPRISE_SIGNER_V1 permits only the signed session's literal mTLS signer/TSA destination tuples and denies DNS/proxy/redirect expansion; live firewall, connection and negative-endpoint probes are part of the readback. Task G0-05 owns docs/evidence/f57-evidence-signer-broker-windows-install-readback.v1.schema.json, its exact Rust wire/static row, signed broker package, deterministic WiX fragment and extraction/runtime goldens; the early evidence runners use a separately provisioned instance under that same wire. Task 11 byte-imports the G0 package/row, installs or exact-adopts the production-host instance, collects its terminal readback and places that ref in ReleaseWindowsServiceInstallEvidencePayloadV1.evidence_signer_broker_install_readback_ref. The recovery lifecycle derives this service as FIXED_EVIDENCE_SIGNER_BROKER_SERVICE/STOP_THEN_START; no capability-graph participant may alias it. Clean-SSD rehearsal unlocks DATA_HDD through the independent two-person BitLocker path, reinstalls/verifies the broker binary/bootstrap, rebinds or reprovisions only under the evidence-key custody policy, adopts the exact HDD journal, and proves operation-ID query/adopt before READY; it never reconstructs a private key from public metadata or creates a second journal.

This 89-row registry deliberately does not replace three existing runtime trust domains: `SignedF57AuthorityStorageManifestV1` is verified only by the customer deployment trust roster; `CapabilityPackageArtifactV1`, `SignedCapabilityPackageMaintenancePlanV1` and their signed registry are verified only by the package trust domain with distinct package/customer-maintenance issuer roles; and both `SignedBusinessArtifactV1<GenerationManifestV1>` and `SignedBusinessArtifactV1<MigrationPlanPayloadV1>` are verified only by the generation/migration approval trust registry. Their exact trust-registry artifact refs and digests are generation/candidate inputs and must be typed-verified before an F57 evidence producer can reference them; none may borrow an F57 evidence signer or authorize an F57 receipt. Conversely, these external/runtime artifact types and the plain internal `GenerationParticipantV1` ACK never enter the 89-row candidate-evidence lookup. A new F57 evidence kind requires an explicit row/count amendment; a new runtime kind requires an explicit artifact-kind/issuer-role row in its owning domain registry, so neither side has a wildcard gap.

`GateRunJournalV1` is the crash-recovery authority for one `CandidateRunIdentityV1`, not an in-memory cache and not a business database. The caller supplies one exact validated `--run-journal` path to the run creator and forwards that same path byte-for-byte to every candidate-bound validation/client build, candidate build/freeze, L2/L3, gate and release-bearing physical harness command; there is no default or discovery branch. G0–G3 gate commands create their own explicit journal. The file is UTF-8 without BOM and consists only of frames `<8 lowercase hexadecimal byte length>\t<exact JCS signed-envelope bytes>\n`; the length counts only the envelope bytes, frames are contiguous, blank lines are forbidden, and every complete frame ends in one LF. The first frame is the signed header. For `maximal_profile!=G6_RELEASE`, `storage_root_binding` is exactly null. For `G6_RELEASE`, it is mandatory and is created before the run directory or any pre-freeze output: the run creator calls the sole `verify_authority_data_root_v1` constructor with the one storage-manifest path plus exact six-path `AuthorityStorageTrustBootstrapInputPathsV1`, consumes its private `ValidatedDataRootV1`, and freezes one `G6VerifiedDataHddRootBindingV1`. `canonical_data_root_path_sha256` is `SHA256(UTF-8 final-handle canonical data_root without a trailing separator)` and `release_evidence_root_path_sha256` is the same formula over exact derived `<data_root>\evidence\release-candidate`; both are nonzero, and `data_volume_identity` byte-equals the manifest plus live-volume identity. This establishes only evaluator state `VERIFIED_DATA_HDD_ROOT`, never a future P340 certification. The journal itself is create-new/fsynced below that derived root, and every G6 command and recovery re-entry exact-matches the immutable header binding before reading or writing evidence. Subsequent signed records have contiguous `sequence` beginning at `1`; record 1's `previous_record_sha256` hashes the exact signed-header JCS bytes, and every later value hashes the prior exact signed-record JCS bytes. The trusted-clock header fixes `created_at_unix_ms < expires_at_unix_ms` with the exact maximum run lifetime above. Every record/checkpoint must be issued inside that window, and every checkpoint repeats the header's exact expiry; a resumed or extended prefix can never extend the run lifetime. `JournalPrefixRefV1` is deliberately not an `ArtifactRefV1`: it fixes `media_type=application/vnd.ep.f57-gate-run-journal-v1`, `journal_uri=evidence-relative://bundle/<canonical bundle-relative path of the explicit gate-run.jcs.jsonl>` (equivalently the path join of `RUN_DIR_REL` and `gate-run.jcs.jsonl`, with no empty or doubled segment), prefix byte count and hash of the exact complete framed bytes from the header through the final LF of its last authenticated record. `ArchitectureDecisionAttemptPrefixRefV1` is a distinct non-substitutable type with the same structural fields but fixes `media_type=application/vnd.ep.f57-client-architecture-decision-attempt-v1+jsonl` and `journal_uri=architecture-archive-relative://root/g5/client-stack-decision-attempt.jcs.jsonl`, resolved only against the root containing the already verified architecture archive manifest in global, initial, committed or current-run materialization; neither prefix type accepts the other's media, a noncanonical URI spelling, percent-encoding, slash alias, case drift or path escape. A live/final journal may be longer; verification requires `file_length >= prefix_size_bytes` and hashes exactly the first `prefix_size_bytes`, so a later append cannot invalidate an earlier checkpoint. Ordinary `ArtifactRefV1` retains exact whole-file size/hash semantics. Header/record/checkpoint purposes serialize exactly as `EP-F57-GATE-RUN-JOURNAL-HEADER-V1|EP-F57-GATE-RUN-JOURNAL-RECORD-V1|EP-F57-GATE-RUN-JOURNAL-CHECKPOINT-V1`; events use the displayed `event_kind`/`event` shape.
