Values derive from the referenced signed archive/TLS/path policies and fix loopback-only listening, TLS, SCRAM, `fsync/full_page_writes/synchronous_commit=on`, `wal_level=replica`, `archive_mode=on`, empty temp tablespaces and exact `max_connections=64|reserved_connections=4|superuser_reserved_connections=3`. The typed scalar fields exact-repeat those GUCs as `reserved_connections=migration_connection_reserve=4`, `superuser_reserved_connections=recovery_connection_reserve=3` and `unallocatable_safety_reserve=2`.

On Windows, `wal_sync_method=fsync_writethrough` is a compatibility pin selecting the certified PostgreSQL 16 WAL synchronization path; the setting name, like `fsync=on`, is not by itself evidence that a drive, controller or cache honors durability. Before production activation, the bundled, installed-file-verified `pg_test_fsync.exe` runs `fsync` and `fsync_writethrough` against the same test file beneath the same final-handle DATA_HDD root. `Postgres16WindowsFsyncQualificationV1` must exact-repeat the selected method and volume, say both methods are supported with positive throughput, `fsync_and_fsync_writethrough_same_test_file=true` and `io_error_count=0`, and bind the current storage-driver-stack and write-cache-policy digests. Production durability is established only when Task 15 exact-joins those identities/digests to the same candidate's signed P340 UPS/write-cache policy and controlled HDD flush/power-cut evidence; the textual GUC never substitutes for that chain. A volume, driver-stack, firmware, write-cache policy, UPS policy, tool binary or selected method change makes the qualification and dependent production evidence stale.

Logging is equally closed: `logging_collector=on`, `log_destination=stderr` (therefore never `eventlog`), `log_directory` exact-matches SERVER_LOG on DATA_HDD, `log_filename=postgresql-%Y-%m-%d_%H%M%S.log`, `log_rotation_age=24h`, `log_rotation_size=100MB`, `log_truncate_on_rotation=off`, and both PostgreSQL `event_source` and the `pg_ctl` Windows-service `-e` source in the exact argv are fixed non-customer infrastructure identifiers. Before configuration load, only pg_ctl/early-start infrastructure diagnostics may reach the two contract-registered Windows providers; after configuration load, all server stderr is captured and rotated on DATA_HDD. Only the typed complete Event Log coverage object above—not source names or a zero scalar—proves that no fixture token reached that channel.

`client_connection_rows` is a controlled enrichment of the pre-build compiled-graph `DatabaseConsumerV1` vector, strictly sorted/unique by `consumer_id`; each source-owned field—`consumer_id|service_identity|database_role|purpose|connection_privilege_class|steady_pool_max|peak_pool_max|acquire_timeout_ms|statement_timeout_ms|capacity_budget_weight`—byte-equals its consumer. `database_name=ep`, source CIDRs are exactly `[127.0.0.1/32,::1/128]`, TLS is required, authentication is `SCRAM_SHA256`, client policy is `client_channel_binding=REQUIRE`, and `0 < steady_pool_max <= peak_pool_max`. Let `N|R|S` be checked sums of `peak_pool_max` for `NORMAL|RESERVED|SUPERUSER`: `N+2<=64-4-3`, `R<=4`, `N+R+2<=64-3`, `S<=3`, and `N+R+S+2<=64`. Every application consumer is `NORMAL`; its role has `rolsuper=false` and no `pg_use_reserved_connections`. Only graph-designated migration consumers may be `RESERVED`, with `rolsuper=false` and effective membership in `pg_use_reserved_connections`; only the recovery consumer may be `SUPERUSER`. Thus normal applications cannot consume the four reserved or three superuser slots, migration remains able to acquire its four slots after normal saturation, recovery remains able to acquire its three after reserved saturation, and the two-slot safety margin has no consumer. Runtime topology and P340 remeasure that same candidate without feeding a future ref into this contract.

`effective_critical_setting_rows` byte-equals the complete vector. `hba_rows|ident_rows` preserve semantic file order as contiguous zero-padded `00000:<canonical parsed row>` entries and are the complete parser output of the exact referenced bytes; HBA is nonempty, ident may be empty only when its referenced file parses empty, and effective vectors byte-equal projections. Every HBA row exact-projects one client row only as database `ep`, the two loopback CIDRs, record type `hostssl` and method `scram-sha-256`; HBA does not and cannot prove libpq channel binding. `authenticated_client_probe_rows` is instead a bijection with client rows and proves TLS, SCRAM, client-side `channel_binding=require`, negotiated channel binding, the authenticated session digest and observed role attributes; runtime `authenticated_probe_sha256=SHA256(JCS(authenticated_client_probe_rows))`. `trust`, plain `host`, external CIDR, duplicate/case alias, unknown include, ambient override, client-policy drift or an unbound/missing probe is invalid. Runtime `listen_addresses` is exactly sorted unique `127.0.0.1|::1`. Schema/byte goldens mutate file/SBOM/DACL fields, client source/class/role attributes, each classified budget boundary, either reserved GUC, channel-binding policy/probe while leaving HBA unchanged, HBA `hostssl`/SCRAM, Event Log contract/fixture/provider/bookmark/count/coverage, logging/rotation, WAL compatibility pin or either same-file fsync qualification, identifiers/extensions/paths/effective equality/ambient includes/existing lock; every mutation fails closed.

The service readback exact-matches product sources `observed_pg_ctl_event_source=EnterprisePlatform.PostgreSQL16` and `observed_postgres_event_source=EnterprisePlatform.PostgreSQL16` plus PostgreSQL's only permitted pre-parameter fallback `observed_early_fallback_event_source=PostgreSQL`, and requires `server_eventlog_destination_enabled=false`. Its `event_log_scan_coverage_ref` strict-loads the 19-field coverage root and exact-joins the install contract's scan-contract digest, one boot, the exact two provider-registration rows, nondecreasing start/end bookmarks and times, complete record interval, the committed fixture ref/digest and all zero clear/drop/gap/token counters. An absent, truncated, cleared, dropped, gapped, cross-boot, cross-contract, wrong-provider, wrong-fixture, digest-mismatched or `coverage_complete=false` capture fails; desired configuration or a zero scalar alone is not evidence.

Runtime readback accepts only typed `service_state=RUNNING`; an arbitrary SCM string, pending/stopped state or unknown value cannot satisfy readiness. Its held image identity exact-joins engine readback, token SID exact-joins the resolved service row, listener count equals the canonical loopback vector length, and both nonloopback counters are zero.

The exact service is `ep-postgres16` / `Enterprise Platform PostgreSQL 16` / `NT SERVICE\ep-postgres16`, SID type `UNRESTRICTED`, `DEMAND_START`, `NO_AUTOMATIC_RESTART`, `WIN32_OWN_PROCESS`, normal error control and not delayed. It invokes `C:\Program Files\EnterprisePlatform\PostgreSQL\16\bin\pg_ctl.exe` from SSD Set A with argv `[runservice,-N,ep-postgres16,-D,<signed-PGDATA>,-e,EnterprisePlatform.PostgreSQL16,-w]`, while configuration fixes `event_source=EnterprisePlatform.PostgreSQL16`; dependencies are `[CryptSvc,EPF57DataVolumeUnlockBroker,EventLog,KeyIso,RpcSs]` and privilege is `[SeChangeNotifyPrivilege]`. SYSTEM alone has full control; Authority has only query/start `0x00020015`, Recovery only query/start/stop `0x00020035`, and both are denied change-config/delete. A dependency does not prove readiness: Authority explicitly starts it only after current-boot DATA_HDD unlock, storage manifest, vault, effective config and TLS policy pass. Before HDD unlock its process count is zero; afterward it listens only on exact loopback and has zero non-loopback outbound sockets.

`installer/windows/postgresql16.lock.json` pins the exact PostgreSQL 16 minor/build, offline package digest, Authenticode signer, SBOM-bijective installed-file vector/digest, locale, encoding, checksums and extension set. PGDATA, including live `pg_wal` and database temporary relations, is `<data-root>\postgres\data`; `<data-root>\postgres\wal` is archive staging only, `<data-root>\postgres\temp` is process/restore scratch only, and logs/TLS/config remain on their signed HDD roots. V1 forbids `initdb --waldir`, user tablespaces, reparse descendants, ambient includes and `postgresql.auto.conf` overrides. Both exact config bytes and parsed effective values prove loopback `hostssl` plus SCRAM in HBA, while the separate authenticated client probe proves libpq `channel_binding=require` and successful negotiation. They also prove checksums, exact `max_connections=64|reserved_connections=4|superuser_reserved_connections=3`, the `NORMAL|RESERVED|SUPERUSER` role-class budgets and attributes, `fsync|full_page_writes|synchronous_commit=on`, `wal_sync_method=fsync_writethrough` only as a compatibility pin, same-file `fsync` plus `fsync_writethrough` DATA_HDD qualification, `wal_level=replica`, `archive_mode=on`, the signed archive executor (**F-71**: `archive_mode=on` retains WAL segments until archiving succeeds, so the executor's *persistent-failure* path must be explicitly bounded and covered by a case. `max_slot_wal_keep_size` bounds slot retention only and does not bound archive-failure retention. Stage 14 had deliberately removed this growth path and recorded that removal as a net gain for the single-machine form; `archive_mode=on` reinstates it. The owning task must state the bound and prove it with an injected persistent archive failure — the repository has cases for local-spool-full and for pg_receivewal stopped, but none for a persistently failing archiver), collector-backed rotated HDD logging with no server eventlog destination, no `trust`, no external CIDR and `temp_tablespaces=''`. Only the later Task-15 join to current P340 storage-driver/write-cache/UPS and controlled flush/power-cut evidence completes the physical-durability claim. The host service formula remains `10 + active_additional_windows_service_count`.

PostgreSQL log retention is a separate signed policy and high-risk cleanup capability, not a mutable GUC, environment value or generic file task. Its exact normal targets are `maximum_age_seconds=2592000`, `maximum_total_bytes=21474836480`, `minimum_retained_age_seconds=604800` and `delete_current_log=false`; site legal/contract retention and object legal holds can only extend them. The accounting set is every closed/rotated regular file under the final-handle-verified `SERVER_LOG` root, deduplicated by file identity; the current open log, every file younger than seven days and every held object are ineligible. Only the existing `EPAuthorityControl` service may execute typed `POSTGRES_LOG_RETENTION_CLEANUP` after two different authorized humans approve an immutable preview sorted by `(closed_at_unix_ms,canonical_path,sha256)`, with policy, trusted time, legal-hold and free-space readbacks bound. Execution reopens every candidate, refuses identity/digest drift, records the exact deleted/retained sets and before/after tree digests, and emits one audit receipt. PostgreSQL, backup-writer and normal Authority identities have ACL-denied delete/change-ACL/release-hold/change-policy probes. If holds make age and size targets impossible, protected bytes remain and capacity handling fails closed. Effective bulk suspension begins below `max(existing_yellow_free_bytes,53687091200)` and deployment-wide hold below `max(existing_red_free_bytes,42949672960)`; existing P340 reserve/growth and 100-GiB file floor remain authoritative whenever stricter. Tests cover equality, size-only/age-only pressure, current/young/held files, hard-link/path alias, concurrent rotation, response loss, partial deletion, legal-hold change and every ACL negative.

`Postgres16WindowsInstallReadbackV1.tls_readback_ref` and `.firewall_readback_ref` each fix `application/octet-stream` and live in `EvidenceObjectStoreV1`; they are decoded only by the same owner’s closed field parsers `EP_F57_POSTGRES16_TLS_READBACK_V1` and `EP_F57_POSTGRES16_FIREWALL_READBACK_V1`. TLS parsing exact-binds contract/policy, server certificate SPKI/chain, nonexportable private-key provider and service-SID key ACL, with zero unauthorized key access. It also exact-binds every `authenticated_client_probe_rows` entry to the matching consumer/session: TLS established, SCRAM authentication, client policy `channel_binding=require`, negotiated channel binding, runtime session-binding digest and observed `rolsuper`/`pg_use_reserved_connections` attributes for the declared `NORMAL|RESERVED|SUPERUSER` class. HBA parsing proves only `hostssl` plus `scram-sha-256` and never substitutes for that client-side probe. Firewall parsing exact-binds installed `postgres.exe`, service SID and loopback endpoint set, with zero nonloopback listener, inbound external allow, outbound nonloopback socket or unexpected rule. Parsed outputs exact-equal the typed configuration/runtime scalars, including `authenticated_probe_sha256=SHA256(JCS(authenticated_client_probe_rows))`; the two captures gain no purpose, schema root or signer row because their hashes are authenticated by the signed strict install-readback parent. Missing/unbound probe bytes, generic parser selection, cross-contract capture or desired-policy echo fails.

Task 11 freezes the deployment source for exactly six component IDs: `BACKUP_WRITER_SERVICE`, `BACKUP_CHECKPOINT_SIGNER_SERVICE`, `DATA_VOLUME_UNLOCK_BROKER_SERVICE`, `RECOVERY_TOOL`, `PG_PASSPHRASE_HELPER`, and `BACKUP_TARGET_AGENT`. The first three are the following exact `WindowsBackupServiceInstallRowV1` rows; vectors are source-order where stated and otherwise canonical UTF-8 sorted:

| Role | Service / display / account | ImagePath and argv | Start / recovery / dependencies / privileges | Pipe and closed capability set |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `BACKUP_WRITER` | `EPF57BackupWriter` / `Enterprise Platform F57 Backup Writer` / `NT SERVICE\EPF57BackupWriter` | `C:\Program Files\EnterprisePlatform\Authority\backup-writer.exe`; argv `[--service-mode,windows-scm,--component,BACKUP_WRITER_SERVICE]`; source `apps/backup-writer/src/main.rs#windows_service_main` | `UNRESTRICTED`; `AUTO_START`; `RESTART_ON_FAILURE_MAX_THREE`; deps `[CryptSvc,EventLog,RpcSs,VSS]`; privileges `[SeBackupPrivilege,SeChangeNotifyPrivilege,SeManageVolumePrivilege]` | `\\.\pipe\EnterprisePlatform.F57.BackupWriter.v1`; capabilities `[BACKUP_SNAPSHOT_READ,BACKUP_TARGET_WRITE]` |
| `BACKUP_CHECKPOINT_SIGNER` | `EPF57BackupCheckpointSigner` / `Enterprise Platform F57 Backup Checkpoint Signer` / `NT SERVICE\EPF57BackupCheckpointSigner` | `C:\Program Files\EnterprisePlatform\Authority\backup-checkpoint-signer.exe`; argv `[--service-mode,windows-scm,--component,BACKUP_CHECKPOINT_SIGNER_SERVICE]`; source `apps/backup-checkpoint-signer/src/main.rs#windows_service_main` | `UNRESTRICTED`; `AUTO_START`; `RESTART_ON_FAILURE_MAX_THREE`; deps `[CryptSvc,EventLog,RpcSs]`; privileges `[SeChangeNotifyPrivilege]` | `\\.\pipe\EnterprisePlatform.F57.BackupCheckpointSigner.v1`; capabilities `[BACKUP_CHECKPOINT_SIGN]` |
| `DATA_VOLUME_UNLOCK_BROKER` | `EPF57DataVolumeUnlockBroker` / `Enterprise Platform F57 Data Volume Unlock Broker` / `LocalSystem` | `C:\Program Files\EnterprisePlatform\Authority\data-volume-unlock-broker.exe`; argv `[--service-mode,windows-scm,--component,DATA_VOLUME_UNLOCK_BROKER_SERVICE]`; source `apps/data-volume-unlock-broker/src/main.rs#windows_service_main` | `RESTRICTED`; `AUTO_START`; `RESTART_ON_FAILURE_MAX_THREE`; deps `[BDESVC,CryptSvc,EventLog,KeyIso,RpcSs,Winmgmt]`; privileges `[SeChangeNotifyPrivilege,SeManageVolumePrivilege]` | `\\.\pipe\EnterprisePlatform.F57.DataVolumeUnlockBroker.v1`; capabilities `[UNLOCK_BOUND_DATA_HDD]`; `outbound_network_allowed=false`; `data_volume_identity_binding_required=true` |

Writer and checkpoint signer use service-object template `O:SYG:SYD:P(A;;0x000F01FF;;;SY)(A;;0x00020005;;;{SID_EP_AUTHORITY_SERVER})(A;;0x00020035;;;{SID_EP_F57_RECOVERY})` and pipe template `O:{SID_COMPONENT}G:{SID_COMPONENT}D:P(A;;0x001F01FF;;;SY)(A;;0x001F01FF;;;{SID_COMPONENT})(A;;0x00120183;;;{SID_EP_AUTHORITY_SERVER})`. All three executable files use protected template `O:SYG:SYD:P(A;;0x001F01FF;;;SY)(A;;0x001200A9;;;{SID_COMPONENT})(A;;0x00120089;;;{SID_EP_AUTHORITY_SERVER})(A;;0x00120089;;;{SID_EP_F57_RECOVERY})`; final-file replace/delete/write-DAC/write-owner probes by every non-SYSTEM principal must fail. The LocalSystem/restricted-SID unlock broker instead uses service-object template `O:SYG:SYD:P(A;;0x000F01FF;;;SY)(A;;0x00020005;;;{SID_EP_AUTHORITY_SERVER})(A;;0x00020005;;;{SID_EP_F57_RECOVERY})` and pipe template `O:SYG:SYD:P(A;;0x001F01FF;;;SY)(A;;0x001F01FF;;;{SID_EP_F57_DATA_VOLUME_UNLOCK_BROKER})(A;;0x00120183;;;{SID_EP_AUTHORITY_SERVER})`: SYSTEM is its primary owner, the restricted service SID has full server-instance access, AS has client data rights without pipe-instance creation, and RT can query but cannot start or stop it. MSI resolves the named SIDs with the same placeholder-before-parser and deterministic binary-descriptor serialization rules as the eighteen-row table and records the resolved bytes/digests. The writer row has no signing or unlock capability; the checkpoint signer has no backup-source, backup-target, unlock or plaintext-content capability; the unlock broker has no database, backup, signer, file-enumeration, shell or arbitrary-volume capability. Task-11 schema, generated deployment registry, WiX projection and MSI extraction compare every field, not an opaque row digest. Live `WindowsBackupServiceInstalledReadbackV1` independently reads the final-handle executable identity and canonical DACL plus parsed SCM canonical command line/argv, resolved account SID, distinct service SID and observed SID type, start/recovery/dependencies/required-privileges, canonical resolved service SDDL, pipe endpoint/DACL, outbound firewall disposition, volume-binding flag and advertised capability set; those values exact-project from the static row after placeholder resolution before its runtime nonce proof is accepted. Runtime readback separately records token user SID, service SID, dynamic service-logon SID, the canonical restricted-SID set/digest and exact privileges. The broker requires user SID `S-1-5-18`, its own `S-1-5-80-...` service SID, `RESTRICTED`, and a restricted set containing its service SID plus the Windows-defined World, dynamic service-logon and Write-restricted SIDs; writer/signer require their own UNRESTRICTED service identity. `data_hdd_unlock_broker_bootstrap_readback_ref` is nonnull only for the broker and typed-loads the current strict bootstrap readback; it is null for writer/signer. RT can read/stop/start writer/signer during a derived recovery closure but cannot change or delete them; live negatives prove RT START/STOP on the unlock broker is denied and the broker remains KEEP_RUNNING.

The unlock broker accepts exactly `BEGIN_OR_ADOPT_UNLOCK|QUERY_UNLOCK` over its pipe from the live AS SID. Request fields are only `{schema_version,operation_id,windows_boot_id,deployment_id,authority_epoch,unlock_authority_ref,expected_data_volume_identity}`; the broker ignores no field and accepts no path, thumbprint, protector, method, provider, volume or credential override. It loads only the fixed pre-HDD locators, verifies the registry and authority closure, exact-matches the request, opens `LocalMachine\My`, requires `FindValidCertificates` to contain the one explicit nonzero thumbprint, and calls only `UnlockWithCertificateThumbprint` with the fixed empty PIN. Its CNG key descriptor is `O:SYG:SYD:P(A;;0x001F019B;;;SY)(A;;0x00120089;;;{SID_EP_F57_DATA_VOLUME_UNLOCK_BROKER})`. The `Root\CIMV2\Security\MicrosoftVolumeEncryption` namespace uses `MERGE_REQUIRED_ACE_INVARIANT`, not an OS-descriptor replacement: SYSTEM reads the current descriptor, preserves required OS/provider ACEs, merges exactly one broker-SID required ACE mask `0x00000003=WBEM_ENABLE|WBEM_METHOD_EXECUTE`, writes it during installation and reads it back. That broker SID has none of `0x00000004|08|10|20|40|80`; ordinary runtime verifies but never repairs the namespace. The full canonical live descriptor/hash is evidence, while cross-patch conformance compares the required/forbidden ACE projection rather than static whole-SDDL bytes. The COM/WMI connection is local-computer only, namespace `ROOT\CIMV2\Security\MicrosoftVolumeEncryption`, `CoSetProxyBlanket` authentication `RPC_C_AUTHN_LEVEL_PKT_PRIVACY`, impersonation `RPC_C_IMP_LEVEL_IMPERSONATE`, no supplied caller credential and no delegation. The compiled certified-volume identity alone derives the exact encryptable-volume instance path and the only method is `UnlockWithCertificateThumbprint`; caller WQL, server, namespace, object path and method are unrepresentable, and lower authentication/remote/delegated probes fail. Windows WMI has no per-method ACL, so method minimization is enforced honestly by the fixed signed broker binary, WDAC, closed typed protocol and negative tests—not claimed as an OS ACL feature. Restricted primary/restricted token SIDs, namespace required/forbidden ACE projection, BitLocker policy/EKU/KeyUsage/organization-ID readback, certificate provider/hardware/export/use policy, `LocalMachine\My` DER/thumbprint/SPKI/private-key binding, outbound program/service firewall block and bound-volume/protector set are all observed in `DataHddUnlockBrokerBootstrapReadbackV1`. That readback requires `protector_type=7`, `protector_certificate_type=2`, the exact PUBLIC_KEY/certificate/public-key digest and `FindValidCertificates` exact-thumbprint result; its ref is repeated by the broker component and every unlock readback. SYSTEM and the broker SID must both satisfy restricted-token key/namespace access; AS, RT, other service SIDs and Administrators receive no private-key ACE. Private export/delete/DACL-owner mutation, auto-search thumbprint `0`, nonempty PIN, alternate volume/protector/method, `CreateNamedPipe` by AS, remote pipe access and any outbound socket are negative probes. A restricted-LocalSystem WS2022 qualification must return method code `0`, observe protector type `7`/PUBLIC_KEY, exact-match the certificate and volume and prove fixed-data auto-unlock remains false; otherwise this profile cannot ship. The broker returns strict plain `DataHddBitLockerUnlockReadbackV1` over the authenticated session; AS create-new persists it on DATA_HDD after mount, and signed build/install/P340/POWER evidence reaches that exact ref. It is deliberately not another independently signed business envelope or signer-registry row.

Ordinary reboot and clean-SSD recovery are different contracts. Ordinary reboot reopens the existing Microsoft Platform Crypto Provider persisted key by its CNG name and performs unattended certificate unlock. The OS-disk CNG machine-key record and certificate-store binding are bounded, TPM-bound, nonexportable, no-customer-field Set-A rows under `TPM_BOUND_REENROLLABLE_MACHINE_KEY_METADATA`; they are necessary pre-HDD runtime state but never the sole recovery authority. A clean SSD destroys that provider/container binding, so the design **does not** claim that DER, SPKI, a TPM handle or public metadata can recreate the old key. Clean-SSD qualification keeps admission closed, uses the off-host 48-digit recovery-password ceremony under two-person authorization to unlock DATA_HDD, creates a new TPM-backed nonexportable key and CA-chained certificate, adds and verifies a new PUBLIC_KEY protector, signs a strictly higher unlock-authority epoch, advances the separate TPM policy-protected NV anti-rollback record, performs a normal-reboot broker unlock, then removes the old protector. `SsdDataHddRecoveryAndReenrollmentReadbackV1.steps` is exactly the eight displayed enum variants in sequence `1..8`, one operation ID, strictly increasing trusted times and a previous-step hash chain; each typed evidence ref proves its named effect. Outer IDs/epoch/Booleans are derived from that chain, both recovery-secret counters are zero, the normal-reboot unlock and new bootstrap refs exact-match their steps, and admission-opened-before-closure is false. The readback never opens admission itself; only after it plus every remaining current production-certification gate passes may the separate admission authority reopen. TPM/mainboard loss follows the same recovery-password path and is never advertised as unattended.

`RECOVERY_TOOL` is the sole `ON_DEMAND_SCHEDULED_TASK` row and uses the exact principal/action/folder/task/executable/IPC/operation contract above. Its live row repeats the complete principal policy, resolved account name/SID, actual user rights, direct/effective groups and empty prohibited intersection, normalized registration COM projection, both parent-folder DACLs, task/executable/pipe DACLs and held file identity; desired-policy echo or OS-reserialized XML cannot substitute. `PG_PASSPHRASE_HELPER` is the sole `ON_DEMAND_EXECUTABLE` row at `C:\Program Files\EnterprisePlatform\Authority\pg-passphrase-helper.exe`; it runs only as the resolved `EPF57Recovery` principal with empty argv, empty secret-bearing environment and transport `INHERITED_ANONYMOUS_HANDLES_V1`. Its request/response caps are `65536/4096`, Job Object policy is `active_process_limit=1`, `kill_on_job_close=true`, `child_process_creation_allowed=false`, outbound network is denied, and its executable DACL template is exactly `O:SYG:SYD:P(A;;0x001F01FF;;;SY)(A;;0x001200A9;;;{SID_EP_F57_RECOVERY})`. Its ordered operation set is `[VERIFY_RECOVERY_KEY_ACCESS,WRITE_PASSPHRASE_TO_BOUND_POSTGRES_STDIN]`: the latter writes plaintext only to the installer/recovery-tool-created inherited stdin handle of the already identity-bound PostgreSQL restore process and returns a nonsecret receipt. Plaintext is forbidden in argv, environment, stdout/stderr, filesystem, event log, crash dump and telemetry. The live row independently reads resolved executable DACL, token, argv, handle transport, Job limits, child-process mitigation and outbound firewall state; the three plaintext-leak counters must be zero. A desired policy/digest without those observed values is invalid.

Neither on-demand component has an SCM row. The target is `OFF_HOST_ONLY` and separately packaged. Generated `installer/windows/generated/BackupComponents.wxi` contains exactly the five on-host binaries, the three typed service rows and one immutable task-registration row; the off-host package contains only the target agent. A co-located target, shared writer/signer/unlock identity, downloaded helper, caller-selected action/argv, second recovery task or SCM row, missing field/row or off-host binary in the Authority MSI fails closed. The fixed **EnterprisePlatform-owned** production-build inventory is exactly **nine SCM services** (five Authority, the one G0 evidence-signer broker and these three), **one product Scheduled Task**, and **one on-demand executable**. The complete production-host inventory additionally contains the separately pinned `ep-postgres16` SCM service and exactly the non-aliased `ACTIVE/WINDOWS_SERVICE` rows from the runtime-deployment closure; its cardinality is therefore `10 + active_additional_windows_service_count`, with exact set equality rather than a guessed constant. Windows/third-party system rows are outside that cardinality, while any unknown `EP*|EnterprisePlatform`-owned row fails. “Five Authority services” means only that launcher-role subset; it never excludes the G0 broker, component services, PostgreSQL or graph-derived rows from complete-host inventory.

The immutable authority executable owns only one Windows SCM/argv dispatcher plus kernel verification/lifetime management. `apps/core-server/src/platform/windows_service/dispatcher.rs` recognizes the five exact manifest vectors, maps them to closed numeric roles and invokes the verified table; it has no role handler. `crates/platform/authority-kernel/src/dispatch.rs` alone owns the five role implementations: ordinary Authority, continuation, control broker, raw-evidence signer facade and gate-journal signer facade. Task 14 must land both sides and the exact ABI before the authority build; the manifest, MSI service/file tables, signed pointer, ABI/export golden, five-row static/dynamic install readback and Authenticode evidence exact-prove each SCM vector enters the selected kernel through the same launcher. Ordinary Authority kernel role owns only `boot::prepare`, database recovery, HTTPS/API startup and the recovery-proof endpoint. Control/raw-facade/journal-facade argv are respectively `power-shutdown-control-broker`, `power-shutdown-signing-broker --role raw-evidence`, and `power-shutdown-signing-broker --role gate-run-journal`; Authority and those three services are permanent `AUTO_START`, `UNRESTRICTED` and use `RESTART_ON_FAILURE_MAX_THREE`. Control alone depends on `[CryptSvc,EventLog,RpcSs]`; raw/journal facades depend on `[CryptSvc,EPF57EvidenceSignerBroker,EventLog,RpcSs]`; Authority depends on `[CryptSvc,EPF57DataVolumeUnlockBroker,EPF57EvidenceSignerBroker,EventLog,RpcSs]`. Only control has `[SeChangeNotifyPrivilege,SeShutdownPrivilege]`; Authority and each facade have exactly `[SeChangeNotifyPrivilege]`. Empty/zero/free-form helper authority, unsorted patch IDs, build/UBR or volume drift, target/ref/tool mismatch, missing install start, duration rounding/boundary drift, time inversion and every one-at-a-time field mutation have named failing goldens; no helper is a loose log or unreachable second authority.

The runtime SSD persistent allowlist is one generated `RuntimeSsdExceptionRegistryV1`, not prose and not a scanner exclusion. Its canonical owner/schema/media are `crates/platform/runtime/src/storage/runtime_ssd_exceptions.rs`, `docs/schemas/f57-runtime-ssd-exception-registry.v1.schema.json`, and `application/vnd.ep.f57-runtime-ssd-exception-registry-v1+json`; `profile_id=WINDOWS_SERVER_2022_P340_SINGLE_DISK_V1`. It is a static five-field policy `{schema_version,purpose,profile_id,rules,canonical_rule_set_sha256}` and therefore contains no deployment/storage-manifest back-reference or hash cycle. The generated JCS bytes are compiled into the launcher/kernel and installed read-only at exactly `C:\Program Files\EnterprisePlatform\Authority\policy\f57-runtime-ssd-exception-registry.v1.json`; build, MSI extraction, installed-file final-handle readback and embedded-byte readback must all be byte-equal. The signed storage manifest's `policy_ids` must contain exactly one token `runtime-ssd-exception-registry-sha256:<64-lowerhex>` whose suffix equals SHA-256 of those exact bytes; boot, clean restore, P340, offline verification and production admission accept only the embedded/installed/offline copies with that digest, never a latest/neighbor file. Its `rules` are sorted by the following exact four class ordinals and no fifth row is legal:

| Class / canonical root | Relative grammar | Hard budget | Exact retention and rebuild authority |
|---|---|---:|---|
| `POWER_CONTROL_CAPSULE` / `C:\ProgramData\EnterprisePlatform\continuation-control\power-shutdown` | `POWER_ATTEMPT_V1` | total `1073741824`, each complete attempt and every object at most `33554432`, entries `4096` | one active + eight mirrored terminal attempts, terminal age `7776000` seconds; `AttemptControl.maximum_instance_bytes=33554432`; rebuild set `[DATA_HDD_EVIDENCE_OBJECT_STORE,OFF_HOST_CONTROL_MIRROR]` |
| `PACKAGE_RECOVERY_CONTINUATION_CAPSULE` / `C:\ProgramData\EnterprisePlatform\continuation-control\package-maintenance` | `PACKAGE_RECOVERY_OPERATION_V1` | total `4294967296`, each operation at most `536870912`, every object at most `268435456`, entries `8192` | one active + eight mirrored terminal operations, terminal age `15552000` seconds; `AttemptControl.maximum_instance_bytes=536870912`; rebuild set `[DATA_HDD_PACKAGE_RECOVERY_STORE,OFF_HOST_CONTROL_MIRROR,TPM_MONOTONIC_HEAD]` |
| `AUTHORITY_KERNEL_SLOT_POINTER_AND_JOURNAL_HEAD` / `C:\ProgramData\EnterprisePlatform\authority-kernel\control` | `KERNEL_POINTER_AND_HEAD_V1` | total `67108864`, every object and `MonotonicPointer.maximum_journal_head_bytes` exactly capped at `4194304`, entries `4096` | current pointer + previous pointer + current journal head only; there is no undeclared compacted-history file; rebuild set `[DATA_HDD_AUTHORITY_KERNEL_POINTER_ARCHIVE,TPM_MONOTONIC_HEAD]` |

Each rule's `allowed_objects` is a canonical unique path-pattern → `RuntimeSsdMediaContractIdV1` → maximum-size map, never a loose filename list or media allowlist. `POWER_ATTEMPT_V1` has exactly ten rows below `<attempt-id>\`: `plan.v1.json→CARRIER_STAGING_PLAN_V1`, `artifact-signer-registry.v1.json→ARTIFACT_SIGNER_REGISTRY_V1`, `gate-run-prefix-through-pre-shutdown-committed.bin→GATE_RUN_JOURNAL_PREFIX_V1`, `continuation-state-prefix-through-pre-shutdown-committed.bin→POWER_SHUTDOWN_CONTINUATION_STATE_PREFIX_V1`, `dispatch-commit-intent.v1.json→POWER_SHUTDOWN_DISPATCH_COMMIT_INTENT_V1`, `dispatch-api-call-committed.v1.json→POWER_SHUTDOWN_DISPATCH_API_CALL_COMMITTED_V1`, `dispatch-acknowledgement.v1.json→POWER_SHUTDOWN_DISPATCH_ACKNOWLEDGEMENT_V1`, `postboot-resume-controller.v1.jcs.jsonl→POWER_SHUTDOWN_POSTBOOT_RESUME_CONTROLLER_V1`, `failure.v1.json→POWER_SHUTDOWN_CONTINUATION_FAILURE_READBACK_V1`, and `failure-cleanup.v1.json→POWER_SHUTDOWN_CONTINUATION_FAILURE_CLEANUP_READBACK_V1`; each row's maximum is `33554432`, while existing per-inline-component `1048576` caps still apply. The contract ID resolves only through the sole media registry, so this policy cannot invent or alias a media string.

`PACKAGE_RECOVERY_OPERATION_V1` has exactly three patterns below `<operation-id>\`: `capsule-frames\<20-digit-zero-padded-sequence>.signed.v1.json→PACKAGE_RECOVERY_CONTINUATION_CAPSULE_FRAME_V1`, `operation.v1.jcs.jsonl→PACKAGE_RECOVERY_OPERATION_JOURNAL_V1`, and `terminal-reseal.v1.json→PACKAGE_RECOVERY_TERMINAL_RESEAL_PAYLOAD_V1`; each has `maximum_object_bytes=268435456`. Thus the registry has exactly four classes, nineteen distinct media-contract IDs and twenty path rows (`10+3+3+4`). The rule's `allowed_object_set_sha256` covers every separate path pattern, contract ID and per-object limit; `|` is never treated as an implicit pattern operator.

Every rule fixes `authoritative_business_data_allowed=false`. Its root must final-handle resolve to the certified RUNTIME_SSD without reparse traversal; every unregistered root, media, name, alternate-data stream, hard-link alias, budget excess, retention excess or business/customer-attributable byte is a failure. Retirement requires the row's authenticated HDD/off-host copy and current TPM/head proof first. Exact purpose/media pairs are: `RuntimeSsdScanScopeV1` → `EP-F57-RUNTIME-SSD-SCAN-SCOPE-V1` / `application/vnd.ep.f57-runtime-ssd-scan-scope-v1+json`; `RuntimeSsdPersistenceLocatorSetV1` → `EP-F57-RUNTIME-SSD-PERSISTENCE-LOCATOR-SET-V1` / `application/vnd.ep.f57-runtime-ssd-persistence-locator-set-v1+json`; `RuntimeSsdBusinessSignatureSetV1` → `EP-F57-RUNTIME-SSD-BUSINESS-SIGNATURE-SET-V1` / `application/vnd.ep.f57-runtime-ssd-business-signature-set-v1+json`; `RuntimeSsdExceptionRetentionReadbackV1` → `EP-F57-RUNTIME-SSD-EXCEPTION-RETENTION-READBACK-V1` / `application/vnd.ep.f57-runtime-ssd-exception-retention-readback-v1+json`; Their schemas deny unknown fields, bind every `ArtifactRefV1` to only its stated media and are owned beside the runtime policy schema; wrong-media and missing-object negatives are mandatory.

The signed Residency object exact-loads the registry, scope, complete locator set and resolution readback, reproducible inventory, four accepted entry sets, rejected entry set, Windows policy readback, whole-volume classification, every rebuild rehearsal and every digest. The offline verifier re-enumerates or, when evaluating a frozen evidence bundle, recomputes from every complete `RuntimeSsdScanEntryV1`: logical path, final-handle path/volume, file ID, complete hard-link set, ADS name, logical/allocated size, content hash, media and source binding. It then independently maps each accepted entry to Set A or one of the twenty exact Set-B path rows, recomputes per-object/instance/class budgets and retention, and requires the rejected set empty plus `unregistered_persistent_entry_count=inaccessible_entry_count=partial_enumeration_count=0`. A zero summary without the referenced canonical entry bytes is invalid. SSD-loss rehearsal installs only the immutable launcher/MSI, reconstructs the four rows from the closed rebuild authorities, and proves service readiness without treating any SSD byte as the sole copy.

The scan has two disjoint coverage sets rather than pretending an installed Windows volume contains only four roots. Set A is the signed `RuntimeSsdReproducibleRuntimeInventoryV1`: clean Windows component/catalog files, the immutable launcher/MSI installation and explicitly bounded OS runtime caches that are reconstructible and forbidden to contain customer fields. Set B is exactly the four mutable exception rules above. `runtime_ssd_scan_scope_ref` freezes the whole-volume identity, complete product roots and a typed locator-set ref/digest; its resolution readback carries every concrete product namespace, service working directory, paging/dump/WER/quarantine/VSS, Event Log/ETL, Defender-history and firewall/HTTP-log path derived from the actual registry/provider/channel configuration. `unregistered_persistent_entry_count=0` is evaluated over all product namespaces and those complete resolved locators after subtracting byte-exact Set A and Set B; it does not misclassify unrelated catalog-verified Windows servicing files. Independently, the referenced whole-volume allocation/content-classification readback scans all allocated streams and exact-references the same accepted/rejected sets, registered customer canaries, known authority-object digests and business-data signatures; PASS requires `rejected_or_unclassified_allocated_bytes=customer_authority_match_bytes=customer_canary_match_count=known_business_digest_match_count=inaccessible_entry_count=partial_enumeration_count=0` and derives `runtime_ssd_customer_authority_bytes=0`. Set overlap, an unclassified product/persistence entry, a Set-A byte/catalog mismatch, VSS/hard-link/ADS escape, inaccessible directory or scanner partial failure fails closed.

Windows itself may not create a hidden fifth exception. The installed policy and post-reboot `WindowsPersistentFilePolicyReadbackV1` contain exactly eight rows sorted by kind, and each row carries the displayed strict tagged observed-details union rather than only a digest. `PAGE_FILE`, `SWAP_FILE`, `HIBERNATION_FILE`, `KERNEL_OR_FULL_CRASH_DUMP`, `MINI_DUMP`, and `WER_LOCAL_DUMP` are all `DISABLED`; this avoids relying on a DATA_HDD pagefile before the certificate-protected HDD can be unlocked. `VSS_DIFF_AREA` is configured only on the verified DATA_HDD and its readback names every provider, association and final-handle-resolved extent; no shadow copy or diff area is permitted on RUNTIME_SSD. `PRODUCT_MALWARE_QUARANTINE` resolves to one storage-manifest DATA_HDD quarantine root and carries the full scanner/exclusion/pipeline/root observation. MSI/Task 15 sets `PagingFiles=[]`, disables automatic managed pagefiles and `SwapfileControl`, hibernation, crash dumps and both global/per-executable WER LocalDumps, clears every dump locator, fixes VSS shadow storage to DATA_HDD, and configures the product scanner's quarantine there before reboot. The exact no-pagefile profile is release-valid only when the 72-hour 20-user P340 run observes physical RAM `34359738368`, system commit limit at least `32212254720`, peak commit charge and every sample's committed bytes at most `25769803776`, working set at most `17179869184`, no commit-allocation failure, no OOM/SCM restart and zero hard-fault counter reset; a pagefile on either disk or a lower headroom result fails certification and admission.

Defender remains enabled for Windows and installed code, but the exact storage-manifest customer-authority roots are a generated, digest-bound Defender exclusion set because those roots are scanned by the product's controlled malware pipeline; the product pipeline quarantines only into the DATA_HDD root and returns an immutable scan result to the command/effect flow. No wildcard, parent-volume or caller-selected exclusion is legal. The readback exact-compares exclusions with the complete current customer-root set and proves real-time protection for every non-excluded OS/code root. It then verifies the explicit registry values, `powercfg /a`, VSS provider/association/extent identities, Defender/exclusion state, product-quarantine final handle and actual file absence across both fixed volumes after reboot. A `pagefile.sys|swapfile.sys|hiberfil.sys|MEMORY.DMP`, any dump/quarantine/diff-area on SSD, overbroad/stale Defender exclusion, an unverified drive-letter alias, or policy/file disagreement makes Residency, P340 and production admission fail; none becomes an SSD exception.

OS telemetry is not an undeclared persistence escape. Generated `WindowsOsTelemetryDataMinimizationPolicyV1` has exact purpose/media `EP-F57-WINDOWS-OS-TELEMETRY-DATA-MINIMIZATION-POLICY-V1` / `application/vnd.ep.f57-windows-os-telemetry-data-minimization-policy-v1+json`, one storage-manifest policy pin `windows-os-telemetry-data-minimization-policy-sha256:<digest>`, and exactly the seven rows below in enum order. An SSD-resident row permits only its fixed no-customer-field schema and bounded retention; customer IDs, names, email/phone, customer-derived free text, client IP tied to a customer, HDD attachment/quarantine path and business-object IDs are forbidden. Every customer-bearing audit/access event is written directly through the Authority audit pipeline to DATA_HDD. The post-reboot locator readback records every effective channel/session/path and the whole-volume negative probe injects registered canaries and known IDs through product HTTP, Task, Defender and firewall paths; any hit in an SSD stream fails Residency and admission. This policy reduces what Windows may record; it does not add a fifth mutable SSD exception.

| Channel kind | Exact channel/session or disposition | Placement and exact cap |
|---|---|---|
| `PRODUCT_OPERATIONAL_EVENT_LOG` | `EnterprisePlatform-F57/Operational`; generated no-customer-field schema | `RUNTIME_SSD_BOUNDED_NO_CUSTOMER_FIELDS`, `67108864` bytes |
| `PRODUCT_OPERATIONAL_ETL` | `EnterprisePlatform-F57-Operational`; generated no-customer-field schema | `RUNTIME_SSD_BOUNDED_NO_CUSTOMER_FIELDS`, `67108864` bytes |
| `RECOVERY_TASK_OPERATIONAL_EVENT_LOG` | `Microsoft-Windows-TaskScheduler/Operational`; product task emits only operation ID/status | `RUNTIME_SSD_BOUNDED_NO_CUSTOMER_FIELDS`, `33554432` bytes |
| `DEFENDER_OPERATIONAL_AND_HISTORY` | Defender operational/history with exact manifest customer roots excluded and product scanner covering those roots | `RUNTIME_SSD_BOUNDED_NO_CUSTOMER_FIELDS`, `268435456` bytes |
| `WINDOWS_FIREWALL_TEXT_LOG` | text logging disabled for domain/private/public profiles; ETW remains no-customer probe-covered | `DISABLED`, `0` bytes |
| `HTTP_SERVICE_ERROR_LOG` | HTTP.sys `ErrorLoggingDir` fixed below the manifest-derived DATA_HDD system-telemetry root | `DATA_HDD`, `268435456` bytes |
| `AUTHORITY_HTTP_ACCESS_AUDIT` | Authority structured access/audit pipeline below the manifest-derived DATA_HDD audit root | `DATA_HDD`, storage-manifest retention/budget |

Every SSD row has a nonnull content-addressed `allowed_field_schema_ref`; DATA_HDD/disabled rows have null. The readback exact-checks all seven rows, Windows channel/session/registry configuration, maximum size, final-handle volume, Defender exclusions and HTTP.sys restart application; `unregistered_channel_or_session_count=0` and every canary/business-digest match count is zero. Firewall text-log files must be absent, not merely have logging disabled. A channel that cannot meet its exact schema/cap must be moved to the DATA_HDD system-telemetry root by a reviewed policy revision or disabled; silently accepting its default SSD path is forbidden.

The only legal definition is deterministic, non-expiring `P340CertificationPolicyDefinitionV1` at `docs/generated/f57/policy/p340-certification-policy.v1.json`, media `application/vnd.ep.f57-p340-certification-policy-definition-v1+json`, purpose `EP-F57-P340-CERTIFICATION-POLICY-DEFINITION-V1`, and ID `F57_P340_CERTIFICATION_POLICY_V1`. It belongs to the exact 30-family closed projection set and its exact digest is therefore candidate-bound without embedding time. Immediately before the input manifest and before physical STARTED, the fixed P340 policy signer issues one `P340CertificationPolicyAttestationV1` with media `application/vnd.ep.f57-p340-certification-policy-attestation-v1+json`, purpose `EP-F57-P340-CERTIFICATION-POLICY-ATTESTATION-V1`, the exact definition/candidate/projection refs and the common 90-day cap. The input manifest, carrier staging plan, outer soak and ten nested bindings point to this attestation, whose definition ref typed-loads the projection member. For the policy attestation, capacity-input manifest and all seven pre-start helpers, the payload `issued_at_unix_ms` or `generated_at_unix_ms` is captured before hashing; its actual trusted CMS/RFC-3161 signing time must lie in the common signing-interface window `[payload_time,min(payload_time+300000,payload_expiry)]`, never equal a time learned after signing. Each payload time and trusted signing time is `<=TEST_STARTED.recorded_at_unix_ms`, every expiry covers `context.finished_at_unix_ms`, and `expiry<=payload_time+7776000000` under checked arithmetic. The input exact-loads each helper and the policy; all candidate/host/config refs and expiry minima agree. A future/pre-STARTED violation, expired-mid-soak input, CMS-window drift, cross-attempt ref or arithmetic overflow fails before PASS. Definition values are frozen: `continuous_duration_seconds=259200`, `sample_period_seconds=60`, `maximum_gap_seconds=120`, the exact complete set of all 25 displayed `P340RequiredMetricV1` variants, read P95 `<=2000 ms`, write P95 `<=3000 ms`, accepted heavy-report admission `<=2000 ms`, background heavy-report concurrency `=1`, per capacity-relevant table minimum `10000` rows, at least `10000` attachments totaling `53687091200` bytes with every one of the three size buckets nonzero, index bytes `>=5368709120`, WAL bytes `>=2147483648`, initial HDD used ratio in inclusive basis points `3500..=7000`, SSD remaining life `>=20%`, at least one complete memory-test pass with zero errors, SSD clean reinstall plus authority restore `<=28800` seconds, data HDD exactly `CMR` with manufacturer workload rating `>=55 TB/year` and warranty valid through evidence expiry, scanner-definition age `<=259200` seconds, absolute W32Time offset `<=1000 ms`, last successful sync age `<=900` seconds, and maximum CPU/SSD/HDD temperatures `85000/70000/55000` millicelsius. A changed threshold, omitted metric, self-issued definition, wrong projection member or unbound attestation is not a configurable alternative; it is a different unsupported profile and fails.

The remaining capacity budgets are equally fixed, not evaluator choices: `maximum_error_count=0`; CPU utilization P95 `<=8500` basis points and every sample `<=9500`; working set `<=17179869184` bytes; committed memory `<=25769803776` bytes; adjacent-sample hard-page-fault delta `<=3000`; HDD read/write P95 `<=100/200 ms`; HDD queue P95/max `<=4/16`; HDD free space always `>=1500` basis points of total; runtime SSD free `>=42949672960` bytes with Windows update/rollback budget `>=21474836480` bytes; runtime SSD capacity `>=240000000000` bytes and data HDD capacity `>=1000000000000` bytes. PostgreSQL configured maximum is `<=64`, active connections `<=48` and also `active<=maximum`, commit P95 `<=500 ms`, waiting locks `<=4`, long transactions `=0`, and checkpoint age `<=900 s`. HTTP/worker/plugin queue depths are `<=40/200/40`. Automation due/running/unknown are `<=1000/64/0`; the policy fixes `maximum_automation_retry_basis_points=100`, the final cumulative accepted-command count must be positive, and at every sample checked `u128` requires `retry_count*10000 <= policy.maximum_automation_retry_basis_points*accepted_command_count`; `accepted_command_count=0` permits only `retry_count=0`. Latest backup age/replication lag are `<=900/300 s`; audit checkpoint age/pending count are `<=300 s/100`; UPS is online and communication-healthy with runtime `>=900 s`; Control Center response P95/queue are `<=2000 ms/10`. These numbers populate the correspondingly named policy fields exactly, and goldens include equality, one retry over, `0/0`, retry-positive/accepted-zero, final accepted zero and every cross-product overflow.

All P340 evaluator arithmetic is fail-closed and independent of compiler overflow mode. Every nonnegative add, subtract, multiply, sum, histogram merge, ratio cross-product, ceiling division and rank calculation first promotes operands to checked `u128`; subtraction first proves the left operand is not smaller. Signed timestamp/offset arithmetic uses checked `i128`. A value is downcast only after proving the destination range, and no saturating, wrapping, floating-point or build-profile-dependent operation is allowed. Overflow, underflow or failed downcast returns the single code `P340_ARITHMETIC_OVERFLOW` before any PASS can be formed. Boundary goldens include `u64::MAX` for retry ratios, 90-day row floors, attachment bucket sums, histogram bucket/frame merges, HDD watermarks and growth, plus `i64::MIN|MAX` time/offset vectors.

Every one of the 25 required metric variants has one deterministic predicate: principal/action/overlay variants equal the frozen mixes; latency uses merged histograms. In every frame, read/write histogram operation counts are at least the corresponding `ActionMix` values, `ErrorRate.high_risk_completed_count>=ActionMix.high_risk_commands`, and `ErrorRate.attachment_completed_count>=ActionMix.attachment_operations`; checked `u128` then requires `ErrorRate.operation_count=read_histogram.operation_count+write_histogram.operation_count+high_risk_completed_count+attachment_completed_count`, `operation_count>0`, `error_count<=operation_count`, and `error_basis_points=min(10000,ceil(error_count*10000/operation_count))`, followed by the release requirement of zero errors. CPU P95 is the one-based nearest-rank value at `ceil(95*N/100)` after numeric ascending sort, while memory uses the scalar budgets; `PageFaults` starts at cumulative zero, never decreases, and every checked adjacent delta is within policy. HDD latency/queue use their bounds, every queue row additionally requires `depth_p95<=depth_max`, and read/write throughput are each positive. For every `HddFreeAndGrowth` frame, checked arithmetic requires `free_bytes+used_bytes=input.hdd_total_bytes`, `free_bytes*10000 >= policy.minimum_hdd_free_basis_points*input.hdd_total_bytes` in `u128`, and `projected_daily_growth_bytes == max(input.p95_daily_growth_bytes_30d,input.p95_daily_growth_bytes_90d)`; that same maximum equals the watermark's `p95_daily_growth_bytes`, while `minimum_free_bytes=min(all frame free_bytes)`, `maximum_used_bytes=max(all frame used_bytes)`, and both watermark/input totals exact-match. Every `SsdHealth` frame requires `policy.minimum_ssd_remaining_life_percent<=remaining_life_percent<=100`, `0<windows_update_rollback_budget_bytes<=free_bytes<=RUNTIME_SSD.volume_total_bytes`, and both free/rollback policy floors; SSD/HDD health also requires zero media/bad-sector/interface/timeout/drop/retry counters, and all temperature samples meet their limits. PostgreSQL values meet connection/commit/lock/checkpoint bounds, require `active<=maximum`, and treat WAL as attempt-relative cumulative evidence: sample 1 is exactly zero, every later value is nondecreasing, and the final value is strictly positive. All three queues meet their bounds; automation cumulative counters start at zero, remain monotonic and meet exact-once/retry bounds, with final accepted count positive; backup, audit, UPS and Control Center meet their bounds in every sample; `HeavyReportAdmission` requires `accepted=true`, decision time within policy and background concurrency exactly one. The HDD watermark additionally requires `minimum_free_bytes >= yellow_free_bytes > red_free_bytes >= emergency_reserve_bytes`, `maximum_used_bytes = total_bytes - minimum_free_bytes`, and `minimum_free_bytes >= emergency_reserve_bytes + 30*p95_daily_growth_bytes`. No required metric is informational or presence-only. Generated evaluator goldens cover equality at every boundary plus one-beyond failure for every scalar and relational predicate, including operation-count omission/double-count, completed-count below action mix, WAL nonzero at sample 1/reset/zero final, `depth_p95>depth_max`, SSD `101%`, free-above-volume, rollback-above-free, and `active=48,maximum=1` rejection.

Before `P340_RELEASE72_HOUR` STARTED, and only after the exact qualification closure/checkpoint above, the trusted release-hardware assessor creates and signs one `P340CapacityInputManifestV1` with media `application/vnd.ep.f57-p340-capacity-input-manifest-v1+json` and purpose `EP-F57-P340-CAPACITY-INPUT-MANIFEST-V1`, stores it content-addressed, and binds its ref plus the policy-attestation ref into the signed carrier staging plan; STARTED carries only that plan ref. It exact-loads `qualification_plan_ref`, requires `qualification_checkpoint_ref` to authenticate the one same-plan `P340QualificationClosureBound`, and exact-joins its seven helper refs/kinds/attempt IDs to that closure. It binds the final signed candidate and projection, PostgreSQL `server_version_num` in major 16 and exact build digest, software/config generations, complete graph-derived `capacity_relevant=true` table set, attachment distribution, index/WAL sizes, HDD used/total bytes, complete graph-derived queue initial set, host fingerprint, and the exact pre-start patch/custody/UPS/power-policy/HDD-flush/memory/SSD-restore supporting refs. `capacity_history_kind` is exactly `QUALIFICATION_SYNTHETIC`: this qualifies the frozen P340 test dataset and must never be represented as observed customer/site history. `capacity_history` contains exactly 90 canonical ascending, consecutive, complete UTC dates ending on the UTC date immediately before the date containing TEST_STARTED; each day contains the exact graph-derived capacity-table set once plus one HDD-growth value. The last 30 rows are the sole 30-day suffix. For each table and for HDD growth, the evaluator independently sorts the 30- and 90-value series and recomputes the one-based nearest-rank P95 at `ceil(95*N/100)`; the manifest's table and HDD P95 scalars must equal those recomputations and be positive. Missing/duplicate/nonconsecutive dates, a missing table/day, local-time alias, zero/misranked value, stale/nonextending qualification checkpoint or `SITE_OBSERVED` claim fails.

Every table requires `row_count>=max(10000,90*p95_daily_insert_count_90d)` and both recomputed insert P95 values greater than zero; attachment buckets sum exactly to count. Initial HDD ratio uses no rounded intermediate value: checked `u128` requires `hdd_total_bytes>0`, `hdd_used_bytes<=hdd_total_bytes`, `hdd_used_bytes*10000 >= 3500*hdd_total_bytes`, and `hdd_used_bytes*10000 <= 7000*hdd_total_bytes`; overflow or any failed inequality hard-fails, and goldens cover both inclusive boundaries plus one byte below/above. All other byte floors meet policy. The typed memory row exact-matches the repeated tool/pass/error/completion fields, tests all `34359738368` RAM bytes, has at least one full pass, zero errors and remains valid through finish. The SSD clean-restore row exact-matches duration/target and passes within `28800` seconds. The pre-start HDD flush row exact-matches the DATA_HDD and host fingerprint, passes its controlled power cut, and remains valid through finish. Empty/small/low-fill/no-growth/unknown-table/unknown-queue input, stale helper evidence, SMR/unknown recording technology, unknown or sub-55 TB/year HDD rating, or warranty ending before evidence expiry fails before the physical load starts.

`host_fingerprint_sha256` is exactly `sha256(JCS(host_fingerprint_input))`. The input contains the exact P340 profile, SMBIOS system UUID, raw normalized WMI CPU identity plus typed CPU SKU, canonical-sorted complete RAM-module identities, exact two tagged storage devices with role/model/serial/firmware/raw-device-capacity/volume-total/controller/volume identities plus CMR/rating/warranty for the HDD, storage-controller driver, Windows build/UBR, scanner provider and policy digest, UPS adapter, software generation, configuration generation and configuration-set digest. The frozen CPU canonicalizer removes only the enumerated trademark tokens and clock suffix, normalizes ASCII case/space, and maps the real WMI name golden `Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-10500 CPU @ 3.10GHz` to exactly `INTEL_CORE_I5_10500`; outer `cpu_sku` must match, while an i5-10400/10500T/10600 or ambiguous identity is rejected. RAM module identities are nonempty and unique, and their checked `u128` capacity sum is exactly `34359738368`, equal to outer `ram_bytes`.

Storage roles are exactly `{RUNTIME_SSD,DATA_HDD}`. `raw_device_capacity_bytes` is the physical-device size and `volume_total_bytes` is the certified NTFS volume size; for each role checked arithmetic requires `raw_device_capacity_bytes>=volume_total_bytes>0`. Only raw capacity is compared to the fixed `240000000000/1000000000000` SSD/HDD device floors. Each `volume_total_bytes` exact-matches the same role's filesystem-geometry row. `input.hdd_total_bytes` exact-matches DATA_HDD `volume_total_bytes`, every watermark `total_bytes`, and every frame's checked `free_bytes+used_bytes`; sample 1 additionally requires `used_bytes=input.hdd_used_bytes` and `free_bytes=input.hdd_total_bytes-input.hdd_used_bytes`, and all 4321 frames keep the volume total stable. The outer context, input manifest, capacity certificate and final readbacks exact-repeat the host digest; UPS identity exact-matches `ups_adapter_identity`. A raw-vs-volume inversion/drift, RAM sum/duplicate, CPU canonicalization mismatch, sample-1 drift, capacity/role mismatch, or any model/serial/firmware/controller/driver/CMR/rating/warranty/Windows/scanner/UPS/generation/configuration/volume change invalidates the attempt and requires a new profile-aware certification; it cannot be masked by retaining an old hash.

The Windows readback exact-repeats the pre-start patch-attestation ref, requires Windows Server 2022, Defender realtime protection and WDAC enforcement, and exact-matches `scanner_provider_identity` plus `scanner_policy_sha256` to the host fingerprint. Scanner provider and engine version are nonempty, policy and definition digests are nonzero, and the definition digest is the exact bytes whose authenticated metadata supplies `scanner_definition_issued_at_unix_ms`. The evaluator recomputes scanner definition age from the common trusted finish time without a rounding loophole: `finish>=definition_issued`, checked `delta_ms=finish-definition_issued`, and `scanner_definition_age_seconds=ceil(delta_ms/1000)` before applying the policy maximum. W32Time uses checked `abs(i128::from(w32time_offset_milliseconds))<=1000`; `i64::MIN`, overflow, an empty source, future definition, mismatched claimed age or stale last-sync age fails. Both rollback/fast-forward negatives must PASS. Its nonempty `windows_boot_id` must byte-equal the outer soak, workload aggregate and every one of 4321 sample rows. Boot security requires TPM 2.x ready, physical-presence protection for clear, `approved_boot_entry_ids == observed_boot_entry_ids`, `observed_boot_order[0] == windows_boot_manager_entry_id`, no unapproved entry, USB/external-media and PXE boot disabled, Intel AMT exactly `DISABLED_UNCONFIGURED`, BIOS `ac_power_recovery_mode=POWER_ON`, nonzero dual-custody record digest, a present tamper control with passing inspection, removable-device default deny, AutoRun disabled, and the BadUSB negative PASS. The BitLocker custody ref typed-loads the pre-start attestation, exact-matches both certified volume identities, requires quorum `2`, at least two distinct custodian domains and `contains_recovery_material=false`; its schema denies password, key, recovery-secret and blob fields, and no recovery material is copied into the evidence bundle. `ResidencyReadbackV1.storage_manifest_ref` typed-loads the existing canonical `SignedF57AuthorityStorageManifestV1` under its exact vendor media, not opaque bytes. Both filesystem-volume rows point to the same `UpsPowerWriteCachePolicyV1` later consumed by `POWER_SHUTDOWN`; the HDD SMART row points to the exact input-manifest-bound pre-start `HddFlushVerificationV1`. Provider/policy/engine/definition drift, policy/ref/content disagreement, stale scanner/time state, boot/source drift, an alternate boot entry, enabled AMT, absent or non-`POWER_ON` AC recovery, missing physical control, or generic-octet substitution fails.

The Windows readback requires `product=WINDOWS_SERVER_2022`, `build_number>=20348`, `update_build_revision>0`, and the exact typed `patch_policy_attestation_ref` already frozen by the input manifest and valid at STARTED; it never means ambient “latest”. Boot security requires UEFI Secure Boot enabled, TPM present and ready, TPM `2.0`, and a nonempty measured-boot log ref from the same boot in addition to the closed boot/AMT/tamper/USB controls below. BitLocker requires exactly two distinct volume identities with roles `{RUNTIME_SSD,DATA_HDD}`: both are `XTS_AES_256`, `FULLY_ENCRYPTED`, protection `ON`, and `100` percent; the runtime SSD protector set is exactly `{TPM,RECOVERY_PASSWORD}`, and DATA_HDD exactly `{PUBLIC_KEY,RECOVERY_PASSWORD}`. `GetKeyProtectors(7)`, `GetKeyProtectorCertificate`, certificate DER/SPKI/thumbprint and the authority's protector ID must all identify the same PUBLIC_KEY row. `recovery_custody_attestation_ref` exact-loads the no-secret, quorum-two off-host recovery-password custody proof.

The pre-HDD bootstrap locator set is build/MSI-fixed and has no discovery path: registry `C:\Program Files\EnterprisePlatform\Authority\bootstrap\data-hdd-unlock-trust-registry.v1.json`; authority `C:\ProgramData\EnterprisePlatform\Bootstrap\data-hdd-unlock-authority.v1.json`; public object root `C:\ProgramData\EnterprisePlatform\Bootstrap\data-hdd-unlock\objects\sha256`; immutable product-pinned artifact-registry trust bundle, revocation snapshot and monotonic checkpoint under `C:\Program Files\EnterprisePlatform\Authority\bootstrap\trust\`; and the distinct unlock-certificate CA bundle `unlock-certificate-ca-chain.p7b`, revocation snapshot `unlock-certificate-revocation.bin` and checkpoint `unlock-certificate-checkpoint.bin` in that directory. Exact maximums are registry `1048576`, authority `1048576`, and public-object total `16777216` bytes. `runtime-ssd-bootstrap://data-hdd-unlock/objects/sha256/<64-lowerhex>` is the sole resolver for every authority-nested public ref and final-handle proves the fixed SSD volume, no reparse/ADS/hard-link escape and exact bytes. Every unlock-certificate trust ref/digest in policy, authority and readback resolves only to those three fixed files and freezes the accepted leaf-to-root SPKI path; it is not the artifact-signing registry. The signed bootstrap registry has exactly one row: artifact kind `DATA_HDD_BITLOCKER_UNLOCK_AUTHORITY_V1`, authority media, signer subject `EP_F57_DATA_HDD_UNLOCK_AUTHORITY_V1`, exact deployment signer DN/SPKI and `CURRENT_AT_VERIFICATION`; the registry envelope itself verifies only under the locator-set product-pinned root/SPKI, archived chain, revocation snapshot and checkpoint. Registry revision and authority epoch must be positive, nondecreasing and exact-match the separate policy-protected TPM NV anti-rollback tuple. The Microsoft Platform Crypto Provider key is a persisted CNG key plus TPM-backed attestation—not a claimed TPM NV sealed object; the **different** TPM NV index stores only `(deployment_id,authority_epoch,authority-envelope-sha256)` anti-rollback state.

The locator set is generated at docs/generated/f57/security/data-hdd-unlock-bootstrap-locator-set.v1.json with purpose/media EP-F57-DATA-HDD-UNLOCK-BOOTSTRAP-LOCATOR-SET-V1 / application/vnd.ep.f57-data-hdd-unlock-bootstrap-locator-set-v1+json and is the nonnull data_hdd_unlock_bootstrap_locator_set_ref only on the unlock-broker install row. Its nine literal rows are: C:\Program Files\EnterprisePlatform\Authority\bootstrap\data-hdd-unlock-trust-registry.v1.json; C:\ProgramData\EnterprisePlatform\Bootstrap\data-hdd-unlock-authority.v1.json; C:\ProgramData\EnterprisePlatform\Bootstrap\data-hdd-unlock\objects\sha256; C:\Program Files\EnterprisePlatform\Authority\bootstrap\trust\registry-trust-bundle.p7b; registry-revocation.bin; registry-checkpoint.bin; unlock-certificate-ca-chain.p7b; unlock-certificate-revocation.bin; and unlock-certificate-checkpoint.bin. The last six filenames share that exact trust directory; concatenation, environment substitution, alternate drive, 8.3 alias and discovery are forbidden. Registry/authority/public-object limits are 1048576/1048576/16777216 bytes; each trust bundle/revocation snapshot is at most 4194304 bytes and each checkpoint at most 65536 bytes. JSON rows use their exact vendor media, both P7B files application/pkcs7-mime, revocation files application/vnd.ep.revocation-snapshot-v1, checkpoints application/vnd.ep.monotonic-checkpoint-v1, and the directory row has no media/content ref. SYSTEM owns each protected descriptor; the leaf files grant SYSTEM full and only broker/AS read, the two roots use the equivalent inherited read/traverse ACEs, and no non-SYSTEM principal receives create/delete/write-DAC/write-owner. MSI is the sole installer/projector; post-reboot DataHddUnlockBootstrapLocatorResolutionReadbackV1, purpose/media EP-F57-DATA-HDD-UNLOCK-BOOTSTRAP-LOCATOR-RESOLUTION-READBACK-V1 / application/vnd.ep.f57-data-hdd-unlock-bootstrap-locator-resolution-readback-v1+json, final-handle checks exactly nine rows, SSD volume, file IDs, descriptors, media/digests, zero reparse/ADS, hard-link policy and zero unregistered locators. These bytes are bounded no-customer Set-A entries in RuntimeSsdReproducibleRuntimeInventoryV1, reconstructible from signed build/off-host custody and never a fifth mutable exception; each replacement is an immutable verified revision projected atomically by SYSTEM.

`DataHddBitLockerCertificatePolicyV1` has exactly four ordered registry requirements under 64-bit `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\FVE`: DWORD `FDVAllowUserCert=1`, DWORD `FDVEnforceUserCert=0`, string `CertificateOID=1.3.6.1.4.1.311.67.1.1`, and string `IdentificationField=EP-F57-<lowercase-hyphenated-deployment-id>`. The provisioning and every boot collect a fresh `DataHddBitLockerCertificatePolicyReadbackV1`; authority binds the policy plus provisioning readback, while unlock readback binds the current readback and exact-compares all rows and certificate/provider properties before effect. The referenced chain policy has purpose/media `EP-F57-DATA-HDD-UNLOCK-CERTIFICATE-CHAIN-TRUST-POLICY-V1` / `application/vnd.ep.f57-data-hdd-unlock-certificate-chain-trust-policy-v1+json` and fixes exclusive pinned-root mode, no network URL retrieval, cached revocation `CHAIN_EXCLUDE_ROOT`, required trust status zero, canonical unique allowed-root SPKI set count `1..=8` and `maximum_chain_length=8`. The exact purpose/media registry is: locator set `EP-F57-DATA-HDD-UNLOCK-BOOTSTRAP-LOCATOR-SET-V1` / `application/vnd.ep.f57-data-hdd-unlock-bootstrap-locator-set-v1+json`; signed bootstrap registry `EP-F57-DATA-HDD-UNLOCK-BOOTSTRAP-TRUST-REGISTRY-V1` / `application/vnd.ep.f57-data-hdd-unlock-bootstrap-trust-registry-v1+json`; certificate policy `EP-F57-DATA-HDD-BITLOCKER-CERTIFICATE-POLICY-V1` / `application/vnd.ep.f57-data-hdd-bitlocker-certificate-policy-v1+json`; policy readback `EP-F57-DATA-HDD-BITLOCKER-CERTIFICATE-POLICY-READBACK-V1` / `application/vnd.ep.f57-data-hdd-bitlocker-certificate-policy-readback-v1+json`; broker bootstrap readback `EP-F57-DATA-HDD-UNLOCK-BROKER-BOOTSTRAP-READBACK-V1` / `application/vnd.ep.f57-data-hdd-unlock-broker-bootstrap-readback-v1+json`. The unlock authority/readback purpose/media are respectively `EP-F57-DATA-HDD-BITLOCKER-UNLOCK-AUTHORITY-V1` / `application/vnd.ep.f57-data-hdd-bitlocker-unlock-authority-v1+json` and `EP-F57-DATA-HDD-BITLOCKER-UNLOCK-READBACK-V1` / `application/vnd.ep.f57-data-hdd-bitlocker-unlock-readback-v1+json`. The sole owner is `crates/platform/backup/src/windows_components/unlock.rs` with strict schema `docs/evidence/f57-data-hdd-bitlocker-unlock.v1.schema.json`; Task 11 owns broker build/install while Task 13 imports, collects and verifies these wires. The authority is registry-signed; the readback is strict plain JCS authenticated by broker IPC, stored create-new on DATA_HDD and authenticated offline only through its enclosing signed install/POWER/P340 evidence. Bootstrap readback also requires enabled normal-token `BUILTIN\Administrators`, the Windows-defined restricted-token projection and provider qualification return code `0`. Readback requires explicit nonzero thumbprint, empty PIN, return code `0`, auto-unlock false, export/leak counts zero, exact NV head, unlocked+mounted+dirty-clear and the expected volume identity. Clean-SSD/P340 follows the two-person recovery-and-reenrollment contract above rather than pretending the lost CNG provider binding can be reconstructed from public bytes.

Residency exact-matches the same two volume identities and the signed storage manifest. Its complete canonical `customer_authority_data_roots` set is derived from that manifest and every PostgreSQL data/WAL, attachment, audit, Outbox, search index, working-file, attributable generated-data root, global architecture-authority archive root, and G6 release-evidence root must resolve to the HDD volume. The P340 outer `storage_root_binding` byte-equals the G6 journal header and final candidate; Residency's manifest/volume fields plus canonical roots and the DATA_HDD geometry row independently reconstruct and exact-match that tuple before the evaluator may upgrade it from `VERIFIED_DATA_HDD_ROOT` to `CERTIFIED_DATA_HDD`. For PASS, `runtime_ssd_customer_authority_bytes=0` and `violations=[]`; the SSD may contain Windows Server and only reproducible or closed control/code bytes. The residency scanner uses one generated tagged exception registry whose complete set is exactly `POWER_CONTROL_CAPSULE|PACKAGE_RECOVERY_CONTINUATION_CAPSULE|AUTHORITY_KERNEL_SLOT_POINTER_AND_JOURNAL_HEAD|RECONSTRUCTIBLE_SIGNED_NATIVE_CODE_SLOT_OR_CACHE`. POWER retains its independent `33554432`-byte cap and closed filenames/media; the package capsule, pointer/head and code-slot/cache rows each carry their own nonzero maximum size, literal non-reparse root, allowed media, terminal/retention predicate and reconstruction source. The two capsule classes must be retired after terminal off-host/HDD proof; pointer/head must match the TPM/DATA_HDD/off-host monotonic quorum; code slots/cache must be content-addressed, Authenticode/SBOM-bound and disposable. None may contain customer fields or serve as authoritative state. An unknown fifth class, business-data signature, extra descendant, size/retention breach, terminally orphaned activation, unverified code or scanner/registry drift fails. File-system geometry contains the same exact two roles and identities, both `GPT`/`NTFS`; each `volume_total_bytes` exact-matches its host-fingerprint storage row, logical and physical sectors are powers of two in `512..=4096`, physical is not smaller than logical, and cluster size is a power-of-two multiple of physical sector size in `4096..=65536`. Both rows exact-load the same signed UPS policy; their `write_cache_enabled` values respectively equal `runtime_ssd_write_cache_enabled` and `data_hdd_write_cache_enabled`. If the HDD cache is enabled, the policy must require power-loss flush and the input-manifest-bound same-host/same-serial pre-start HDD flush qualification must PASS and remain valid through finish. Both SMART `device_health_passed` fields must be true only after their underlying predicates pass; a helper Boolean can never override a failed field. Any cache/policy/role/capacity/exception/root-binding mismatch or enabled unprotected cache fails.

The workload sample object is UTF-8/no-BOM and uses exactly the same `<8 lowercase hex byte length>\t<JCS row bytes>\n` framing rule as the journals. It contains exactly `4321` samples with sequence `1..=4321`; `scheduled_at_unix_ms = context.started_at_unix_ms + (sequence-1)*60000` is evaluated in checked `i128` and range-checked back to `i64`, so the first and last scheduled points equal the common start and finish. Actual `observed_at_unix_ms` must be within `±5000 ms` of its scheduled point using checked signed subtraction, remain strictly increasing and never leave the interval. At sample 1 the sampler freezes the nonempty Windows boot ID, nonempty boot-scoped monotonic-source ID and that source's baseline tick; `monotonic_elapsed_ms=0`. Every later row repeats both IDs and stores the checked, frequency-normalized millisecond delta from that same baseline tick, which must strictly increase; a reboot, source switch, tick rollback, frequency drift, overflow or wall-clock-only substitute fails. The workload aggregate repeats the two IDs, and its boot ID byte-equals the Windows readback and outer soak. Sequence 1 uses the all-zero SHA-256 predecessor; every later `previous_frame_sha256` hashes the prior complete framed bytes including length, tab and LF, and `sample_chain_root_sha256` hashes the final complete frame. Each sample contains the exact 20 distinct authenticated principal/session rows with 15/3/2 entry counts, a distinct authenticated Control Center session, exact `11/5/2/2` action mix, all overlays and exactly one of every closed tagged metric details variant.

Read/write latency is never stored as an unmergeable per-minute percentile. Each sample stores one `P340LatencyHistogramV1` whose 16 mutually exclusive buckets are exactly `<=1`, `(1,2]`, `(2,5]`, `(5,10]`, `(10,20]`, `(20,50]`, `(50,100]`, `(100,200]`, `(200,500]`, `(500,1000]`, `(1000,1500]`, `(1500,2000]`, `(2000,3000]`, `(3000,5000]`, `(5000,10000]`, and `>10000` milliseconds. Bucket counts sum exactly to `operation_count`; every frame requires read `operation_count>=ActionMix.reads` and write `operation_count>=ActionMix.writes`, so both are strictly positive under the fixed `11/5/2/2` mix. `maximum_ms=0` iff the count is zero and otherwise is consistent with the highest nonempty bucket; a valid P340 frame therefore never takes the zero branch. The evaluator sums matching buckets across all frames, hard-fails if either merged `N=0`, defines P95 as the least finite bucket upper bound whose cumulative count reaches `ceil(95*N/100)`, and treats a percentile landing in `>10000` as failure. All cumulative fields in `AutomationEffects`, the attempt-relative cumulative counters in `SsdHealth`, and `PageFaults.hard_fault_count_cumulative` equal zero in sample 1 and never decrease or reset; `unsafe_shutdown_count_absolute` is deliberately excluded because an older SSD may have a nonzero historical SMART count. That absolute count is constant across all 4321 samples. Scalar SSD remaining-life/free/rollback values are not counters. The final automation accepted-command count must be positive, and the outer accepted/lost/duplicate/unexplained/customer-linked-write summary fields must equal the corresponding final cumulative values. The evaluator recomputes sample count, maximum actual gap, chain root, active barriers, both P95 values, CPU nearest-rank P95, queues, overlays and every reconciliation total from frames; it rejects any summary mismatch. PASS requires read/write P95 within policy, every heavy-report admission accepted within policy at concurrency one, and zero lost accepted command, duplicate effect, unexplained obligation or customer-linked SSD write. Goldens include zero-count, count-below-action-mix, merged-zero, historical unsafe-shutdown count `7->7` PASS and `7->8` FAIL.

SMART contains exactly two distinct tagged device rows, `RUNTIME_SSD` and `DATA_HDD`, whose model/serial/firmware exact-match the input manifest. Both `smart_snapshot_set_ref` values, `P340TemperatureReadbackV1.sensor_series_ref`, and `P340HddWatermarkReadbackV1.watermark_series_ref` must byte-equal the one `P340WorkloadTimeseriesEvidencePayloadV1.samples_ref`; there is no second snapshot/sensor/watermark series or independent parser. The shared framed object supplies the exact 4321 ordered sequence/boot/source/attempt-bound metric rows and the verifier recomputes every readback from it. SSD remaining life/free space/rollback budget equal the interval minima; they also obey `policy minimum<=life<=100` and `0<rollback<=free<=RUNTIME_SSD.volume_total_bytes`. Media/drop/retry fields equal the terminal nondecreasing attempt-relative counters. `P340DeviceHealthReadbackV1::RuntimeSsd.unsafe_shutdown_count` equals the absolute SMART value in sample 1 and sample 4321, and every intermediate `unsafe_shutdown_count_absolute` is byte-equal; a historical nonzero value is allowed but any interval increase fails. HDD free space equals the interval minimum, every health counter equals its terminal nondecreasing value, and the flush ref exact-matches the input manifest's same-host/same-serial pre-start qualification. SSD PASS requires health true, the full bounds above and zero media/drop/retry increases or counts. HDD PASS requires health true, zero reallocated/pending/offline-uncorrectable/interface-CRC/command-timeout/drop/retry counts, nonzero free space and an unexpired PASS typed pre-start flush readback. Temperature maxima are recomputed from all 4321 shared workload rows, every sample is in the structurally valid `0..=policy maximum` millicelsius interval, and no missing/NaN/sentinel sensor value is representable. HDD watermark uses the same rows and checked `u128` to compute `five_percent_bytes=ceil_div(total_bytes*500,10000)`, fixes `twenty_gib_bytes=21474836480`, then recomputes `emergency_reserve_bytes=max(twenty_gib_bytes,five_percent_bytes)`, `yellow_free_bytes=max(2*emergency_reserve_bytes,p95_daily_growth_bytes*30)`, and `red_free_bytes=emergency_reserve_bytes`, followed by proved `u64` downcasts. Its total exact-matches the DATA_HDD volume total and its other values exact-match the shared sample series and input manifest. Goldens cover exact multiples, nonzero remainders that require ceiling, 20-GiB-vs-5% crossover, overflow and failed downcast. A missing/duplicate/out-of-order row, boot/source/attempt drift, any of the four series-ref aliases, missing SSD row, role swap, firmware drift, metric/summary drift, unsafe-shutdown drift, life above 100, free above volume, rollback above free, negative/sentinel temperature, stale update budget or opaque PASS Boolean fails.

The capacity certificate exact-repeats the hardware, storage, workload, candidate, run, host fingerprint and software/config generations from its binding/input; fixes `certified_concurrent_users=20`, `continuous_duration_seconds=259200`, `high_availability_certified=false`, and `outcome=PASS`; and its sorted `measurement_refs` is exactly the five non-certificate security readbacks plus the four typed workload/SMART/temperature/HDD-watermark envelopes.
