Each of those nine refs is distinct, belongs to the same certified interval/host/policy/input, and is typed-verified before the capacity certificate can satisfy the soak. The outer soak exact-matches that certificate and all four repeated measurement refs and itself remains `SINGLE_DISK_DEGRADED_PRODUCTION`; it can never imply RAID, HA, ransomware safety, additional HDD capacity, or customer production admission. Wrong/lax policy, small or drifted input, wrong Windows product/build, absent TPM/Secure Boot, unlocked/weak/partially encrypted volume, recovery material inside the bundle, SSD-resident authority bytes, HDD/SSD identity reversal, missing SSD health, malformed geometry, unprotected write cache, wrong workload/concurrency, a gap/short soak, missing metric, aliased/cross-host/cross-run ref, `high_availability_certified=true`, or any non-PASS nested envelope fails closed.

Before final G6 candidate freeze, the installed `EPAuthorityServer` exposes exactly one authenticated command, `FinalInstalledGenerationAuthorityV1::begin_or_adopt`; xtask is only its client/composition adapter, invoked as `cargo xtask f57 generation activate-installed-release --candidate HEAD --bundle-root <g6-data-hdd-evidence-root> --run-journal <g6-data-hdd-evidence-root>\gate-run.jcs.jsonl`. The public request contains only `{schema_version,candidate_run,precursor_journal_checkpoint_ref,windows_authority_build_result_ref,windows_service_install_result_ref}`. Authority typed-loads the exact terminal same-run build/install chains, five Authority service runtime readbacks, the fixed G0 evidence-signer-broker install/readiness readback, the graph-exact `WindowsRuntimeDeploymentClosureV1|WindowsRuntimeDeploymentReadbackSetV1`, the exact six-row server component set, five on-host component readbacks and the off-host target proof; caller-supplied manifest, item, participant, process list, binary, generation number or topology ref is forbidden. It first proves complete CapabilityGraph participant IDs ↔ complete closure participant IDs ↔ complete readback participant IDs. Under the G1 transition-store lease it then exact-loads the current OBSERVED predecessor, deterministically builds/signs the immediately-next generation and every reverse plan from final installed artifact/file/service/endpoint/component/config identities plus every positive carrier-specific readback, constructs a runtime-topology declaration whose participant IDs exact-equal the graph-`ACTIVE` IDs and whose `database_consumers` independently exact-equal the graph's database-consumer projection for active service identities, and constructs a generation whose canonical item set plus every required participant's `required_item_ids` independently exact-equal the active graph-derived installed-item relation. It persists the manifest/approval/declaration triple and invokes the sole G1 activation coordinator until that exact attempt is durably `OBSERVED_COMMITTED` with one plain ACK per required active participant. An active participant may have zero or multiple consumers and zero or multiple required items; participant-to-item edges may be many-to-many, but every item is referenced and no consumer or item edge falls outside its exact projection. Every `DEFERRED_DISABLED` participant remains represented only by its negative absence readback and is forbidden from artifact, declaration participant, database-consumer, required-participant, participant-item edge and ACK sets; neither the five Authority services nor the backup component set can substitute for the graph-wide closure check. The private `VerifiedFinalInstalledObservedGenerationV1` exposes only attempt/manifest/declaration/ACK refs and is reconstructible only from exact command identity plus transition store—never scan/latest. Every crash cut adopts the exact prefix and cannot create a second attempt, redispatch an already applied item or accept a pre-install/old/desired-only generation. Final freeze must reconstruct and select this exact wrapper; omitted/extra/deferred-present participant, consumer, item or relation edge; orphan item; deferred participant in a positive set; old artifact; wrong carrier/host/configuration generation; mixed ACK set; or any service/component/readback drift fails before candidate construction.

`F57OfflineSchemaManifestV1` is the only offline schema locator. Its purpose/media are exactly `EP-F57-OFFLINE-SCHEMA-MANIFEST-V1` and `application/vnd.ep.f57-offline-schema-manifest-v1+json`; `closure_root=RELEASE_CERTIFICATE`, its signer is `CN=EP F57 Offline Schema Authority,O=Enterprise Platform`, and its validity uses the common 90-day cap. The closure generator starts at the canonical `RELEASE_CERTIFICATE_V1` schema root plus the minimal offline-manifest bootstrap—not from a not-yet-issued certificate object—then follows every discriminator-reachable typed signed `ArtifactRefV1` contract through candidate, L2/L3, six receipts, journal/checkpoints, all 276 TestResultStore descriptor rows and their exact five envelope kinds, client/package, six carrier/P340 roots, the 89-row signer registry and reachable external trust-domain artifacts, then recursively follows every canonical JSON-Schema `$ref`. For a TestResultStore row the binding is exactly `artifact_kind=<TestResultEnvelopeKindV1 SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE wire>`, `discriminator=<exact TestID wire>`, and `media_type=<that descriptor's fixed media>`; this produces 276 descriptor bindings over five kinds, never 276 invented schema kinds. It also joins the 185 handler artifact media contracts so a typed signed envelope reachable through a Requirement result cannot disappear behind a generic `artifact_refs` vector. Opaque binary/log/sample objects remain digest/media checked but do not invent JSON schemas. The output must exact-equal this complete transitive closure; no developer-curated allowlist or hardcoded four-file shortcut is legal.

Every `F57OfflineSchemaDescriptorV1` contains all seven fields shown by the type: `schema_id`, canonical-sorted `artifact_bindings`, canonical-sorted `imports`, `relative_path`, `media_type=application/schema+json`, `sha256`, and `size_bytes`. `schema_id` is exactly `urn:ep:f57:schema:<sha256(UTF-8 canonical repository schema path)>` and must equal the source schema's `$id`; every binding is the exact `(artifact_kind,discriminator,media_type)` selected by the compiled typed-ref contract, while helper-only imported schemas have an empty binding set. `relative_path` is exactly `schemas/repo/<canonical repository schema path>`; `imports` contains the corresponding bundle-relative descriptor paths. Source/copy bytes are identical and keep their reviewed relative `$ref` spellings. Descriptors sort by `relative_path`, IDs/paths/bindings are unique, and the generated current count plus descriptor-set digest are byte-golden outputs rather than hand-maintained constants.

`OfflineSchemaManifestStoreV1` first create-new copies and fsyncs that exact closure below the final `RUN_DIR`; existing exact schema bytes are adopted and a conflict fails. It then freezes the descriptor set in a journal checkpoint and appends exactly `EVIDENCE_ENVELOPE_FINALIZATION_STARTED{artifact_kind=OFFLINE_SCHEMA_MANIFEST,finalization_attempt_id,frozen_input_checkpoint_ref,issued_at_unix_ms,expires_at_unix_ms}` before writing the signed manifest only at `<RUN_DIR>/schemas/offline-schema-manifest.v1.json`. Its canonical URI uses the same segment-join function as every bundle ref: empty `RUN_DIR_REL` yields exactly `evidence-relative://bundle/schemas/offline-schema-manifest.v1.json`; nonempty `RUN_DIR_REL` yields exactly `evidence-relative://bundle/<RUN_DIR_REL>/schemas/offline-schema-manifest.v1.json`. Empty/doubled segments, a leading/trailing slash in `RUN_DIR_REL`, percent/case alias or path escape is noncanonical; byte-goldens cover both empty and nested run directories. A crash before STARTED may leave only exact static copies, which a later invocation may reverify/adopt; after STARTED, recovery uses the frozen checkpoint and may create the first manifest or adopt exact existing typed bytes, never re-signing complete bytes. Conflict, partial manifest, second ref or alternate path quarantines the run. The final `ReleaseCandidateV1.offline_schema_manifest_ref` points to this exact manifest; typed verification exact-matches its candidate run/identity and its own `finalization_attempt_id` to the journal bound/reconciled event. L2, L3 and the certificate include its expiry in their aggregate minimum.

The offline verifier's only built-in schema/trust TCB is strict parsing for the four-field signed envelope, `ArtifactRefV1`, the locator fields of `ReleaseCertificateV1` and `ReleaseCandidateV1`, `F57OfflineSchemaManifestV1`, canonical JCS/CMS verification, the signer-registry corporate-root bootstrap, and the product-pinned Stage-14 deployment bootstrap needed to authenticate `AuthorityStorageTrustBootstrapV1`. The latter pin is the exact deployment-root set/digest and required deployment-manifest purpose/EKU carried by the independently signed product manifest; the leaf's recomputed SPKI token must byte-equal `DeploymentManifestV1.manifest_signer_subject` and its chain must be uniquely ACTIVE to that pin through the archived deployment bundle. Rotation is accepted only through a new independently signed product release whose transition is authorized by the previous pin under the existing product-root policy; a root merely bundled beside the candidate, a different deployment/build, ambient Windows root, self-signed replacement or network-completed chain never authorizes anything. It uses that minimum only to reach and authenticate the archived deployment/storage bootstrap, candidate signer registry and offline manifest, then revalidates the certificate, candidate and every reachable signed JSON envelope against the manifest binding selected by exact kind/discriminator/media. No bootstrap parse result alone can yield PASS. Missing/extra descriptor, closure/version drift, wrong `$id`/import/digest/media, path escape, alternate manifest, unsigned descriptor list, unknown typed signed JSON, bundled-self-root, wrong-deployment/rotation, directory discovery or network resolution fails closed; byte goldens cover both bootstrap domains and every cross-domain substitution.

`docs/evidence/f57-p340-soak-evidence.schema.json` is the sole canonical schema owner for the one P340 raw carrier root `P340SoakEvidenceV1`, the ten nested P340 signed-envelope types, all seven named supporting envelopes, `P340QualificationPlanV1`/store/plan-row/class, policy definition/attestation, `P340CapacityInputManifestV1`, the fixed latency histogram and the framed sample-row contract; it imports `f57-foundation.v1.schema.json` exactly once for shared nominals and the detached-CMS envelope, the common carrier helper exactly once, and the gate-journal owner exactly once for `G6VerifiedDataHddRootBindingV1`, `P340QualificationOperationKindV1`, `P340QualificationOutputRefV1` and the qualification journal/checkpoint family, and never imports release. G0's `docs/evidence/f57-gate-receipt.v1.schema.json` is the sole canonical owner for `GateReceiptV1`, its payload, plain `GateReceiptRefV1`, and the embedded `ObjectiveClosureBindingV1` family; no later crate or schema may redefine those nominal types. `docs/evidence/f57-l2-candidate-evidence.schema.json` is the sole canonical schema owner for the three L2 purpose/target/candidate rows and reuses the objective-closure family through exactly one relative `$ref` to the gate-receipt schema. `docs/evidence/f57-gate-run-journal.v1.schema.json` is the sole canonical schema owner for `AuthorityStorageTrustBootstrapV1`, `G6VerifiedDataHddRootBindingV1`, `JournalPrefixRefV1`, `PowerShutdownContinuationStatePrefixV1`, `P340QualificationOperationKindV1`, `P340QualificationOutputRefV1`, all gate-journal header/record/event/checkpoint definitions and `JournalCheckpointStoreV1` refs, including all five continuation, five qualification and three completion-finalization delta variants. The sole production-linkable Rust owner is G0's foundation-only `crates/platform/gate-journal-contract/`, including `src/storage_root_binding.rs`, `src/journal.rs`, `src/port.rs`, strict codecs/transitions and byte goldens; the file adapter alone persists it, and later runtime/P340/release/core-server/xtask code only imports the contract. FAILED and qualification records carry only gate-owned nominals plus generic refs/error code, so no gate-to-release or gate-to-P340 schema edge is introduced. `docs/evidence/f57-windows-authority-manifest.v1.schema.json` is the sole canonical owner for `WindowsAuthorityManifestV1`, `PowerShutdownServiceInstallPlanRowV1`, `PowerShutdownServicePreshutdownPolicyV1` and its endpoint/static enums. `docs/evidence/f57-offline-schema-manifest.v1.schema.json` is the sole canonical owner and fixed bootstrap schema for `F57OfflineSchemaManifestV1`; it is a mandatory closure seed and descriptor binding, and the offline verifier reaches its fixed copied path without directory discovery.

The two G0 gate schemas each have one direct edge to `f57-foundation.v1.schema.json`: gate receipt reuses principal/generation/identifier/result/Fresh-PG-ref/ArtifactRef/envelope nominals; gate journal reuses UUID/delivery/TestID/error/digest/ArtifactRef/envelope nominals. L2 has edges only to gate receipt and foundation. These are forward uses of the zero-import root, not G0→G1 dependencies; neither gate schema imports the later security-context schema, requirement-result schema or client schema. The schema-DAG golden freezes these exact edges and rejects a copied foundation nominal, a gate→security-context/result/client edge, a missing direct foundation edge or any foundation reverse import.

`docs/evidence/f57-release-evidence.schema.json` binds all six signed raw carrier roots but defines exactly five release-local roots and reaches the sixth, `P340SoakEvidenceV1`, through exactly one relative `$ref` to its canonical P340 owner. It imports `f57-foundation.v1.schema.json` exactly once for shared nominals and the detached-CMS envelope, `f57-release-carrier-common.v1.schema.json` once for the shared binding/context/outcome family, the gate-journal owner once for verified storage/continuation/finalization events, client-common once for `ClientPackageArtifactIdV1`, and the common UPS schema once for its manifest/status/command/ACK; it never copies those families. Release is the sole Rust owner for `G6CertifiedDataHddRootV1`, `ReleaseCandidateV1`; carrier staging/completion/control capsule; continuation state header/records; dispatch intent, API marker, User32 inline-control bytes and composite acknowledgement while importing the typed UPS command/ACK; six plain power readbacks, one plain `PowerShutdownAuthorityRecoveryProofV1`, success draft/command/controller/failure controls and both failure readbacks; `WindowsAuthorityArtifactSetV1`; Authority and backup-service dynamic readbacks, installed backup/recovery component and external-target readbacks; the seventeen strict service/PITR/recovery subordinate-readback definitions plus their exact eighteen `RELEASE_CARRIER_SUBORDINATE_READBACK_V1` field bindings; `ReleaseCarrierResultV1`; L3; release certificate; and release-only reference definitions. It exposes L2, gate receipt/ref/objective closure, gate-journal/checkpoint/continuation-prefix/storage-root-binding, client-common, Windows authority manifest, runtime-deployment, server-component-set and offline-manifest definitions only through one relative `$ref` apiece to their canonical schemas and never copies those families. The import order is foundation/gate/client-common/carrier-common plus UPS-common → P340 → release: UPS-common imports foundation only; P340 imports foundation/gate/carrier-common/UPS-common; release imports foundation/gate/client-common/carrier-common/UPS-common/P340; and no reverse edge exists; generation, generation-approval, runtime-topology, runtime-deployment, server-component-set and production activation remain separate helper/schema targets reached by their concrete media contracts. Task 10 owns the carrier-common helper plus Windows manifest and runtime-deployment schemas, five-row/MSI/preshutdown projection and byte goldens. G0 already reserves and strict-parses all thirteen delta variants. Task 13 imports the contract and activates only the five qualification transition/reconciler/semantic handlers `P340_QUALIFICATION_OPERATION_STARTED|COMPLETED|UNKNOWN|RECONCILED|CLOSURE_BOUND`; Task 14 imports the same unchanged contract and activates only the five continuation plus three completion-finalization handlers. Neither task modifies/adds a gate enum, wire or schema variant. Task 13 owns qualification operations/crash cuts, Task 14 owns release operations/crash cuts and the exact count/DAG golden, and neither release nor P340 copies a journal type. Task 14's release verifier gives FAILED's two generic refs their exact failure/cleanup media and payload contracts. Every other reachable envelope keeps its already named sole schema owner; the offline certificate closure copies all certificate-reachable owners including gate, generation, generation-approval, client-common, carrier-common, runtime-topology, runtime-deployment, P340, UPS-common, Windows manifest, component-set, backup-safeguard and PostgreSQL package-lock/install schemas without duplicating definitions; post-certificate production-activation records are verified against their separate schema and are not retroactively inserted into the frozen candidate closure. The schema-import-DAG golden rejects copied storage/event/client/generation/approval/qualification/runtime-deployment/component types, a delta count other than thirteen, any Task13/14 mutation of the reserved contract, `gate -> P340`, or any reverse edge/cycle. G4/G5/G6 respectively own Development/Integration/Final L2 goldens; G0 owns generation/approval, storage-bootstrap/binding, all thirteen journal delta wires/checkpoint/continuation-prefix/qualification nominals and gate-receipt/ref/objective-closure goldens; Task 14 uniquely creates the offline-manifest bootstrap, server-component-set and production-activation schemas and owns the offline closure/manifest, five remaining release raw roots, carrier rows, capsule/staging/completion-finalization crash cuts, authority/component sets, three-row recovery set, production-activation state machine and all cardinality/cross-purpose/schema-DAG negatives. Tasks 10–13 construct the exact in-memory types during rehearsal even though only Task 15 produces candidate evidence.

`docs/evidence/f57-windows-runtime-deployment.v1.schema.json` is the sole schema owner for `WindowsRuntimeDeploymentClosureV1|WindowsRuntimeDeploymentReadbackSetV1`, their strict active/deferred rows and one-to-one carrier-specific artifact/readback variants. `docs/evidence/f57-windows-server-component-set.v1.schema.json` is the sole schema owner for `WindowsServerComponentSetV1` and its six component rows; `docs/evidence/f57-production-activation.v1.schema.json` is the sole schema owner for single-disk acceptance, activation binding/event/record and typed failure/retry state. All three direct-import foundation for shared nominals, none imports the consolidated release schema, and production activation verifies its certificate/candidate/runtime-deployment references through typed media rather than copying their definitions.

`ReleaseCandidatePayloadV1` above is the complete final candidate wire; Task 14 may not redefine or omit one of its fields. Its purpose serializes exactly as `EP-F57-RELEASE-CANDIDATE-V1`, `finalization_attempt_id` exact-matches the one `FINAL_RELEASE` candidate-finalization/bound event, and `data_classification` is exactly `PRODUCTION_SIGNED_NO_BUSINESS_DATA`. `artifact_signer_registry_ref` exact-loads the 89-row registry whose envelope digest is repeated by `identity`; `offline_schema_manifest_ref` exact-loads the already bound same-run closure; `client_artifact_set_ref` exact-loads a `RELEASE` mode four-platform set; and `pre_freeze_carrier_refs` exact-load the same-run PASS results for `WINDOWS_AUTHORITY_BUILD` and `WINDOWS_SERVICE_INSTALL`. `generation_observed_selection_ref` exact-loads the plain content-addressed selection created for this same `CandidateRunIdentityV1`; it byte-equals the nonnull field on `CANDIDATE_MANIFEST_FINALIZATION_STARTED` and closes the pre-candidate OBSERVED race. Its five tagged artifacts are exactly one direct Windows authority-set envelope plus the four wrapper refs from that client artifact set—never copied packages, a sixth lane or double-signed authority. Source tree, graph/projection/facade manifests, migration identity plus all four source artifacts, runtime topology and toolchain exact-match `CandidateIdentityV1` and the frozen precursor checkpoint. A bare payload, missing field, alternate authority wrapper, registry/offline expiry bypass, wrong mode/run, selection drift, or checkpoint that does not extend every precursor fails before signing.

The final observed selection is not merely whichever generation is current at freeze time. `GenerationObservedReleaseSelectionPortV1::begin_or_adopt_current_observed(candidate_run,deployment_id,authority_epoch,preselection_prefix)` accepts the fourth private `VerifiedGateRunJournalPrefixV1`, authenticates the same run and persists its checkpoint ref/sequence/terminal hash atomically with the immutable selection and lease. It must return the same attempt ID, manifest/declaration refs and complete ACK set as `VerifiedFinalInstalledObservedGenerationV1`; the row begins and remains `PRESELECTION` after begin. Equal prefixes and valid strict pre-finalization extensions containing no candidate-finalization record may renew while remaining `PRESELECTION`. The sole monotonic transition to `SELECTION_BOUND` is the first authenticated `CANDIDATE_MANIFEST_FINALIZATION_STARTED{candidate_kind=FINAL_RELEASE,generation_observed_selection_ref=<this exact selection_ref>}`; a missing/wrong ref or conflicting earlier finalization fails. Every later accepted prefix must retain that binding, and only the matching `CANDIDATE_MANIFEST_BOUND` makes the verified progress expose a candidate ref. `bind_candidate_and_release` accepts only `VerifiedGenerationObservedSelectionLeaseProgressV1`, derives the candidate ref from that authenticated progress, and never accepts a raw ref.

The lease carries nonnil `lease_id`, boot owner, monotonically increasing version and checked expiry; the stored `last_candidate_checkpoint_binds_selection` moves only false-to-true at that exact finalization event. Recovery calls only `load_exact_for_recovery(&VerifiedBusinessArtifactV1<GateRunJournalHeaderPayloadV1>)`: the verified signed header yields the unique candidate-run equality lookup, the returned private wrapper exposes its last persisted checkpoint ref, and only then does the G0 exact-read port load that authenticated prefix for `verify_progress|resume_expired_same_run`; no caller selection ref, caller checkpoint ref or latest scan is accepted. Equal-or-strict legal progress is recoverable both before and after selection binding. Same-run expiry can CAS-resume only the same immutable selection against the complete persisted old lease tuple after rechecking the OBSERVED pointer/terminal/ACK set; it allocates a new lease identity/version/expiry without changing selection, generation or candidate binding. An unrecoverable failed freeze requires two distinct currently authorized human capability contexts to mint the private live `AuthorizedGenerationObservedSelectionResolutionV1`; only its create-new persisted, exact-reloaded bytes plus still-live authorization window may become `VerifiedPersistedGenerationObservedSelectionResolutionV1` and drive terminal `FAILED_RELEASED` against the exact prior checkpoint/expired lease tuple. Timeout alone never releases, deletes or reassigns the row, and an orphan resolution object is never scanned or adopted. Freeze rejects an earlier installed generation, desired-only state, mixed ACK set or any service/component/config drift. The candidate's runtime-topology declaration therefore derives from final installed facts, not a pre-install or pre-candidate plain declaration.

`ReleaseCertificatePayloadV1` is likewise complete. Purpose/verdict serialize exactly as `EP-F57-RELEASE-CERTIFICATE-V1` / `RELEASE_CERTIFIED`; `finalization_attempt_id` exact-matches its envelope-finalization/bound event. It references the exact final candidate and L3 envelope, carries six plain typed `GateReceiptRefV1` values and the canonical 185-result bijection, and repeats the same candidate identity/run plus the latest strict-extension checkpoint; the identity transitively and exactly binds the 89-row registry digest rather than inventing an unlisted certificate field. Its `certified_data_hdd_root` exact-copies the final candidate/header `G6VerifiedDataHddRootBindingV1`, then names the one PASS `P340SoakEvidenceV1` and that envelope's exact Residency and filesystem-geometry refs. The producer typed-loads all four artifacts, proves manifest ref/volume identity/root digests and the Residency/geometry DATA_HDD identity are identical, and only then recognizes `CERTIFIED_DATA_HDD`; an earlier `VERIFIED_DATA_HDD_ROOT` alone cannot satisfy the certificate. Before construction the producer exact-loads the one verified finalization record, requires `artifact_kind=RELEASE_CERTIFICATE` and the registry-selected certificate signer row, and copies `run_journal_checkpoint_ref`, `issued_at_unix_ms`, `expires_at_unix_ms`, and `finalization_attempt_id` only from that record. The frozen expiry is the precomputed minimum including the bound offline schema manifest, P340/root-upgrade chain and every other time-bearing reachable input; no resumed constructor may read the latest checkpoint, live clock or recompute a different bound. A partial certificate, second verdict, signed-ref wrapper around a receipt, stale manifest, unequal L2/L3/carrier sets, missing root upgrade or any cross-run/root ref fails closed.

`ProductionActivationAuthorityV1` is a separate post-certificate verifier; issuing `ReleaseCertificateV1` never opens business routes. It exact-reconstructs candidate, final-installed OBSERVED selection, topology certification, P340/certified-HDD root, the graph-exact runtime deployment closure/readback, five Authority services, the fixed G0 evidence-signer-broker install/readiness readback, six server components, backup/restore chain, UPS/BitLocker/TPM and external/offline safeguards from the explicit bundle. `acceptance_id` resolves only through the immutable Authority audit/fact store to `SingleDiskDegradedProductionAcceptanceV1`, which must bind profile `SINGLE_DISK_DEGRADED_PRODUCTION`, `certified_concurrent_users=20`, the complete five-risk set, exact deployment/candidate/certificate, complete safeguard refs, future expiry and two distinct currently authorized customer approvers. The verifier captures and stores four fresh sealed objects: topology, graph-exact runtime-deployment readback set, installed Authority/G0-broker/backup-component readback, and strict `StorageSafeguardReadbackV1` under purpose/media `EP-F57-STORAGE-SAFEGUARD-READBACK-V1` / `application/vnd.ep.f57-storage-safeguard-readback-v1+json`. Before accepting those bytes it typed-loads the certified latest `BackupCheckpointV1`, reconstructs its predecessor chain, typed-loads the active-config-selected `BackupTopologySigningTrustCurrentPointerV1` and its independent current `BackupTopologySigningTrustManifestV1`, then verifies the current `BackupTopologyV1` signer only through the resulting private `VerifiedBackupTopologySigningTrustCurrentV1`, exact-loads the current authority-storage manifest whose target set is the singleton current continuous target, and verifies every referenced target/offline support object under that topology; the fresh readback's head/latest must byte-equal that certified checkpoint, never an inferred newest object or a valid ancestor. The safeguard binding must byte-match this activation ID, retry ordinal, observed attempt, candidate, certificate and OBSERVED selection; nonce, authenticated collector session and object are new for every retry on the same current Windows boot, expiry checked-equals topology policy, `protection_state=HEALTHY`, target/quota/permission probes pass and exact A/B media are disconnected. A prior retry's still-unexpired object is invalid. It then proves complete graph participant IDs ↔ complete closure participant IDs ↔ complete readback participant IDs. It separately proves graph-`ACTIVE` participant IDs ↔ positive-readback participant IDs ↔ certified topology/declaration participant IDs ↔ generation required-participant IDs ↔ ACK participant IDs; exact graph-derived `database_consumers` and the canonical generation item/`required_item_ids` relation are verified as independent projections, never as members of that bijection. Every deferred participant must have exactly one negative absence row and no artifact/declaration participant/database-consumer/required-participant/item edge/ACK presence. It may persist only through `LIVE_READBACK_BOUND` and returns private `VerifiedProductionActivationReadyV1`; there is no independently durable release-owned terminal commit. The upper `ProductionGenerationAdmissionAuthorityV1` then calls the sole `commit_activation_and_genesis_admission_cas`, which in one PostgreSQL transaction appends `ACTIVATED`, inserts the genesis `ProductionGenerationAdmissionV1{admission_kind=GENESIS_FULL_CERTIFICATION}`, advances its current-head pointer and increments monotonic `business_api_generation` for that exact OBSERVED tuple. Genesis `impacted_scopes` is exactly one current complete `DEPLOYMENT` scope; legal-entity rows are forbidden. All rows share one commit time and either all become durable or none do. Only this joint terminal transaction opens business routes and yields user status `PRODUCTION_ACTIVATED_SINGLE_DISK_DEGRADED`. Before it, `EPAuthorityServer` remains control-plane/recovery ready but production-quarantined and never claims RAID or HA.

`ProductionGenerationAdmissionAuthorityV1` is the sole continuing route authority and admissions are deployment-wide, never a partially advanced per-entity pointer map. Every business command and query exact-checks that current durable OBSERVED `(epoch,generation,manifest ref,digest,attempt)` equals the one deployment current admitted tuple and that no matching live hold exists, but a read-only check is insufficient: the check and durable accepted-request registration are one linearization point defined below. A package maintenance flow may initially hold only its legal-entity scope, while the four global classes hold all business writes; however, when a new generation becomes global OBSERVED the generation/admission mismatch temporarily closes every route until one atomic delta admission succeeds. That admission carries the canonical complete `impacted_scopes` exact set/digest and exact transition set for every changed item. The verifier proves every unlisted scope/item is byte-identical and therefore carried forward in the same new generation; no partial entity admission exists.

Scope intersection is one pure upper-owned same-partition function, `hold_intersects_v1(deployment_id,left_scope,right_scope,current_tenancy_snapshot) -> Result<bool,ScopeValidationErrorV1>`. Admission/hold stores are physically keyed by deployment; a caller cannot supply scopes from another partition, and the outer dispatcher returns “not in this deployment” before this function rather than converting an unverifiable foreign scope into `false`. The function strict-validates both tagged scopes against the one current `TenancyAuthoritySnapshotV1`: deployment ID, positive/current tenancy generation, exact snapshot ref, legal-entity ACTIVE row and key-domain generation, and for `DEPLOYMENT` the complete canonical impacted-legal-entity set/digest. Missing/duplicate/unknown/stale/mismatched input returns error; the route gate treats error as DENY and the hold store treats it as an intersecting conflict. After validation the same-deployment truth table is exact: `DEPLOYMENT↔DEPLOYMENT`, `DEPLOYMENT↔LEGAL_ENTITY`, and `LEGAL_ENTITY↔DEPLOYMENT` → `true`; `LEGAL_ENTITY(a)↔LEGAL_ENTITY(b)` → `a==b`. A deployment scope's impacted-ID set is completeness evidence and never narrows its global effect. For `PACKAGE_DELTA|ROLLBACK_REOPEN`, `ProductionGenerationAdmissionV1.impacted_scopes` is either exactly one `DEPLOYMENT` row or one-or-more unique `LEGAL_ENTITY` rows; for `GENESIS_FULL_CERTIFICATION` it is exactly one complete current `DEPLOYMENT` row. Mixed, overlapping, stale-snapshot or mixed-tenancy-generation vectors are illegal.

crates/platform/generation-activation/src/admission_store.rs and docs/evidence/f57-production-admission.v1.schema.json are the sole Rust/schema owners for ProductionGenerationAdmissionV1, ProductionAdmissionHoldCauseV1, ProductionAdmissionHoldV1 and ProductionAdmissionExecutionLeaseV1. Their exact plain-JCS media are respectively application/vnd.ep.f57-production-generation-admission-v1+json, application/vnd.ep.f57-production-admission-hold-v1+json and application/vnd.ep.f57-production-admission-execution-lease-v1+json; `ProductionAdmissionHoldCauseV1` is embedded only in the hold wire and has no independent media. Their displayed purposes are mandatory and no generic JSON/octet-stream ref substitutes. PostgreSQL row-chain/CAS verification, the current-head projection and the signed Authority audit checkpoint authenticate these operational rows; they are not independently CMS-signed artifacts. Schema, SQL projection, Rust wire and create-new/adopt goldens must remain byte-identical, including tagged cause/reference closure, predecessor_admission_ref, lease cas_version|row_sha256, cause-specific nullability and one-way state rules.

The admission bypass is a generated exact registry, not `/control/*` prefix logic. Its owner/schema/media are `crates/platform/generation-activation/src/admission_gate.rs`, `docs/evidence/f57-production-admission-bypass-registry.v1.schema.json`, and `application/vnd.ep.f57-production-admission-bypass-registry-v1+json`; purpose/profile are `EP-F57-PRODUCTION-ADMISSION-BYPASS-REGISTRY-V1` / `WINDOWS_AUTHORITY_V1`. Its ten canonical rows are:

| Method + exact canonical route | Post-strict-parse selector | Authorization | Mutating |
|---|---|---|---:|
| `GET /internal/v1/health/live` | `HEALTH_LIVE` | `f57.platform.health.read` | false |
| `GET /internal/v1/health/ready` | `HEALTH_READY` | `f57.platform.health.read` | false |
| `POST /control/v1/commands` | `PRODUCTION_ACTIVATION_COMMAND` | `f57.production.activate` | true |
| `POST /control/v1/commands` | `PACKAGE_MAINTENANCE_COMMAND` | `f57.package.maintenance.execute` | true |
| `POST /control/v1/commands` | `RECOVERY_OPERATION_COMMAND` | `f57.recovery.operate` | true |
| `POST /control/v1/queries` | `PRODUCTION_ADMISSION_STATUS_QUERY` | `f57.production.admission.read` | false |
| `POST /control/v1/queries` | `PACKAGE_MAINTENANCE_QUERY` | `f57.package.maintenance.read` | false |
| `POST /control/v1/queries` | `RECOVERY_OPERATION_QUERY` | `f57.recovery.operation.read` | false |
| `POST /control/v1/queries` | `AUTHORITY_RECOVERY_PROOF_QUERY` | `f57.recovery.proof.read` | false |
| `GET /control/v1/commands/{request_id}` | `ORIGINAL_COMMAND_BYPASS_INHERIT` | exact stored original command classification/capability | false |

The generator emits exactly one canonical JCS registry artifact from the same compiled router/capability sources used by the Authority build. `WindowsAuthorityArtifactSetV1.production_admission_bypass_registry_ref` binds those bytes and exact media into the signed build result; service-install evidence exact-repeats that ref and attests the installed bytes, the final candidate reaches it only through its already signed Authority artifact set, and startup typed-loads only that candidate-bound installed ref. An ambient file, database-editable route, latest-file scan, build-only registry not present in the candidate closure, or registry bytes from another run/attempt/build is a hard failure before any bypass route becomes ready.

Every row fixes response class `CONTROL_METADATA_NO_CUSTOMER_FIELDS` and `bypasses_only_production_admission_and_hold=true`. It does **not** bypass canonical parsing, authenticated identity, CSRF, authorization, MFA/reauthentication, SoD, authority epoch, operation ID, query/adopt, rate limit, audit or typed response filtering, and it can never create `AuthorizedPgTx` for a business schema. The eight distinct capability IDs in the table are exact `PLATFORM_MECHANISM` rows in the authored CapabilityGraph and generated capability/authorization registry; Task 14's router-registry exact join fails if one is absent, duplicated or merely a free string. Receipt lookup first exact-loads the persisted original request and inherits only one of the three registered command selectors; unknown/missing/conflicting classification denies. Authentication session start/reauth/end occur on the separate pre-gate auth surface and are not bypass rows. Events, files, employee/portal APIs, MCP and any unknown route/selector remain gated. Startup and CI exact-join the generated router to this ten-row set; no wildcard/default/handler-local Boolean exists.

To preserve the dependency DAG, `crates/platform/command/src/admission.rs` owns only the displayed lower request/port/error contracts. Its private non-serialized `VerifiedAdmissionTargetScopeSetV1` is constructible only after the generated route parser, authenticated `VerifiedSecurityContextV1`, field/row authorization and current tenancy authority agree; it binds one deployment, one current snapshot and a nonempty canonical set of every payload/path-derived target scope. No client raw scope or header can construct it. `begin_or_adopt_business_request` takes the stable authenticated `request_id` plus a digest over the full request/route/context binding. Under the same deployment-scoped serializable lock/CAS used by the admission head and hold writer, it exact-loads the current authority epoch plus OBSERVED/current admission/API generation, requires the epoch to equal the typed-loaded admission, OBSERVED generation and verified security-context epochs, checks every target scope against every live hold, and create-new inserts—or exact-adopts after response loss—one `ProductionAdmissionExecutionLeaseV1{state=ACCEPTED}` before returning the affine `VerifiedBusinessAdmissionPermitV1`. `authority_epoch` is server-derived, is included in `request_binding_sha256`, and is never accepted from a client field/header. A reused request ID with any changed byte or epoch fails; an existing terminal row may be queried only through the registered receipt path and never re-executed. There is no check/handler gap and no process-local in-flight counter.

The command transaction consumes that permit and atomically terminalizes its lease as `COMPLETED_IN_PLACE` with the durable command/query result, or an exact-once Outbox/workflow handoff terminalizes it as `HANDED_OFF_EXACT_ONCE`; no other terminal argument is accepted by `finish_business_request`, and the upper implementation rejects caller-selected forged refs. Crash recovery adopts the same request/lease and reconciles only against the durable command/Outbox identity. A hold writer takes the same deployment lock, appends `ADMISSION_CLOSED` before releasing it, thereby preventing every new intersecting lease, and may append `DRAIN_COMPLETE` or `BARRIER_COMMITTED` only after a durable query proves every already-accepted intersecting lease terminal in one of those two states. The sole exception is the `DATA_HDD_DISASTER_REPLACEMENT` cause: because the old authority can be destroyed with the disk, its exact two-custodian recovery attempt may instead supply typed proof that every old authority/lease/volume/host write path is unreachable and fenced; that proof is not available to any other cause. An `ACCEPTED` orphan without either normal positive no-effect/handoff proof or that exact disaster fence keeps the hold closed; it is never guessed complete. Interleaving goldens cover permit-before-hold, hold-before-permit, response loss, process crash, multi-scope intersection, cross-cause fence substitution and terminal-CAS loss, proving no business write can appear after the barrier.

Separately, the identity/control boundary creates `VerifiedControlOrHealthSecurityContextV1` without requiring business DB readiness, and `ControlAdmissionBypassPortV1` returns the non-interchangeable `VerifiedControlBypassPermitV1`; that permit has no constructor/accessor accepted by `AuthorizedPgTx` or any business handler. The command pipeline/common query boundary calls `begin_or_adopt_business_request` and `finish_business_request`; health/control handlers call `check_control_or_health`. `ep-platform-generation-activation` implements both with the sole concrete registry/gate, and `ep-authority-kernel` injects them. Lower command/query code never imports the upper crate. Any store error, invalid/empty/mixed-deployment scope set, route/selector mismatch, API-generation drift, OBSERVED/admission mismatch, intersecting hold or lease conflict returns no permit and no protected handler/repository call occurs.

An ordinary-class `PACKAGE_DELTA` is legal only when fresh participant/item/transition/readbacks prove its permission, data, network, host, executor and resource footprint is wholly within the previously certified envelope, with current backup and no new participant, service, database consumer, capacity increase or safeguard weakening. `RUST_KERNEL|POSTGRESQL_DATABASE_MIGRATION|CRYPTOGRAPHY_FOUNDATION|STORAGE_FOUNDATION`, any resource increase, or any new participant/service/database consumer requires a complete new clean build/install, P340/capacity/recovery certification, release certificate and customer production activation. `ROLLBACK_REOPEN` is legal only after fresh typed predecessor readback and exact equality to a prior admission. Each single-row admission CAS names its predecessor, exact ACK/transition refs, complete impact set and increments `business_api_generation`; crash tests prove multi-scope delta is all-or-nothing. No direct route override, observed-only shortcut or package-local `APPLIED_VERIFIED` can reopen traffic.

Invalid certificate, acceptance or safeguard input fails before an activation attempt exists. A collector failure or post-request live drift instead CAS-appends typed `FAILED_HELD`; graph delivery/readback drift maps specifically to `RuntimeDeploymentDrift` and is never hidden inside fixed installed-component evidence. Repeating the exact command must revalidate the same still-current certificate and two-person acceptance, append `RETRY_COMMITTED` against the exact prior failure-record hash under the same `activation_id`, strictly increment its retry ordinal, and freshly recollect all four live readbacks before another `LIVE_READBACK_BOUND` readiness proof. The exact allowed state edges are `REQUEST_COMMITTED|RETRY_COMMITTED -> LIVE_READBACK_BOUND`, either nonterminal pre-activation state to `FAILED_HELD`, `FAILED_HELD -> RETRY_COMMITTED`, and the single upper-owned atomic `LIVE_READBACK_BOUND -> ACTIVATED + GENESIS_FULL_CERTIFICATION`; history is append-only, stale or partially reused readbacks are forbidden, routes remain quarantined while held, and a second activation ID for the same certificate/deployment/epoch always fails.

Migration `20261025092530` creates `platform_core.production_activation_attempts` within its already reserved version, with exact columns `{activation_id uuid primary key,deployment_id uuid not null,authority_epoch bigint not null,candidate_run_identity_sha256 bytea not null,candidate_manifest_ref_jcs bytea not null,release_certificate_ref_jcs bytea not null unique,runtime_topology_certification_ref_jcs bytea not null,generation_observed_selection_ref_jcs bytea not null,observed_activation_attempt_id uuid not null,customer_acceptance_ref_jcs bytea not null,profile text not null,state text not null,cas_version bigint not null,last_record_sha256 bytea not null,record_prefix_jcs bytea not null,created_at_unix_ms bigint not null,updated_at_unix_ms bigint not null}`. Release activation deliberately has no `business_api_generation`; that value exists only in the upper admission row written by the same terminal transaction. The same migration creates CAS projections `platform_core.production_generation_admissions` and `platform_core.production_admission_holds`; both store canonical object/ref JCS, predecessor/current tuple, scope, state, `cas_version`, `row_sha256` and monotonic times, while each hold additionally stores `cause_kind` plus canonical `cause_jcs` covered by its hashes and checked against the exact variant reference closure. There is one current admission per deployment/epoch and one live hold per nonoverlapping scope, independent of cause. The migration also creates `platform_core.production_admission_execution_leases` with exact columns `{lease_id uuid primary key,request_id uuid not null,deployment_id uuid not null,authority_epoch bigint not null,request_binding_sha256 bytea not null,target_scopes_jcs bytea not null,target_scope_set_sha256 bytea not null,admission_ref_jcs bytea not null,observed_generation_manifest_ref_jcs bytea not null,observed_generation_digest_sha256 bytea not null,business_api_generation bigint not null,state text not null,terminal_result_ref_jcs bytea null,sequence bigint not null,previous_record_sha256 bytea null,record_prefix_jcs bytea not null,cas_version bigint not null,row_sha256 bytea not null,recorded_at_unix_ms bigint not null,updated_at_unix_ms bigint not null}`, unique `(deployment_id,request_id)`, a deployment/state/scope-overlap lookup index, canonical-scope/digest checks, and one-way state constraint `ACCEPTED -> COMPLETED_IN_PLACE|HANDED_OFF_EXACT_ONCE`; sequence-zero ACCEPTED exact-matches the server-derived current epoch, typed admission, OBSERVED generation, security context and request-binding digest and has null predecessor/result. A terminal record is sequence one, retains the same epoch, hashes the exact accepted record, extends `record_prefix_jcs`, requires a nonnull result ref and may never return to ACCEPTED. The unique constraint deliberately excludes epoch so a reused `(deployment_id,request_id)` can never produce a second effect after reenrollment. The same deployment advisory/row lock orders admission head, live holds and execution leases; a hold's cause-specific `DRAIN_COMPLETE|BARRIER_COMMITTED` CAS requires the indexed exact intersecting ACCEPTED count across all epochs to be zero, except disaster replacement may substitute the typed unreachable-and-fenced proof frozen by its recovery attempt. An old-epoch orphan otherwise remains fail-closed. A single db-pg transaction implementation of `ProductionActivationAdmissionCommitPortV1` locks and exact-checks activation-ready, current OBSERVED and admission head, then writes activation terminal record, genesis admission and head/API-generation advance before one commit; no lower store exposes a terminal-activation method. Checks close activation profile/state, admission kind, tagged hold cause/state and all cause-specific nullability; route read uses their exact current rows in the same authorized transaction. Crash tests cut every statement and commit/response boundary, including cross-cause substitution, cross-epoch request-ID replay and terminal epoch drift, proving zero partial visibility, while delta/rollback tests prove a stale concurrent writer can neither reopen nor increment the API generation.

The three generation artifact fields plus `generation_observed_selection_ref` are mandatory only on the final `ReleaseCandidatePayloadV1` displayed above. Before copying any generation object, final freeze calls only `GenerationObservedReleaseSelectionPortV1::begin_or_adopt_current_observed(candidate_run,deployment_id,authority_epoch,preselection_prefix)` for the already fixed values and authenticated locked current prefix. The returned immutable selection record names the exact terminal OBSERVED attempt and ACK set, is create-new materialized in the final bundle, and remains `PRESELECTION` while equal or strict pre-finalization progress is renewed. Its ref is first bound only by `CANDIDATE_MANIFEST_FINALIZATION_STARTED{candidate_kind=FINAL_RELEASE,generation_observed_selection_ref=<exact nonnull selection_ref>}`; after the candidate bytes and matching `CANDIDATE_MANIFEST_BOUND` are fsynced, freeze calls `bind_candidate_and_release` with the command-authority-produced `VerifiedGenerationObservedSelectionLeaseProgressV1`, from which the store derives the exact candidate ref—never with a raw ref. `generation_manifest_ref` typed-loads the selected signed envelope whose whole-envelope SHA-256 equals the candidate declaration's `generation_digest_sha256`; `generation_approval_registry_ref` byte-equals the private verified-generation proof's relocatable pinned-registry provenance; and `generation_participant_ack_refs` is the canonical unique exact-set of strict plain ACK objects named by the selection for every manifest-required participant, all from one durable OBSERVED activation attempt. Each ACK ref uses exact ACK media and recomputes the required declaration-row/item-subset digests. Final freeze uses only that verified selection plus the explicit authority-generation bundle root to perform a closed graph copy. The canonical signed approval-registry envelope is domain-verified and materialized through `EvidenceInputStoreV1` at final-bundle `inputs/<whole-envelope-sha256>.json`. The canonical signed authority-storage-manifest envelope is the sole dual-locator exception: its already header-authenticated fixed archive ref remains `inputs/storage-root/authority-storage-manifest.v1.json`, while the byte-identical digest-named `EvidenceInputStoreV1` ref is also materialized because immutable generation/declaration objects already carry that portable URI. Those two refs must have identical media, size, SHA-256 and exact bytes; the fixed locator serves only boot/history, the digest locator serves only portable graph traversal, the offline bundle retains both while deduplicating content identity, and no third alias is legal. The other six G6 archive rows remain byte-for-byte at their fixed `inputs/storage-root/deployment-manifest.v1.json|deployment-manifest.p7s|deployment-trust-bundle.p7b|storage-trust-root.der|storage-revocation.bin|storage-checkpoint.bin` paths and never pass through the digest-named port. Generation manifest, every nested reverse plan, every ACK, runtime-topology declaration, graph/projection/policy objects and every other reachable object go create-new to exact `objects/sha256/<digest>`. Every digest-named `evidence-relative://bundle/...` URI remains byte-identical across authority and final roots, while all seven fixed archive refs remain byte-identical to the signed G6 header. Freeze typed-reloads the entire closure from the final bundle, exact-compares every ref/media/size/digest/JCS/trust-policy proof, proves the dual-locator identity, fsyncs a checkpoint for that copied closure, and only then may sign the candidate. It never rewrites a signed manifest, substitutes the fixed registry source path, discovers a directory, renames a bootstrap binary or leaves an authority-root-only ref. Missing/conflicting/cross-root bytes, a third storage-manifest alias, desired-only state, a generic generation proof, wrong registry, selection drift, missing/extra/duplicate/mixed-attempt ACK, or declaration/generation/graph/storage/policy drift fails before candidate output. An offline golden makes the authority-generation root unavailable after freeze and must still verify the candidate, traverse the selection/reverse-plan/ACK/declaration closure and produce topology certification/release closure from the final bundle alone. These fields make the final certificate's offline graph reach the generation envelope, its selection/trust provenance and exact OBSERVED ACK set without inventing another signed snapshot or signer-registry row.

`IntegrationCandidateV1` fixes `schema_version=1`; `IntegrationCandidatePurposeV1` serializes exactly as `EP-F57-INTEGRATION-CANDIDATE-DEVELOPMENT-SLICE-V1|EP-F57-INTEGRATION-CANDIDATE-INTEGRATION-V1`, matching its closed variant. The `DevelopmentSlice` candidate fixes `data_classification=SYNTHETIC`; the G5 `Integration` candidate fixes `DEIDENTIFIED`; no caller selects either value. G4/G5 persist only `SignedIntegrationCandidateV1`; a bare payload is evaluator input and cannot enter L2. The signed envelope's exact-byte SHA-256 is recorded as `candidate_manifest_ref.sha256`; only `verify --level l2|l3 --candidate` accepts that SHA in its `--candidate` position, while source-building `client-gate|client-build|candidate build|candidate freeze` retain the frozen `<git-rev>` grammar and carrier manifest inputs use their separately named `--candidate-manifest`. In verification, `candidate_identity_sha256=sha256(JCS(CandidateIdentityV1))` is separate and never accepted instead. The final signed `ReleaseCandidateV1` follows the same verification rule. G4/G5 journal headers have `storage_root_binding=null` and `SignedIntegrationCandidateV1` contains no storage-root field; the final G6 `ReleaseCandidateV1.storage_root_binding` is mandatory, byte-equals its immutable G6 journal header value, and candidate construction may only copy it—not probe a new root. A G4 candidate build creates one unpredictable `gate_run_id` and journal header. A G5 validation/client build creates them first; the four-client artifact manifest and candidate build must adopt that exact run and journal. The final G6 validation follows the same precursor rule. Before any candidate is signed, its builder invokes or resumes the one internal CandidateBound Fresh-PG envelope for that run's maximal target, verifies the one bound event, embeds the exact plain typed `fresh_pg_receipt`, then flushes and signs a later checkpoint of the complete precursor prefix as `precursor_journal_checkpoint_ref`. Candidate signing precedes the one `CANDIDATE_MANIFEST_BOUND` append. Thus the candidate signs the pre-manifest evidence without a hash cycle, and every later L2 checkpoint must authenticate a strict extension of that precursor checkpoint. The journal header is the create-new, atomically persisted and fsynced source of run identity; after a crash the run creator typed-loads that same header and never generates a replacement ID. Candidate output paths are create-new and atomically renamed. If signed candidate bytes already exist while the journal is unbound, recovery typed-verifies those exact bytes against the run/artifact/Fresh-PG/registry/storage-root closure and precursor checkpoint, then appends their exact ref without re-signing or overwrite; if the bound event already exists, the output bytes must exact-match it and the command returns idempotently. A missing/conflicting output after binding, a second manifest/Fresh-PG ref, wrong classification, root-binding drift, or any identity/artifact/registry/checkpoint drift fails the entire run. Candidate build/freeze exact-includes or exact-references every registered precursor artifact/result, takes `finalization_attempt_id` and the frozen checkpoint only from its `CandidateManifestFinalizationStarted` record, then appends `CANDIDATE_MANIFEST_BOUND`; it never rewrites a precursor result under the later manifest digest. No later command may generate or substitute another run ID. `ValidatedCandidateManifestRefV1` can be constructed only by typed loading of the explicit manifest path, verification of its artifact exact-set/purpose/signature/Fresh-PG/registry/root ref, recomputation of manifest and identity hashes, verification of the precursor checkpoint, exact comparison of `artifact.sha256` with verification CLI `--candidate`, and equality with the journal's manifest-bound event. A digest alone is never enough to reconstruct or authorize a candidate. Golden crash-cut tests cover header-before-Fresh-PG, Fresh-PG-before-candidate, output-before-manifest-bound, bound-before-response, conflicting pre-existing output, storage-root substitution and repeated invocation for G4, G5 and final freeze.

`L2CandidateEvidencePayloadV1` and `L3CandidateEvidencePayloadV1` both fix `schema_version=1` and are persisted only inside the common `SignedBusinessArtifactV1<T>` envelope. From G4 onward, `crates/platform/release/src/l2.rs` is the sole production-linkable Rust owner of the complete three-row L2 nominal/parser/verifier/builder family; `xtask/src/f57/l2.rs` only composes it for CLI/gate orchestration, and no production crate depends on xtask. G6 `crates/platform/release/src/release_evidence.rs` solely owns L3 and the release aggregate, while the already frozen L2 schema remains its separate canonical schema owner. L2 purposes serialize exactly as `EP-F57-L2-DEVELOPMENT-SLICE-V1|EP-F57-L2-INTEGRATION-V1|EP-F57-L2-FINAL-RELEASE-V1`; the sole L3 purpose serializes exactly as `EP-F57-L3-RELEASE-CERTIFICATION-V1`. L3 permits only `target_gate=RELEASE_CERTIFIED` and its `final_l2_evidence_ref` must identify the exact verified signed L2 envelope supplied separately to `gate g6`. Both levels exact-match `candidate_manifest_ref` to the explicit signed manifest bytes and CLI digest, recompute `candidate_identity_sha256` from `JCS(candidate)`, and exact-match those values plus `gate_run_id`, target gate, and the signed journal checkpoint before executing or joining a result. At the one legal first finalization, trusted `now` and the minimum of the level policy cap, bound offline schema manifest, every consumed time-bearing signed evidence/result/carrier expiry and fixed journal expiry are durably captured as `issued_at_unix_ms` and `expires_at_unix_ms` in the exact five-field finalization record. The constructor copies those two times, the frozen checkpoint and finalization ID only from that verified record; crash recovery never rereads the clock or latest checkpoint and never recomputes them. It requires `issued_at_unix_ms < expires_at_unix_ms`, and the envelope must still be valid when the consuming gate signs its receipt/certificate. Immutable candidate manifests and static content-addressed refs have no expiry and are exact-verified but excluded from that minimum. Any other consumed evidence input without a typed verifiable expiry cannot enter an aggregate. `test_results` is the sole TestID-to-result wire: it is sorted/unique by TestID, each artifact is unique, typed loading must repeat that same TestID/candidate run, and each pair exact-matches one terminal journal record. Parallel ID/ref vectors are forbidden. `gate g4|g5|g6` accepts only verified, unexpired typed evidence envelopes and never accepts a bare payload, unsigned JSON, digest-only/generic artifact substitution, directory discovery, purpose/target mismatch, duplicate TestID, cross-candidate ref, or a re-signed old result.

The final release partition is generated mechanically from the same 185-row resolved DeliveryRegistry and is not a scheduler choice. Final L2 owns the canonical sorted TestID vector whose `first_due_profile` is `G0_BOOTSTRAP..G5_INTEGRATION`: exactly `149` IDs and `sha256(JCS(vector))=5ec5a8663b3763bcbf85d84438d6236e9a9680fc0749ad0ca3efa04f124a5a7a`. L3 owns the canonical sorted vector whose `first_due_profile=G6_RELEASE`: exactly `36` IDs and digest `e7a2fae4fa1a3384c47592ffd0310b3b8717cb595bc5c4397f61e0be2cbc85df`. G0 freezes both vectors/digests as generated goldens alongside the first-due map. They are disjoint, their union is the exact 185 Requirement TestID set, and neither level may move, duplicate or omit a row. The six auxiliary carrier TestIDs never enter either vector; final L2 and L3 bind their six results only through the exact `carrier_refs` relation below. Thus `149/36`, not `185/0`, `0/185` or an arbitrary disjoint split, is the sole release partition.

The L2 purpose/target/candidate mapping is one exact closed relation:

| L2 purpose variant | Exact target | Required verified candidate |
|---|---|---|
| `DevelopmentSlice` | `DevSliceGreen` | `SignedIntegrationCandidateV1` with purpose `DevelopmentSlice` and exact artifacts `{windows-authority,windows-client}` |
| `Integration` | `IntegrationGreen` | `SignedIntegrationCandidateV1` with purpose `Integration` and exact artifacts `{android-client,ios-client,macos-client,windows-authority,windows-client}` |
| `FinalRelease` | `ReleaseCertified` | signed `ReleaseCandidateV1` with the exact final release artifact/carrier closure |

The auxiliary-ref relation is also closed:

| Evidence purpose | Exact `client_conformance_refs` | Exact `carrier_refs` |
|---|---|---|
| L2 `DevelopmentSlice` | `{G3_SHELL,G4_CTC_UI_API}` typed `ClientConformanceResultV1` refs | `[]` |
| L2 `Integration` | `{G3_SHELL,G4_CTC_UI_API,G5_FOUR_PLATFORM}` typed refs | `[]` |
| L2 `FinalRelease` | the same exact three selected-stack typed refs | exactly the six typed `ReleaseCarrierResultV1` refs, one per recipe/TestID |
| L3 `ReleaseCertification` | `[]`; it binds the final L2 instead | byte-for-byte the same canonical six refs as final L2 |

`objective_closures` is the one typed business-closure snapshot, sorted uniquely by `objective_kind`; it is never a caller-supplied status vector. G0…G3 receipts require `[]`. Development L2 and the G4 receipt whose verified candidate is `SignedIntegrationCandidateV1::DevelopmentSlice` require exactly four rows: `CONTRACT_FULFILMENT`, `SALES_ORDER_FULFILMENT`, and `RECEIVABLE_COLLECTION` are `CLOSED`, while `PROCUREMENT_FULFILMENT` is exactly `WAITING` with `open_obligation_ids=[PURCHASE_AP_CLOSED]`, no procurement fact/review rows, and the graph-required typed `ProcurementSettlementGapV1` evidence showing PurchaseInvoice/AP/SupplierPayment all absent. This WAITING row is the standalone DevelopmentSlice success contract and cannot be omitted or mislabeled CLOSED.

Integration L2, Final L2, L3, the G5 receipt, and every G4/G5 receipt freshly emitted under a verified `SignedIntegrationCandidateV1::Integration` or `ReleaseCandidateV1` require the same four objectives `CLOSED` with `open_obligation_ids=[]`. Such a later-context G4 receipt preserves the exact G4 due/probe set but copies the byte-identical current Integration/Final-L2 closure snapshot; it never fabricates an impossible current WAITING objective revision after procurement has closed. Every row's `state_result`, `(evidence_id,result)` closure set and strict-positive `objective_generation` are derived from a current public query through `CommandPipeline`/`AuthorizedPgTx`, exact-match the active graph's objective obligations/evidence set, typed-load signed `RequirementEvidenceBindingV1` values from the same candidate run, and are members of the aggregate's authorized result closure: receipt prerequisite/current results, L2 `test_results`, or final-L2-plus-L3 `test_results` respectively. Reopen or any governed mutation advances only that objective's `ObjectiveGenerationV1`; an unrelated deployment activation does not alter it. A raw database query, arbitrary ArtifactRef, duplicated evidence ID, result outside that closure, stale objective revision, deployment `GenerationNumberV1`, or caller scalar cannot construct this type.

Closed procurement additionally has exactly three canonical `procurement_facts`, sorted by fact kind: `PURCHASE_INVOICE` owned by feature `purchase-invoicing`, `ACCOUNTS_PAYABLE_RECOGNITION` owned by `payable-cash`, and `SUPPLIER_PAYMENT_ALLOCATION` owned by `payable-cash`. The three distinct signed result refs exact-prove their tagged fact and owner; no feature may self-assert another owner's fact. Its `closure_review` is exactly `DISTINCT_REVIEWER`: `requested_by` and `reviewed_by` are server-derived typed `PrincipalRefV1` values, compare unequal on the complete `(kind,id)` tuple, and are exact-projected from the request and accepted-review facts for this same objective generation. `review_result` typed-loads the accepted review, repeats both principals and that generation, proves the reviewer was separately authorized, and is recorded only after all three procurement facts. Caller hashes, truncated/pseudonymous equality tokens and result-only reviewer claims cannot construct the binding. Any graph row with `distinct_reviewer_required=true` follows the same binding; all other rows require `NOT_REQUIRED`. Goldens independently mutate either kind, ID, generation, fact prefix and result binding. `WAITING`, `REOPENED`, a reversed fact, same requester/reviewer, changed generation, missing/extra fact or expired closure input blocks G5/final release.

Final L3 typed-reloads Final L2 and requires its four-row vector byte-for-byte while independently revalidating the current objective generations under the final checkpoint; a mutation or reopen between levels fails rather than updating the frozen L2. The release-certificate constructor repeats that verification through L3 immediately before its own finalization and includes every time-bearing closure input in the frozen expiry minimum. Goldens cover the DevelopmentSlice-only G4 WAITING exception, Integration/final G4 all-CLOSED branches, wrong candidate-purpose/snapshot combinations, all-closed G5/final rows, missing/reopened/stale objectives, the three fact owner permutations, absent/reversed facts, same reviewer, spoofed state/result refs and L2/L3 generation drift.

Every conformance ref exact-matches its selector, selected recipe, auxiliary TestID, candidate run, terminal journal record and expiry. Every release carrier ref exact-matches the six-row recipe registry, binding variant and terminal journal record; missing/extra/duplicate recipe/TestID or a different L2/L3 six-ref vector fails closed. The other six L2 purpose × target combinations are invalid. L3 has only `ReleaseCertification` × `ReleaseCertified`, must reference an L2 envelope whose purpose is `FinalRelease`, and must consume the same signed `ReleaseCandidateV1`. The L2 and L3 JSON-Schema/golden suites include every valid row plus negative vectors for all six invalid L2 pairs, a non-final L2 reference at L3, wrong candidate type/purpose, conformance selector used as a TestID, wrong conformance/carrier cardinality, and unequal final L2/L3 carrier sets.

`GateReceiptPurposeV1` serializes exactly as `EP-F57-GATE-RECEIPT-V1`; `ProgramGateV1` serializes exactly as `G0_BOOTSTRAP_GREEN|G1_AUTHORITY_SPINE_GREEN|G2_CTC_DATA_GREEN|G3_CLIENT_SHELL_GREEN|DEV_SLICE_GREEN|INTEGRATION_GREEN`, while `RELEASE_CERTIFIED` is deliberately absent and remains the separate typed `ReleaseCertificateV1`. `GateEvidenceClassV1` serializes exactly as `BOOTSTRAP_CONTRACT|AUTHORITY_SPINE|CTC_DATA_PROBE|CLIENT_SHELL_PROBE|SYNTHETIC_DEV|INTEGRATION`. `GateCandidateBindingV1` is internally tagged and `deny_unknown_fields`: its exact JCS object fields are `binding_kind,candidate_identity_sha256` for `PRE_INTEGRATION`, and `binding_kind,candidate_identity_sha256,candidate_manifest_ref` for `SIGNED_CANDIDATE`. The exact closed gate/class/binding relation is:

| Program gate | Evidence class | Binding variant |
|---|---|---|
| `G0_BOOTSTRAP_GREEN` | `BOOTSTRAP_CONTRACT` | `PRE_INTEGRATION` |
| `G1_AUTHORITY_SPINE_GREEN` | `AUTHORITY_SPINE` | `PRE_INTEGRATION` |
| `G2_CTC_DATA_GREEN` | `CTC_DATA_PROBE` | `PRE_INTEGRATION` |
| `G3_CLIENT_SHELL_GREEN` | `CLIENT_SHELL_PROBE` | `PRE_INTEGRATION` |
| `DEV_SLICE_GREEN` | `SYNTHETIC_DEV` | `SIGNED_CANDIDATE` |
| `INTEGRATION_GREEN` | `INTEGRATION` | `SIGNED_CANDIDATE` |

`prerequisite_receipts` is the complete earlier-gate set, never merely the direct predecessor: G0 has `{}`; G1 has `{G0}`; G2 has `{G0,G1}`; G3 has `{G0,G1,G2}`; G4 has `{G0,G1,G2,G3}`; and G5 has `{G0,G1,G2,G3,G4}`. Each entry is the plain typed `GateReceiptRefV1 { gate, artifact }`, each gate appears exactly once, and refs sort by `(gate ordinal,artifact.uri,artifact.sha256)`. A consumer typed-loads `artifact` as `GateReceiptV1` and exact-matches the repeated gate, candidate run, signer and terminal bound event; no prerequisite ref is itself signed or requires a second signer-registry row. The release certificate separately requires exactly `{G0,G1,G2,G3,G4,G5}` under the same rule. A missing, extra, duplicate, wrong-gate, wrapper/double-signature or direct-predecessor-only vector fails before expiry or result aggregation.

Every receipt in one aggregate exact-matches the same `CandidateRunIdentityV1`. Each receipt uses the binding dictated by its own gate: G0…G3 prerequisites remain `PRE_INTEGRATION`; G4/G5 receipts are `SIGNED_CANDIDATE`, and all G4/G5 receipts in that aggregate exact-match the current manifest ref. The typed verifier requires that ref to load a `SignedIntegrationCandidateV1` for standalone G4/G5 runs and a `ReleaseCandidateV1` when G4/G5 receipts are freshly emitted inside a final G6 run; the enclosing target/purpose selects exactly one type, and neither type can substitute in the other context. A final run never points those receipts to an older G5 integration manifest. Receipts are never required to share a binding variant across gate levels. Every program-gate payload is complete before it enters `sign_business_artifact_v1`: prerequisite/result refs are canonical-sorted and duplicate-free, the Fresh-PG reference and every referenced receipt/result exact-match the run identity, each `run_journal_checkpoint_ref` is the latest checkpoint after the receipt's complete due set and verifies the exact result prefix, and G0 alone has an empty prerequisite vector. Its issue time is trusted `now`, and its expiry is the minimum of the gate policy cap and all consumed time-bearing prerequisite/result/Fresh-PG/checkpoint expiries plus the journal expiry; immutable candidate/static refs are excluded. An input that is time-bearing but lacks a typed verifiable expiry is rejected. A raw string gate/purpose, any unlisted gate/class/binding combination, partial binding/payload, digest-only or generic unsigned receipt, stale/expired ref, expiry extension, wrong candidate-envelope type, or cross-candidate/run join fails closed. The gate-receipt schema/golden suite covers the six valid rows in both allowed candidate contexts and the negative cross-product, a missing candidate manifest ref, an unbound/torn journal, two different manifest refs under the same run, old-G5-ref-in-final-run, wrong envelope type, and an aggregate expiry later than any time-bearing input.

The initial stack decision has its own durable, non-candidate attempt authority; it is never a loose group of four files and cannot be duplicated under two bundle roots. Before any bundle output, the Windows evidence authority calls only `verify_authority_data_root_v1(storage_manifest_path,trust_input_paths)`: that G1-01-owned constructor typed-verifies `SignedF57AuthorityStorageManifestV1` through the complete customer deployment bootstrap, requires `DATA_HDD`, performs the live final-handle non-reparse probe, exact-matches volume identity and anti-rollback state, and returns the private non-serialized `ValidatedDataRootV1`. No raw-path overload or caller-built value exists. This is evaluator state `VERIFIED_DATA_HDD_ROOT`, not `CERTIFIED_DATA_HDD`: no G5 or pre-freeze step consumes the later P340 result. It then creates or adopts the global slot only at `<validated-data-root>\evidence-authority\architecture-decision-slots\<candidate_identity_sha256>\slot.v1.json`; neither a drive letter nor `C:\ProgramData` is part of the wire. Its `slot_id_sha256` is exactly `sha256(JCS({"contract":"EP-F57-CLIENT-ARCHITECTURE-DECISION-V1","candidate_identity_sha256":<64-lowerhex>,"stack_under_test":"TAURI2"}))`, its relocatable `authority_slot_uri` is exactly `evidence-authority://architecture-decision-slots/<candidate_identity_sha256>/slot.v1.json`, its aggregator is `f57-architecture-decision-authority`, its envelope signer is the registry row's exact SPKI token, and the additional leaf-DN constraint is `CN=EP F57 Architecture Decision Authority,O=Enterprise Platform`. It is create-new and fixes the one unpredictable `attempt_id`; the same slot may only resume that attempt. If this archive later supplies the final G6 stack selection, its archived storage-manifest and bootstrap target bytes/digests/media, volume identity and canonical data-root digest must exact-match the corresponding G6 binding values; their relocatable URIs may differ between archive and run stores but never their content identity. The post-freeze P340 evidence must then certify that same physical tuple before release.

Before writing the attempt header, the authority bootstrap-verifies the exact signed 89-row registry as current, validates its exact two-role archive trust-anchor policy, independently verifies the storage-manifest trust bootstrap under the G6 rule above, and create-new copies/fsyncs/reloads all eight immutable inputs: registry, signed storage manifest, and the six `AuthorityStorageTrustBootstrapV1` targets. Registry and storage-manifest paths remain `inputs/<artifact-signer-registry-envelope-sha256>.json` and `inputs/<authority-storage-manifest-envelope-sha256>.json`; the six trust paths are exactly `inputs/storage-bootstrap/deployment-manifest.v1.json`, `deployment-manifest.p7s`, `deployment-trust-bundle.p7b`, `storage-trust-root.der`, `storage-revocation.bin`, and `storage-checkpoint.bin`. `ArchitectureDecisionAttemptPayloadV1` carries the two envelope refs plus the nested six archive-relative refs, exact `data_volume_identity`, and `authority_data_root_path_sha256=sha256(UTF-8 final-handle canonical data_root without a trailing separator)`. Registry digest must equal `candidate_identity.artifact_signer_registry_sha256`; deployment/storage/root/revocation/checkpoint identities and digests must exact-match their two signed manifests and bootstrap rules; and `archive_trust_anchor_policy_sha256` must equal `sha256(JCS(the policy embedded in those exact registry bytes))`. All initial runner, trust-chain and storage-path checks use these archived bytes, and permanent replay uses them rather than ambient files, Windows roots, network completion or current replacements. An existing different slot/attempt/registry/storage manifest/bootstrap/data volume/root digest/policy, alternate physical authority root or second attempt fails. A later attempt requires a different committed candidate identity or a separately approved signed supersession plus plan amendment.

`ArchitectureDecisionStoreV1` uses exactly `<validated-data-root>\evidence-authority\architecture-decision-slots\<candidate_identity_sha256>\archive-root\` as the global create-new canonical persistence root and the explicit initial bundle as an exact materialized view. The `<candidate_identity_sha256>` segment is exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters and byte-equals the slot identity; final-handle canonicalization must yield this literal descendant on the signed manifest's DATA_HDD volume. Caller-selected root, hardcoded `C:`/`D:`, UNC/device path, alternate data stream, empty/dot/parent segment, encoded separator, trailing-dot/space alias, 8.3 alias, junction, mount point, symlink or any reparse traversal fails before a write. It copies the slot bytes without resigning to `g5/client-stack-decision-slot.v1.json` and owns exactly `g5/client-stack-decision-attempt.jcs.jsonl`, `g5/client-stack-decision-platform-results/<windows|macos|ios|android>.v1.json`, `g5/client-stack-decision-attempt-checkpoints/<20-digit-sequence>.v1.json`, `g5/client-stack-decision.v1.json`, the two digest-named registry/storage-manifest inputs, the exact six `inputs/storage-bootstrap/*` files above, `objects/sha256/<64-lowerhex-digest>`, `trust/timestamps/rfc3161-response.tsr`, `trust/chains/decision-signer.p7b`, `trust/chains/tsa.p7b`, `trust/revocation/<decision-signer|tsa>/<five-digit-covered-chain-index>/crl.der`, sibling `ocsp.der`, `trust/trust-closure.v1.json`, and root `archive-manifest.v1.json`. The five-digit index is zero-padded decimal and equals the tagged non-root `covered_chain_index`.

`ArchitectureDecisionStoreV1` alone registers `architecture-archive-relative://root/<canonical-relative-path>`; every archive-internal `ArtifactRefV1` for slot/journal/checkpoint/platform/input/subordinate/decision/trust bytes uses that relocatable scheme, and each proof ref URI is exactly the scheme joined to its kind/role/index-derived fixed path. The attempt's registry, storage-manifest and six bootstrap refs use their exact archive-relative input paths and canonical target media; their digests byte-equal the archived bytes and attempt-bound values. Global, initial, committed and current-run materializations resolve the scheme only against the verified archive manifest's own root; physical DATA_HDD residency is re-proved only for the global authority copy. Recovery resolves each of the eight input refs from the authenticated archive manifest, adopts only exact bytes and never consults an ambient trust directory, current deployment manifest, network or Windows trust store. Canonical bytes are first durably stored below that exact global archive root and copied byte-for-byte to the same relative path below the initial materialization root; conflicting bytes in either root fail. The signed first frame is the one create-new `ArchitectureDecisionAttemptV1`; `ArchitectureDecisionAttemptHeaderRefV1` hashes the exact authenticated prefix through that complete header frame rather than pretending the growing journal is a whole-file `ArtifactRefV1`. Subsequent signed `len8<TAB>JCS<LF>` records use the same sequence/hash-chain, OS-exclusive lease, durable-start-before-side-effect, typed reconciler, torn-tail quarantine, and create-new/adopt rules as the gate journal, but their identity is the slot/architecture attempt. Checkpoints are create-new at the zero-padded sequence path and their `ArchitectureDecisionAttemptPrefixRefV1` authenticates the exact prefix. Before an attempt header exists, the only legal creation grammar is `cargo xtask f57 client-gate --stack tauri2 --candidate <git-rev> --storage-manifest <absolute-path> --deployment-manifest <absolute-path> --deployment-manifest-signature <absolute-path> --deployment-trust-bundle <absolute-path> --storage-trust-root <absolute-path> --storage-revocation <absolute-path> --storage-checkpoint <absolute-path> --bundle-root <path> --out <derived-decision-path>`; all seven storage/bootstrap flags are mandatory once each and no alias is accepted. A pre-header crash repeats that grammar and adopts only byte-identical fixed copies. After the attempt header exists, recovery invokes the same command without all seven bootstrap flags, which are then forbidden, and resolves only the archived refs; any `--out` must exact-equal the derived decision path. Slot copy, journal, checkpoints, platform and trust filenames are never configurable. Parser/path/crash goldens cover each missing/duplicate/extra/wrong-file flag, a non-`D:` legal DATA_HDD path, every exact input/proof mapping and URI, and every SSD/root/escape/alias/role/index/bootstrap-substitution case above.

For each platform, the only legal states are `ABSENT -> PLATFORM_STARTED -> PLATFORM_COMPLETED` or `ABSENT -> PLATFORM_STARTED -> PLATFORM_UNKNOWN -> PLATFORM_RECONCILED`. `PLATFORM_STARTED.execution_attempt_id` is unpredictable and exact-matches the aggregate and all eight embedded lifecycle bindings. Output-before-terminal recovery resolves only the fixed platform path and adopts exact bytes; it never reruns or re-signs. A remaining UNKNOWN makes the architecture attempt inconclusive and forbids a decision.
